info.title: CawCo hub
info.description: The hub's HTTP API as the dashboard uses it, and the dashboard socket's frames (components only). Generated by `bun run openapi` in packages/hub; do not edit.

writes.description: What the page open in the person's tab shows that the hub isn't known to hold: one base64 Yjs update, applied before the picks are read.

runs.description: How many of each routine's newest runs; 5 when left out.

days.description: How many days back from now; 30 when left out.

kind.description: Only tasks in stages of this kind.

conversation.description: A new project's conversation, which sets it up; none when the folder joined one, or it could not start.

joined.description: True when the session's folder joined a project that already had its repository.

sessions.description: The sessions moved into it: this one, then its delegates.

tasks.description: Plan items filed as proposed tasks, and the ones the project refused.

atPlanLimit.description: What its sessions do at a plan limit while its extra usage is on ({@link AtPlanLimit}).

email.description: The email it is signed in as ({@link identity}'s); null until its first sign-in.

identity.description: Null until its first sign-in on any machine.

label.description: A nickname someone gave it; null: it goes by its email ({@link accountName}).

neverBackup.description: Never chosen as the fallback when the pinned account cannot take a session.

order.description: Its place in fill-first order: lowest first.

provider.description:
Who bills the account: a provider id. `anthropic` is a Claude subscription
or Console organization, for Claude Code alone: Anthropic's terms keep its
OAuth tokens out of every other product. Any other is a provider pi or
OpenCode speaks, by pi-ai's id for it (`openai-codex` for a ChatGPT
subscription, `github-copilot`, `opencode-go`, `zai`…), or OpenCode's own
id for one pi-ai has no provider for (`zai-coding-plan`, a configured
`litellm`) — see {@link ProviderInfo}.

reservePct.description:
New sessions stop being placed on it once its weekly window passes this
percentage; null: no reserve.

setupStep.description:
The step its setup (Configure → Accounts → Add) stands at, while that
setup is unfinished; absent once it is done. A reload, or a press on the
account's row, opens the setup there again.

AccountBench.description: An account taken out of placement until its window resets.

scope.description: The model scope it is exhausted for; null: every model.

AccountBorrowFrame.description: A borrower near its borrowed access token's expiry, asking the hub for a fresh one from its lender.

lender.description: The machine that lent it, as the borrower's store names it.

AccountCatalog.description:
An account's model catalog as its Claude Code last reported it, and the
effort each model ran at when a session asked for none (learned from the
sessions themselves; absent until one has).

AccountCatalogFault.description:
Why an account's models could not be read, as the hub's last probe of it
went, its machine named; gone once a probe answers. A picker with no
catalog for the account says it.

bindingWindow.description:
The window that limits the account: the one that runs out soonest at its
pace, else (none runs out before its reset) the one that resets latest.
Null when the account has no windows.

lastSeenAt.description: When its Claude Code last reported; null: never.

AccountHue.description: The colour an account is drawn in: the `--account-<name>` token.

AccountIdentity.description:
Who an account is: an email in an organization, the organization known by
its id (`orgId`), never its name, which is a display name: an org renamed
is the same org, and two orgs can share a name. Claude: as `claude auth
status --json` reports it (`email`, `orgName`, `orgId`). ChatGPT: the
access token's claims, read on the machine — the email
(`https://api.openai.com/profile`.email) and, as `organization` and its
id, the ChatGPT account id (`https://api.openai.com/auth`.chatgpt_account_id),
the workspace the subscription bills. Another OAuth provider: the email its
credential names, if any, and its provider id. A key: its last four
characters (`…a1b2`) and, as `organization` and its id, a fingerprint of
it (`key:` and the first 16 hex of its SHA-256), so the same key on two
machines is one account and the key itself never leaves them.

orgId.description:
The organization's id: what tells two identities apart. Null where
nothing read one (Claude Code's initialize response names none, an agent
older than this field sends none): such an identity is the same as no
other ({@link sameIdentity}).

organization.description: The organization's name, for a screen.

AccountJoined.description:
A sign-in that came out as an account that already exists: the sign-in is
that account's now, and the account made for it is gone. `note` says so
for a screen.

AccountKind.description:
How the account signs in. Claude: a subscription (`claude auth login`) or a
Console organization (`claude auth login --console`). Any other provider:
its own OAuth sign-in through pi-ai (`oauth`), or a key (`api_key`).

AccountLimits.description: One Claude account's own limits, named by its account.

AccountOverage.description: Extra-usage state, as the session's rate-limit events report it.

AccountProbe.description:
What a probe (a session that never takes a turn and names no model) reads
of a config dir at initialize: its {@link SessionAccountRead}, and the models
the account offers, which the hub keeps as its catalog.

identity.description:
Who an account is: an email in an organization, the organization known by
its id (`orgId`), never its name, which is a display name: an org renamed
is the same org, and two orgs can share a name. Claude: as `claude auth
status --json` reports it (`email`, `orgName`, `orgId`). ChatGPT: the
access token's claims, read on the machine — the email
(`https://api.openai.com/profile`.email) and, as `organization` and its
id, the ChatGPT account id (`https://api.openai.com/auth`.chatgpt_account_id),
the workspace the subscription bills. Another OAuth provider: the email its
credential names, if any, and its provider id. A key: its last four
characters (`…a1b2`) and, as `organization` and its id, a fingerprint of
it (`key:` and the first 16 hex of its SHA-256), so the same key on two
machines is one account and the key itself never leaves them.

AccountReading.description:
An account's freshest limit reading, assembled from what its sessions'
Claude Code reported: the windows from `rate_limit_event`s, the plan from
`accountInfo()`.

lastSeenAt.description: When the last event or account read for it arrived.

windowKinds.description:
The account's window set: the windows (core usage/windows.ts
`windowKey`) the provider's last report that named its windows carried
(a Claude `rate_limit_event`'s `unifiedWindows`, a usage endpoint's
answer). A held window outside it is gone. Null until a report names
them: the windows held are all that is known, and a Claude account keeps
the session window it holds until one does.

AccountReport.description:
What one account's store on a machine says: whether it is signed in, how,
and as whom. Claude: `claude auth status` in the account's config dir.
Any other provider: the credential in the account's `credential.json`, its
identity read there (a ChatGPT token's claims, a key's fingerprint). Read
on every connect and again every minute, so a store signed in as someone
else since is seen within a minute. A Claude account's models are the
hub's to ask ({@link CONTROL_PROBE_ACCOUNT}), once per account.

account.description: The account whose store this is, under `~/.cawco/accounts/<id>/`.

identity.description: Who the store is signed in as. Absent when it names nobody.

kind.description: `console` for a Claude Console login; `oauth` or `api_key` for any other provider's credential.

provider.description: The provider of the credential held; absent for a Claude dir.

AccountSignin.description:
One account signed in (or not) on one machine: its one credential there,
which every harness on the machine that speaks its provider uses.

movedAt.description:
When a credential from one of the machine's own stores was moved into
this account there ({@link CONTROL_MOVE_HOME_LOGIN},
{@link CONTROL_MOVE_HOME_CREDENTIAL}), epoch ms; null for a sign-in made
in Configure → Accounts.

movedFrom.description: The store it was moved from: `~/.claude`, pi's own `auth.json`, OpenCode's own; null when not moved.

reason.description:
Why the hub signed it out there itself: the words a session on it met
when Claude Code refused it for good: this machine's credential (revoked,
or a refresh that can't succeed), or the account's own subscription
access, which signs it out on every machine (hub accounts.ts
`claudeCredentialRefused`). It stays signed out, whatever the store says,
until it is signed in again through CawCo, or, for an account-wide
refusal, until a check's turn as the account is answered. Null for any
other state.

refusalReach.description: How far the refusal that signed it out reaches; null with no {@link reason}.

AccountSigninResult.description:
How a Claude sign-in ended, and what the dir's Claude Code said once it
had. `mismatch`: the dir signed in as someone other than the account
already is, so the machine logged that dir out again.

joined.description: Signed in as an account that already exists: it is that account's now.

probe.description:
What a probe (a session that never takes a turn and names no model) reads
of a config dir at initialize: its {@link SessionAccountRead}, and the models
the account offers, which the hub keeps as its catalog.

ActionsFrame.description:
Hub-originated: every approved action waiting on you, whole, on each
change: those proposed, and those that failed or whose outcome is unknown,
until you put them away.

AgentRow.description:
A machine from the hub's `agents` table — what `GET /api/agents` answers with,
and what rides alongside the sessions in an `instances` frame.

auth.description: `unknown` until a daemon that probes has registered at least once.

build.description: The cawco build this machine's daemon is running (NEW.md §12).

chosenModes.description:
The permission mode the person last started each harness's session in
on this machine, from any device (the hub's `chosen_modes`): the mode the
New session form opens on there. Absent for a harness never started.

custody.description: Last register's sessiond read, distinct from an available empty list.

fleetItems.description:
Each fleet item as the machine's harnesses converge it (core fleet.ts
`FleetConvergeFrame`), by item id. Absent until the machine has said.

fleetSync.description:
What became of the last fleet sync the hub sent it: sent, applied,
failed in the machine's words, or unanswered. Absent until the hub has
sent it one.

harnesses.description: What each installed harness can do, as the daemon reported at register.

home.description: The machine's home folder, absolute, as its daemon reported at register; absent until one that says so has.

hostsHub.description: The hub runs on this machine, as the hub reads it: live, never stored.

lastSeenAt.description: A `Date` inside the hub, the ISO string it serialises to everywhere else.

lostAt.description:
Since when (epoch ms) the hub has heard nothing from this machine, once
that has lasted `MACHINE_LOST_MS` with sessions on it (hub
machine-contact.ts): Needs you's item. Null while it answers. Live, as
`status` is: never stored.

pauseStopped.description:
What the pause stopped as it began, as said ({@link stoppedWords}):
"stopped 1 running check". Null when it stopped nothing, or is not paused.

pausedUntil.description:
The owner paused the machine until this time (epoch ms): CawCo starts
nothing on it until then, though its agent stays connected. Null when it
is not paused.

reconnectingUntil.description:
Until when (epoch ms, the hub's clock, as `lostAt`) the hub reads this
machine as on its way back after its agent's link went: a read off it
answers so then (`Retry-After`), and offline after. Null while it is
connected or once it is offline. Live, as `status` is: never stored.

tools.description: Last-known tool status by tool id (NEW.md §10).

ApprovedActionView.description: One approved action as the hub answers it (times in ms epoch).

account.description: The service's account the connection signed in as when it was proposed.

args.description: The call's arguments, JSON, exactly as it will be sent.

argsHash.description: SHA-256 of `args`, hex: what an approval names.

checkedAt.description: When you put a failed or unknown one away.

error.description: Why it failed, was refused, or is unknown.

projectName.description: The project's name, as the board names it.

proposedBy.description: The session that proposed it, and its title while the hub holds it.

result.description: What the service answered, JSON, cut at 16 KB.

routineId.description: The routine whose run proposed it (that run's session, or one it started); null outside any routine.

runAt.description: When it runs, at the earliest; null: as soon as it is approved.

runId.description: That routine's run; null outside any routine.

stageResult.description: What its stage move came to, once it tried.

thenStage.description: The task stage it moves to once done.

name.description: What its chip says; left out, the file's name, the link's host or the artifact's id.

primary.description: The one the reviewer sees first.

ArtifactChoices.description: An artifact's choices as the page reads them through the bridge (`cawco.on("picks")`).

pageHash.description: The page's hash when the hub last built it; null for a preview.

sentAt.description: When the person last sent their picks to the session.

ArtifactHit.description:
One of a session's artifacts a Files search matched
(`GET /api/instances/:id/artifacts/search`), best first: what matched,
and where the words on its page did, the words around the first hit with
each hit between 「 and 」 (the finder's excerpt).

ArtifactKind.description:
The kinds of artifact: HTML the agent wrote, a drawing, a dev
server or folder shown live, a sheet: a story file's stories, each a
real component mounted by the project's own toolchain (core `stage.ts`),
and the project's browser, listed for every session of the project (or of
the machine, for the machine's browser). A browser's source is its key as
a page (`{ page: "project:<id>" }`): the hub holds it, no machine's
preview listener serves it, and every installed app reads that shape.

next_cursor.description: What `cursor` takes for the page after this one; null on the last.

total.description: How many the whole list holds, every page.

ArtifactNeed.description: One artifact waiting on the person: a Needs-you item.

ask.description: What the person does there, in their words: the row's title, the push's body.

href.description: Opens its session with the artifact in its panel at {@link stop}.

instanceId.description: The session whose panel holds it.

link.description: `[title](cawco:artifact/<id>)`: how a line of words names it.

notNow.description:
The notice id its Not now acknowledges (hub notices.ts): the item leaves
the lane until it is raised again, a revision or a new answer.

ownSend.description:
A decision page (one that asks choices): it carries its own Send at its
foot, so its row stands none (the owner's pick, "Only the page's own
Send").

parked.description:
Put away with Not now at this raise or a later one: out of Needs you
(its count, its rows, the push, the phone's list), still waiting in
Files with its dot. Carried so every screen hears it move.

pending.description: Its reasons, strongest first; never empty.

project.description: The project it was made in; null outside one.

raisedAt.description: When it became pending, ms epoch on the hub's clock: its publish, or the agent's newest reply that asks.

title.description: What it is named by to the person (its agent's title): a row's name, a push's title.

unsent.description: What Send sends now; 0 when nothing is written and unsent.

ArtifactNeedNotice.description: One artifact's notice in Caw's panel: one row per artifact.

at.description: When the newest part happened, ms epoch on the hub's clock.

href.description: Opens it, as a need's does; null when no session holds it.

title.description: What it is named by to the person (its agent's title).

ArtifactNeedNoticePart.description: What one notice of an artifact says, with the notice id its ✕ acknowledges.

ArtifactNeedsFrame.description: Hub-originated: every artifact need and notice, whole, on each change.

ArtifactNeedsRead.description: `GET /api/artifact-needs`: the lane's artifacts as they stand.

ArtifactPending.description: An artifact's pending state as its own list reads it (Files, the panel's menu).

ArtifactPromotion.description: An artifact's promote: the project folder's commit that holds it, and when.

answeredAt.description: When his newest pick, note or value on it came; null before any.

changed.description: A canvas's elements the person changed since `since` (or since your last read).

changedUnderYou.description: A canvas's elements you replaced that the person had changed since your last read: "<id> changed under you".

decisions.description: A page's choices in page order, each answered or not ({@link DecisionAnswer}); on every read of a page that asks any.

deleted.description: Elements an update deleted, and the ids it named that the canvas does not hold.

draft.description: A canvas the person opened in the composer and has not sent yet.

edit.description: A sheet's write: the story file, from the clone's root, the 1-based lines it changed, and the formatter that shaped them.

faults.description: What a browser met drawing it at this revision (core page-faults.ts): dials its panel doesn't draw, uncaught errors, assets that failed.

held.description: Your change waits as this next version: your parent had opened the artifact, and their panel keeps the version they opened until they call artifact_show.

marked.description: What this update changed on the page, each by its link (`[label](cawco:change/<artifact>/<anchor>)`): what the agent names each to the person by.

name.description: Its slug, what every artifact tool takes.

outline.description: A canvas, as you read it: one line per element (core `canvasOutline`).

pageHash.description: A built page's hash, which each pick records; null for a preview (the hub never built it) and a canvas. Wire-pinned: installable app builds decode it.

pictureAt.description: When the canvas's latest picture was drawn; null when it has none.

pictureBehind.description: A canvas's picture is from before your last write to it: no screen drew it again within the wait.

png.description: Its picture, base64 PNG, when asked (`png: true`): a canvas's latest, the one after your last write once a screen draws it, null when it has none yet; a preview or a page drawn now as the panel draws it; a component's drawn by its stage.

program.description: A decision page's program as the hub keeps it, on a read without `since`: re-emit a statement from it to revise one.

removed.description: Keys that changed since `since` and are no longer there.

saved.description: Where its picture was kept, as the session names the path (`save`).

sentAt.description: When the page was last sent, by him or by the hub ({@link sentBy}); null before it was (and on a canvas, which has no Send).

sentBy.description: Who sent it at {@link sentAt}: the person pressing Send, or the hub once every question had his answer (needs.ts `answeredWhole`).

sentText.description: What the page's `cawco.send(text)` sent with the person's last send.

seq.description: The cursor for the next read's `since`.

sheet.description: A sheet as its stage reads it: its stories with their args, its meta, and each component's props.

stage.description: A sheet's stage: its status, and the compile errors standing in the modules the sheet imports. A served preview's: its server's status, and why it is in `error`.

state.description: Every key, or with `since` only those changed after it; a canvas's is empty.

title.description: What it is named by to the person.

unreached.description:
The hub's word that a canvas's stage couldn't be reached by its last read
(the doc's `meta.unreached`, which the panel and the agent's read both
say): the hop that failed, in the preview proxy's kinds; why, in the hub's
words; and since when, the first read that failed since one that reached
it. A read that reaches the stage, or the daemon's next word of it, takes
it away.

verify.description: A component canvas's design system round, as `verify: true` asked it: what the ask did.

weight.description: What a sheet loads, from its stage's module graph; null until a view has loaded it.

workspace.description: A port preview's workspace, whose dev server it is.

wrote.description: The element ids an update wrote.

ArtifactReason.description: Why an artifact waits on the person, one reason each.

ask.description: Its line in the panel's head.

does.description: What the person does on it.

madeBy.description: The delegate that put it in this session's panel, when another session made it.

madeByLink.description: That delegate's link, `[title](cawco:session/<id>)`, what the agent names it by.

name.description: Its slug, what every artifact tool takes.

opened.description: Whether the person has had its latest revision on screen.

picks.description: A decision page's choices: how many it asks, how many are picked, how many picks are not sent yet.

picksAwaiting.description: Picks the person sent that the session has not read.

sent.description: It was sent since your last change (a revision, or a new ask), by him or by the hub ({@link sentBy}).

sentBy.description: Who sent it last, when it was sent.

session.description: The session that made it, when it is not the caller's own (a conversation reading its project's).

sessionLink.description: That session's link, what the agent names it by.

shown.description: Whether its session's panel shows it now.

title.description: What it is named by to the person.

unread.description: The person's changes (picks, notes, drawn elements) since the session last read it.

waitingOn.description: Whose move it is: the person's (what Needs you lists it for: never opened, picks not made, marks not sent, an answer not looked at, its ask not retired), the session's (sent picks, a canvas's changes unread, or handed to it or changed by a delegate and not opened yet).

ArtifactStop.description: Where the panel opens an artifact: its first pending stop.

ArtifactSummary.description: One artifact as the panel's list shows it, newest first.

ask.description: The one line the panel's head shows under its title: what the person does here, in their words. Empty on one made before asks were kept.

does.description: What the person does on it.

name.description: Its slug, what the agent's tools and its URLs name it by; never shown to the person.

pending.description:
What it waits on the person for, as Needs you derives it (core
artifact-needs.ts), strongest first; null when nothing is asked of the
person.

promoted.description: Its last promote into the project's folder (`artifact_promote`, the doc's `meta.promoted`); null until one.

sent.description: The person pressed Send on it since the session last revised it or changed its ask.

shownAt.description: When it was last brought to the front of the panel.

thumbnail.description: Its latest picture, served at `GET /api/artifacts/:id/thumbnail/:scheme`; null until a screen drew one.

title.description: What every surface names it by to the person, in the agent's plain words ({@link ARTIFACT_TITLE_LIMIT}). Empty on one made before titles were kept.

waiting.description: What it waits on the person for ({@link pending}) stands: its card and its row wear the needs-you dot.

ArtifactThumbnail.description:
An artifact's latest picture: a page's or preview's thumbnail as the
dashboard's pane took it (both schemes, or one when the page draws the
same in both), a canvas's own picture. `at` changes with every new one.

height.description: Its pixels, as its PNG says: the card is laid out at its shape before it loads.

single.description: The page draws the same in both schemes: `light` is its one picture.

AskAnswer.description:
An answered ask's answer as the hub took it, and where it came from, so a
screen that held the ask and did not answer it says what won and where
(JOURNEY.md Flow 2: "the answer row resolves to the answer that won,
naming where it came from").

behavior.description: Approve or deny; absent when the harness settled the ask itself and did not say.

name.description:
The paired device that answered (a page or the app), or the session that
did (a delegate's parent, its project's conversation), by name; absent when the
hub knows no name (a page or app it trusts by its network).

via.description:
Where it was answered: a dashboard page; the app (a client that is no
page: the iOS and Mac app); another session; the harness itself, in
its own interface; or Full Send, the mode the person put its session
in, which approves an approval the session had open as it entered it
(hub asks.ts `fullSendFiled`).

died.description:
Its process died on a signal while the daemon ran it, and nothing of the
daemon's stopped it (an OOM kill, a sessiond restart, a stray `kill`):
the signal, and the harness's own words. The hub starts it again with
the turn it cut, unless it died so right after the last such start.

kind.description: The daemon stopped an at-rest session's processes, or one ended of its own accord; its next message wakes it.

AtLimit.description:
What a running session does when its account hits its limit: wait for the
reset, or move to another account that can take it (the hub's
`decideStop`). `waitMinutes`: a reset this close is waited for.
`moveWholeUnderK`: a context under this many thousand tokens moves whole
and goes on; one of this many or more, moved to another organization
(whose cache it can't read), is compacted as `compaction` says for the
moment it moves at. A live work item's session is answered so whoever
started its refused turn, the hub's own word to it included; every other
word of the hub's a limit refused is left until a person or the session's
parent writes.

staleAfterHours.description:
How long past its reset a held session is still carried on by itself
(a sign-in hold, which has no reset, counts from when it was held).
Older, its hold goes stale: nothing sends to it or wakes it until a
person or its parent writes to it, and it waits in Needs you and in its
parent's `delegate_list` (hub at-limit.ts `goneStale`).

AtPlanLimit.description:
What a session on an account does once the account reaches a plan limit
while its extra usage is on (Claude Code's `overageStatus` allowed): moves
to an account with plan room (`move`, the default), or keeps going on this
account's extra usage (`extra-usage`). With extra usage off or refused, the
account is at its limit as any other is, whichever it says. It governs a
session that has reached the limit: a new session goes to plan room first,
and to a keep-going account's extra usage only when no account it may run
on has plan room, or when Pinned pins that account.

AttemptResult.description:
An attempt's result (`task_result`, hub task-tools.ts): what the session
that worked it says it did, what the reviewer should check, and what it
handed in, in the order it is drawn. One per attempt; a later call
replaces it. (A task's `TaskResult`, hub tasks.ts, is its newest
finished attempt's `finish_item` report.)

at.description: When it was handed in, ms epoch.

AttemptStart.description:
An attempt as it started; or, `queued`, waiting for files a live item owns
(its ids null until it starts). Wire-pinned: installable app builds decode
these fields from `POST /api/projects/:id/tasks/:taskId/attempts`.

queued.description: Whether it waits for files a live item owns, to start when they are free.

stage.description: The stage the task is in now.

type.description: The delegate type it runs; null, the hub's default.

AuthState.description:
Whether a machine's daemon can actually start sessions for a harness. For
Claude: whether any CawCo account is signed in on the machine.
`unreadable-credentials` is macOS's own failure: Claude Code keeps an
account's credentials in the login keychain, and a daemon outside the GUI
session is refused the secret (`errSecInteractionNotAllowed`). Generalized:
every harness reports its own auth word through the same three states.

BinaryDownload.description: How far a download of a build is, in bytes of its signed size.

BinaryUpdateChannels.description: What the hub knows of each channel; `null` where the release host has no release.

checkedAt.description: When the release host was asked, in milliseconds.

BinaryUpdateLanding.description:
The last install or rollback that finished. It is the event a notice
announces, so nothing but the finish of an install or rollback sets it, and
the next one replaces it: the state's other writes carry it through
unchanged, and the session keeper moving to the build later is part of the
same update, not a new one. Whether a person has seen it is the hub's
record (`POST /api/notices/seen`, as `landed:<machineId>:<at>`), so one
acknowledgement holds for every tab and device.

at.description: When it finished, in milliseconds: the landing's identity.

version.description: The build installed, or the build that failed and was rolled back.

autoUpdate.description: One setting for the whole fleet: a machine does not pick its own.

commands.description:
The ids of the last Install now commands this machine acted on, oldest
first: one delivered again is answered and not acted on twice.

cut.description:
What the last install cut: the work in flight when it was applied anyway,
because a person pressed Install now or auto-update had waited its cap.
Kept until the next install.

download.description:
How far this machine's download of `availableVersion` from its hub is,
while `downloading`; absent in every other phase.

failedVersion.description:
The build that failed to come up and was rolled back (or whose trial
ended undecided). Not retried by itself, unless `hubSilentTrials` says
its trials ended on the hub's silence ({@link failedForGood}).

heldChildren.description: Children a keeper the new build cannot speak to holds, while they are the reason for waiting (`waiting-sessions`).

hostsHub.description: True on the machine that runs the hub.

hubFetch.description:
While `downloading`, and the hub still fetches the build from its
release host: how far the hub's own fetch is, which the machine waits
on. Absent in every other phase, and once the hub holds the build.

hubSilentTrials.description:
How many trials of `failedVersion` in a row were rolled back because
the hub gave no answer for this machine's row (cli binary-health.ts
`HealthProblem`), not for the build's own fault; absent when its last
rollback was the build's own. Written with `failedVersion`, always.

keeperFailedVersion.description: The build whose session keeper could not start; the keeper is not handed to it again by itself.

keeperRestart.description:
The last time the agent found a session keeper wedged (alive, socket
open, no welcome) and restarted it, or (`retiring`) removed it, which
ended every session it held. The event a notice announces, as
`keeper:<machineId>:<at>`; the next one replaces it.

at.description: When the wedge was called, in milliseconds: the restart's identity.

children.description: Processes the keeper held, each a session or a helper, ended with it.

diagnostics.description: Where what the keeper was doing was saved, on that machine.

dials.description: Dials in a row that got no welcome.

retiring.description: It was a retiring keeper (an earlier build's, after a handover), removed rather than restarted: no session starts on it again.

silentForMs.description: From the first silent dial to the call.

landed.description: The last install or rollback that finished.

retiringKeepers.description:
Keepers of earlier builds still holding sessions after a handover, each
with how many: every new session starts on the current keeper
(`sessiondVersion`), and each of these exits once the last session it
holds has ended or gone to sleep. Absent when there is none.

sessiondKept.description:
The current session keeper stopped answering, and the watchdog does not
restart it while its unit holds these processes CawCo did not start: no
session starts on the machine until they end, and the next look after
that restarts it. Absent while it answers.

sessiondVersion.description: The build of the current session keeper, the one every new session starts on: the `keeper` link.

unconfirmedVersion.description:
The build whose trial no update helper could decide (cli binary-apply.ts
`endUndecided`), with `phase` `failed`: it may be the build that runs, its
health never confirmed, not rolled back, and not installed again by
itself (`failedVersion` names it too). Stays until a newer build is
taken up.

updatedAt.description: When anything in this state last changed. Not an identity for anything.

waitingOn.description: What `ready` waits for: the work in flight a restart would cut now.

waitingSince.description: When auto-update first waited on work in flight; it installs anyway once its cap has passed.

BlockArrangement.description:
A project's arrangement, as `GET /api/projects/:id/blocks` answers it:
each page the person has arranged, its blocks in order, and the drafts
standing on a page as proposed blocks. A page never arranged is absent,
and shows its built-in blocks in their own order.

BlockMetadata.description: Everything a renderer may need beyond `content`, keyed by the kind that uses it.

accountMove.description: A `system.account_move`: what the hub did at the session's account's limit.

asked.description: A session asked for it, not its account's limit: true on every line written now.

asks.description: It restarted from the person's own messages alone: nothing was summarised.

by.description:
Who asked for it, as the line's detail names them: a session by its
name, or a comment on a task. Absent on a line a hub stored before
continuations stayed one session.

kind.description:
The session went on in a fresh conversation of its own, seeded with
a summary of the one before (or the person's own messages alone,
`asks`), on `to` from `from` (null on a harness without accounts):
a continuation anything but the person's own Continue asked for,
which stays one session (hub `foldContinued`). The line stands
between the two conversations.

move.description:
It went on from a summary as its move to `to`, as the policy says
({@link Compaction} `summary`): at its account's limit (`limit`:
the window that refused it and when that resets, or its refused
sign-in), or ahead of one (`ahead`: its account's forecast run-out,
its extra usage, or a person's move, `because`). Absent: a session
or a task asked for it.

because.description:
Why a session moved other than at a limit refusing a turn of it
({@link AccountMove} `moved`): its account was forecast to run out at
`runsOutAt` (a rebalance between turns), its cache was cold at its wake,
so the move re-read nothing extra, Claude Code refused `from`'s
credential for good (`refused`: the hub signed it out there), or a turn
of it ran on `from`'s extra usage past its plan, which says to move then.

preparedAtPct.description:
Null on every line written now (no summary is written ahead of a
limit any more), and never shown. Sent only because the TestFlight
builds 20261015 to 20261018 require it, which the hub's wire check
holds to (packages/hub/scripts/openapi.ts); it goes in the change
that expires them.

writtenOn.description: The account whose summariser wrote the summary it went on from; null when nothing was summarised.

asked.description: Moved because a person asked (`POST /api/instances/:id/account`), not at a limit.

because.description: Why it moved other than at a limit ({@link MoveBecause}); absent: its account's limit refused a turn, or a person asked.

compact.description:
Moved to another organization with a context of the policy's
`moveWholeUnderK` or more, compacted natively ({@link Compaction}):
it files its open items, then its harness's `/compact` runs, as its
first steps on `to`, or on `from` before the move
({@link compactFirst}). The line is said again under its id as that
goes.

compactBy.description: The harness whose own `/compact` runs, when it is not Claude Code's: what its compaction keeps is less.

compactFirst.description:
The compaction runs on `from`, warm, and the move follows it: the
policy's `beforeMove`. Absent: it runs on `to` after the move.

cost.description: What the re-read cost on `to`: a percent of the window it is counted against, named as `windowWords` names it; absent when unpriced.

ended.description:
What the move ended with its old process: work it held for later (its
background tasks, its one-time wake-ups), which no resume on another
account brings back. The session is told on arrival what ended.

relaunched.description:
Its process ended on `to` before it took a step of the compaction,
and the hub started it again there to take it.

removed.description: Moved because a person removed `from` (`DELETE /api/accounts/:id`): every session on it moves off.

resetsAt.description: When that window resets, epoch ms; null when nothing said.

sameOrganization.description: Both accounts in one organization: its prompt cache came along.

signedOut.description: Moved because a person signed `from` out on its machine (`DELETE /api/accounts/:id/machines/:machineId`): every session on it there moves off.

signedOutOn.description: With `signedOut`: that machine, as it was named then.

summaryRefused.description:
The policy said to go on from a summary, which could not be written
for this move, in the hub's words: its harness's `/compact` ran
instead.

window.description: The window that refused it, as core usage/windows.ts `windowWords` names it.

action.description: What failed: a move whole (`move`), or, in a stored line, a continuation from a summary (`continue`).

asked.description: The session asked for it (`continue_session`), not its account's limit.

kind.description:
Moving it whole to `to` failed at `step`: it goes on in its
conversation, still on `from`. (`continue`, a continuation from a
summary, and `asked`, are history only: lines a hub stored before it
compacted natively.)

reason.description: What the hub got from the step that failed.

signedOut.description: It was moving off `from` because Claude Code refused `from`'s sign-in: `from` has no reset to wait for.

waits.description:
Only work its process holds for later kept it (a background task, a
one-time wake-up), and no person waits on it: the move goes when that
work ends, or once it has been held {@link RESTART_WAIT_CAP_MS},
ending it.

kind.description:
The session's process was ended, and by whom: a stop someone asked
for, or a signal from outside CawCo. A stop is never a failure; the
line says what starts it again.

cost.description: What the re-read will cost on `to`: a percent of its window; absent when unpriced.

kind.description:
A move whole the policy chose for a context large enough to compact
({@link Compaction} `whole`): it goes at `at` by itself, from `from`
to `to`, unless a person stops the session before then.

Claude Code refused `account`'s credential for good and no other
account can take the session: it stays, and what it is sent waits at
the hub, until `account` is signed in again or another comes free.

A work item's session whose project has Caw off: nothing wakes a
model there, so nothing carries it on past `account`'s limit,
neither a move nor a resume at the reset. A person sends it on.

resetsAt.description: When that limit resets, epoch ms; null when nothing said.

account.description: The account it is held on, at its limit.

accounts.description:
Every other account of its provider and why it didn't take it, or
that it could ({@link HeldAccount}): what a person reads, so a line
never says no account has room beside one that has. Absent on lines
stored before holds named them.

frees.description:
Another account that frees before `account` resets: it moves there
at `until`. Absent: `until` is `account`'s own reset.

until.description: The earliest moment an account takes it again, epoch ms: the line counts down to it.

artifactId.description: An artifact responses note's artifact ({@link import ("./harness").ARTIFACT_RESPONSES}): what its line opens.

artifactKind.description: That artifact's kind, which picks its line's glyph.

artifactLead.description: The words its line says before the artifact's title, by the notice it draws (core `ARTIFACT_NOTICES`): "Comments on", "Fix tray handed you".

artifactTitle.description: That artifact's title, as its line says it.

askRequestId.description: A `user.delegate_ask`'s hub permission requestId — what it waits on to be answered.

attachments.description:
What the reader attached to the turn: texts, parsed back out of its
`<pasted-text>` blocks, and files, out of its `Attached file:` lines.

compactFailure.description: {@link compactError} typed, as its harness typed the error ({@link import ("./session-messages").CompactionFailure}).

compactResult.description:
A compaction boundary read back from a harness that stores how it ended
(opencode): `failed` with the harness's words in `compactError`.

continuation.description:
A send that is the message a session went on from in a fresh
conversation (origin {@link import ("./harness/kinds").CONTINUATION_ORIGIN}):
drawn folded under the `continued` line before it, never as a turn.

delegateInstanceId.description: The delegate a `tool.handoff` started, read once off its result.

delegateTitle.description: The delegate's brief headline, carried beside {@link delegateInstanceId}.

designOffer.description:
A project note of Caw asking whether to build a design system: the
project it is for, whose Build and Not now the note draws under it.

errorTitle.description:
A failure card's heading (`ui.error`, `ui.session_error`); a missing
session's when unset on a session error, "Turn failed" otherwise.

harnessNote.description:
A `ui.system_note` that is a notice of the harness's in the user's role,
typed where its normaliser read it: what a reader draws it from, never
its `content`, which keeps its words for the shipped app.

images.description: A stored transcript can name an image it no longer carries, hence the optional src.

lfsOffer.description:
A project note that a folder was made a repository with files left out
for their size: the offer of Git LFS for them (ProjectNoteEvent `repo`'s
`lfsOffer`), whose Track with LFS and Not now the note draws under it.

noteKind.description: Harness-injected user-role content (task notifications, reminders, compaction).

noteTaskToolId.description: A task notification's Task `tool_use_id` — folds the note into its branch.

notice.description:
A notice's kind, its `system` origin's name ({@link import ("./harness").CAWCO_NOTICE}):
`leak`, `limit`, `work-item`, `routine:<id>`.

peerName.description: Its display name, as the sender's host asserted it.

peerSession.description: The sender's host-openable session, so the card can link back to it.

permissionMode.description: `init` only, and re-reported every turn: what the session answers tools with.

reportHeadline.description: A delegate report's one-or-two-sentence outcome, from `finish_item`'s `headline`; the body is the full report.

reportKind.description: Set when a `user.peer` is a delegate's auto-report rather than a hand-off.

resultImages.description: Images returned by the tool, as the hub's media references.

resultRecord.description:
The stored record a call's result came in (a Claude Code `tool_result`
entry's uuid, a pi entry's id, an OpenCode message's id), which the
call's own block never names otherwise: what a transcript index names a
match in a tool's output by (find in a conversation), so the match opens
at the very call it answered, however many calls ran beside it.

routineMade.description:
A project note that a session made a routine (ProjectNoteEvent
`routine-made`): the note draws Keep, Turn off and Open beside it.

ruleName.description: A `user.rule`'s rule name, read off its `[Rule: <name>]` marker line.

sendFailed.description: Why a send did not go: its record's reason.

sendModeAsk.description: No permission mode to wake its session on: its record's ask ({@link ModeAsk}).

sendRefusal.description: What refused it, when the hub did: its record's refusal.

skills.description: `init` only: which of the commands are skills rather than commands.

slashCommands.description: `init` only: what this session answers behind `/`, without the leading slash.

subagentModel.description: The `model` override the spawn input asked for, when present.

thinkingDurationMs.description:
How long the thinking block ran, measured by the hub's clock between the
block opening and its settled message. Preferred over transcript
adjacency, which reads 0 when thinking and a tool call land in one frame.

toolCut.description:
What cut the call mid-run, when CawCo did (core turn-cuts.ts): "your
Stop", a machine's pause. `toolResult` then says so, in place of the
harness's "rejected" or "aborted", which no answer of the person's was.
On a `ui.interrupted` line, the cut that line is.

toolDiff.description: The unified file diff returned by an apply_patch call.

toolUseResult.description: The reader's answers to an `AskUserQuestion`, normalised by the harness adapter.

tooling.description: `init` only: the MCP servers and tools behind the `/` palette.

BlockPlace.description: One block in a page's arrangement.

hidden.description: Folded off the page; it keeps its place and comes back from the page's end.

width.description: Narrow takes the columns its measure needs; wide spans the row.

BlockTooling.description: The MCP servers and tools an `init` announced.

BlockType.description: What a block is: the row kind a renderer draws it as.

kind.description:
Hub-originated: a project's arrangement of blocks changed (a block
moved, resized, hidden or shown, a view placed or made a tab): read it
again.

BridgedHeldPlace.description:
A project place's `held` as installable apps' documents declare it, which
the places list once showed for the person's Continue and Discard: always
null now, its shape kept for the wire only. The wire check (openapi.ts
`--check`) refuses to stop sending it while TestFlight 20261017 or
20261018 can be installed, though no app reads it; it goes in the change
that expires them (bash apps/apple/scripts/testflight.sh --expire 20261018).

BrowserAskFrame.description:
A browser ask (Projects spec §5.11): a session asks the person to take
over its project's browser, with one sentence of reason and the page's
origin. It parks as a `permission_request` for {@link BROWSER_ASK_TOOL}
carrying this beside the tool's input, so it lands in Needs you, the
transcript and push as every ask does. Take over answers it as taken
(`POST /api/browsers/:key/takeover`, an Approve from an app that has no
Take over yet); Decline denies it with the person's words. The tool's
call waits on until the person hands back.

artifactId.description: The browser artifact in the asking session's panel: Take over opens the panel on it.

machineId.description: The machine the browser runs on: the asking session's.

origin.description: The page's origin the agent named, `scheme://host[:port]`.

reason.description: One sentence: what the person is needed for.

BrowserFrame.description: Daemon-originated: the machine's runtime and every browser on it, whole, on each change.

BrowserHandback.description: What a hand-back answers: the front page's origin, and nothing else of it.

origin.description: The front page's origin as it was handed back; null when no page was in front.

requestId.description: The browser ask the take-over answered, when it answered one.

BrowserHandedBackFrame.description:
Daemon-originated: a take-over ended on the machine, whichever way: the
person's Hand back, no view open for {@link TAKEOVER_UNWATCHED_MS}, or the
browser stopped. Sent before the record's own frame, so the hub learns
every end the same way and the ask's call answers with the page's origin.

origin.description: The front page's origin as it was handed back; null when no page was in front.

requestId.description: The browser ask the take-over answered, when it answered one.

BrowserHostKind.description: Which host runs a browser on its machine: a container where a runtime answers, a local Chromium where none does.

BrowserKey.description: Which browser: a project's, or the machine's for sessions outside any project.

BrowserListFrame.description:
Hub-originated, to every dashboard socket (the app's included): every
browser of the fleet, whole, as the socket opens and on each change of
any (a machine's frame, a start, stop, take-over, hand-back or removal).
A view paints from it and follows it, and never polls.

BrowserPorts.description: One browser's ports; `http` and `media` are the container host's alone.

BrowserRow.description: One browser as its machine reports it.

lastUsedAt.description: ms epoch of the last agent connection or viewer.

origin.description:
The origin of the page the person's view shows (neko's front window on
the container host, the screencast's page on the local host), as the
machine reads it through its own DevTools link; absent while that page
is none (`about:blank`, no page). For the person's band alone: the gate
never sends it to an agent.

ports.description: One browser's ports; `http` and `media` are the container host's alone.

progress.description: How far an image build is, while `state` is `pulling` or `building`.

takeover.description: Who holds the browser privately, since when, and the ask it answers; null while no one does.

BrowserRuntime.description: The machine's container runtime as the agent found it, or the sentence that names the install.

BuildInfo.description: What a daemon reports about the checkout it was started from.

commit.description: Short git SHA, when the checkout is a git one.

dirty.description: Whether that checkout has uncommitted changes.

startedAt.description: When this daemon started, ms epoch.

BuiltOn.description:
A card or pin a done task's attempt was dispatched on whose value moved
since: answered differently, or reopened. Nothing reopens on its own.

CallerKind.description: What a request is to the hub.

CanvasAnchor.description: A canvas's mark stands on one of its elements, by id.

CanvasElement.description: An element as the outline reads it: Excalidraw's own fields, those it needs.

customData.description: Ours on Excalidraw's element: `shape` names what a held stroke was read as when Excalidraw has no type for it (a triangle).

CanvasExport.description: A canvas's export: the `.excalidraw` file, its outline and its latest picture.

host.description: Host mode's `name[:port]` beside `origin`: a bridge for readers before it (core `PreviewAddress`).

origin.description: Its session's preview origin, where the canvas's page stands (`Created.port` / `origin`).

png.description: Base64 PNG; null until a screen has drawn one.

CapAmount.description: A spend cap's amount and the span it counts over.

CapPeriod.description: The span a project's cap counts over, in the hub's own zone.

CarrySpan.description: Which account carries new sessions from `from` to `to`; null: none can.

CatalogMovedFrame.description:
A machine's stored transcripts moved (agent catalog-index.ts): the
sessions whose files were written, added or removed since the last such
frame. The hub reads the machine's catalog again only when one of them may
stand in Recent (hub stored-recent.ts).

CatalogType.description: One entry of a catalog, saying where it comes from.

budget.description: A type's spending limit: any of cost, turns and time, per a period.

lands.description:
Where a work item's work goes once it finishes (hub/src/landing.ts):
`main` onto the repository's default branch, `branch` to a branch of its
own on origin, `pr` to that branch with a pull request, `none` nowhere (the
work is not commits; its outputs are the deliverable).

path.description: The file it was read from, inside its folder (the project's, or its area's).

shadows.description: A project or area type that replaces a type of the same name below it.

CawRunning.description:
One thing Caw started that still runs: a session as a project's forget
lists it (project-stops `RunningSession`), and what it is.

kind.description: An attempt at a task, or a delegate of the conversation's.

offline.description: Its machine is not connected: it stops when its machine is back.

parentId.description: The nearest running row it is a delegate of; null for a top row.

taskTitle.description: Its task's title, for an attempt, as the project's index has it.

title.description: Its name (a turn's: what it answers); null names it by its folder.

CawStart.description:
How every start of a project's conversation goes, the hub's start and the
person's alike (hub caw.ts `startOf`, `POST /api/projects/:id/caw/place`):
where it runs, on the project's harness and model, in the project's mode
(its own, its area's, the fleet's), else the one the person last chose for
that harness on that machine. A null mode is no mode: the start is refused
with the machine and harness to ask one for (core `ModeAsk`).

ChainLink.description:
One link of a sheet's chain: a component, by its name, at the place it is
used (1-based line and column); the last link is the story, by its
export's name, at the export in the story file.

ChannelRelease.description: The newest signed release of one channel, as the release host shows it.

ClaudeExtraUsage.description: Extra usage: requests past the plan's limits, paid as they go.

inUse.description: Whether the account is spending extra usage now (`isUsingOverage`).

offReason.description:
Why it is off, in words from Claude Code's `overageDisabledReason`
("out of credits"); null when on or when it gave no reason worth saying.

on.description: Whether requests past the plan may run as extra usage (`overageStatus`).

resetsAt.description: When extra usage resets, when Claude Code said.

ClaudeLimits.description:
A Claude account's limits, as its sessions' Claude Code reported them
(`rate_limit_event`, `accountInfo()`). A window whose `resetsAt` has passed
with no newer report reads 0%.

error.description:
Why there are no windows, in words. Kept beside {@link errorKind} for the
shipped app, which compares it to "not signed in"; a reader decides on
`errorKind`.

errorKind.description:
Why there are no windows, typed: `not-signed-in`, the account is signed
in on no machine; `no-reading`, nothing on the account has reported any
yet. Null when there are windows.

extraUsage.description: Extra usage as the last `rate_limit_event` said; null: it never said.

fetchedAt.description:
When the windows were last known to be so: Claude Code's last report on
the account, or a later turn on it that changed nothing.

stale.description:
Nothing on the account has confirmed the windows for
{@link CLAUDE_READING_CURRENT_MS}: they are as of `fetchedAt`.

CliInstall.description:
One install of a CLI a sync depends on, as the machine found it.

The reason this exists: a machine may carry several `claude` binaries at
once (a homebrew one, an npm-global one, the local installer's), PATH picks
whichever comes first, and a CLI too old for a flag the sync passes fails
with a sentence that names neither the binary nor its version. Reporting the
install makes that a fact on the dashboard rather than an expedition.

path.description: Absolute path of the executable, resolved through any symlink.

used.description: Set on the one the sync actually ran — the binary a failure came out of.

version.description: What `--version` said, when it would say.

CommandEnvelope.description:
Client → hub: an operator action as a durable, trackable object rather than
a fire-and-forget call. `commandId` is client-generated and unique per
submission; `payload` is exactly what the corresponding legacy relay
operation takes today.

CommandKind.description: The operations a command envelope can carry — 1:1 with existing relay ops.

CommandQueue.description: A command's wait for a slot: which, and who holds it (the marker's words).

CommandQueueFrame.description:
Daemon → hub: a {@link CONTROL_RUN_COMMAND} run named `runId` began
waiting for a slot (`queue`), or stopped (null).

CommentAttachment.description:
A picture, a text or a file a person's entry carries, uploaded to the hub
as it was attached (`POST /api/files`) and kept by its reference: the doc
holds words, never bytes. A picture reaches the agent as an image block,
a text folded into the delivery, a file on the session's machine.

height.description: A picture's pixels, when the composer read them.

ref.description: The hub's reference to its bytes: `/api/files/<sha256>`.

CommentRead.description:
What `comment_read` answers: each of the session's artifacts with pins
that match, the page's address the person last marked it at, and the time to
pass as the next `since`. A pin on ink carries the ink's box in the page.

address.description: The page's address the person last marked it at; its own route before any delivery.

link.description: Its link, `[title](cawco:artifact/<id>)`: what the agent names it by to the person.

CompactMethod.description:
How a session's context is made small as it moves to another organization,
whose cache it can't read: its harness's own `/compact` after a turn that
files its open items (`native`), a fresh conversation of the same session
opened on a summary {@link Compaction.summarizer} writes (`summary`), or
nothing, the conversation moved as it is (`whole`).

Compaction.description:
How a session is compacted when it moves, by the moment the hub moves it
(hub at-limit.ts `compactionPlan`, the one rule every mover reads). A
context under {@link AtLimit.moveWholeUnderK} thousand tokens, or one whose
cache carries to the account it moves to, moves whole whatever this says.
A session that stays on its organization is compacted by its harness on
its own; before that, once a turn ends with its context within
{@link Compaction.fileRoom} tokens of where that harness compacts it, the
hub gives it one turn to file its open items (hub at-limit.ts `fileDue`).

atLimit.description:
Nothing can run on its account (its limit refused a turn, its sign-in
was refused): `summary` goes on from a summary on the target; `native`
moves it whole and compacts it there, cold; `whole` moves it as it is.
A summary that can't be written for a move (its summariser can't fit
the conversation, can't be placed, or the conversation can't be read)
takes `native` for that move, its line saying why.

beforeMove.description:
Its account can run it still (forecast to run out, on extra usage past
its plan, a person's move): `native` files its open items and compacts
it there, warm, then moves it; `summary` files them, then goes on from a
summary on the target; `whole` moves it as it is.

fileRoom.description:
The room, in tokens, short of the point where its harness compacts it
on its own (core harness.ts `NeutralResultMessage.compactsAt`), at which
a session files its open items into its records: once per rise, at the
end of the first turn whose reading is within it, the next compaction
re-arming it (hub at-limit.ts `fileDue`). 0 files none.

summarizer.description: Who writes a summary: its harness and model, placed as any start is.

CompactionFailure.description:
How a compaction failed, as its harness typed the error it failed on:
`kind`, the harness's own sort of it (OpenCode's error `type`, as
`provider.timeout`), or `unknown` when it gave none; `status`, the
provider's HTTP status when there was one; `message`, its words as said.

ComponentDoc.description:
A component's props as the stage read them. `types` says how: `checked`
by the TypeScript checker or a docgen of its own, `jsdoc` from JSDoc
and PropTypes alone (the project has no TypeScript), `unknown` when
nothing could read them, with `note` saying why.

ConfigInspectionView.description: What a machine has, as a read says it ({@link ConfigInspection}).

memory.description:
The machine's own user CLAUDE.md, or null when it has none. `managed` says
cawco wrote what is there — an unmanaged one is worth adopting. `docs`
is whatever the machine has under `~/.claude/memories/`, read the same way.

ConnectAskFrame.description:
A connect ask: a session asks the person to sign the hub in to one of the
fleet's MCP servers that signs in with OAuth (Configure › MCP), so the
session gets its tools. It parks as a `permission_request` for
{@link CONNECT_ASK_TOOL} carrying this beside the tool's input. Connect
starts the hub's sign-in (`POST /api/fleet/mcp/:name/sign-in` with its
`requestId` and `access`) in a tab of its own; the hub keeps the
credential, and its sign-in landing answers the call. Not now declines it.

It stands as a card in the session's transcript at the call that asked
it, and that card becomes the call's record once it is answered.

access.description:
The access Connect asks the provider for: the one the agent named, a
reconnect's held from the sign-in that ended, or the server's one; null
for a server that names no scopes.

again.description: Asked again: the server's sign-in ended (`auth.ended`), its access held.

reason.description: One sentence: why the session needs it.

server.description: The fleet MCP server, as Configure › MCP names it.

url.description: The provider's sign-in address (its authorization endpoint), shown whole before anything opens.

ConnectionState.description: `signed-in`: its tools answer. `needs-sign-in`: a key or a sign-in is owed. `error`: `reason` says what failed.

ConnectionView.description: A connection as every route and tool answers it: never its key.

account.description: Which account of the service it is, in the owner's words (`@brand`).

app.description: For `app` auth, once its registration is held: what names the app.

areas.description: Areas whose every project's sessions may use it, read as each area's projects now (core areas.ts).

command.description: For `stdio`: the command the hub runs.

device.description:
For `device` auth, while its code sign-in can still finish: the code the
person enters, where, and when it lapses, epoch ms.

gh.description: For `gh` auth: the machine whose gh it reads, and the account there.

hasSecret.description: Whether a key or OAuth tokens are held for it.

header.description: For `header` auth: the header (or, for `stdio`, the environment variable) the key goes in.

projects.description: Projects whose every session may use it, beside the delegate types that list it.

reason.description: Why it is in `error` or `needs-sign-in`; absent when signed in.

signIn.description:
The sign-in under way, while it can still finish: the page it was sent
to and when it lapses, epoch ms. A press on the row opens that same
page again rather than starting another.

tools.description: Its tools' names, as the hub last listed them; absent before a first listing.

seen.description: Items its last call saw; null until its first call.

ContinuationJob.description:
A continuation in a new session the hub is carrying, as every dashboard
follows it: the source files its open items (a person's Continue), is
summarised, then a new session starts seeded with the summary and those
items. The hub owns it from the POST that starts it to its end; its Cancel
(`DELETE /api/continuations/:id`) stops it in any stage before `started`.

inPlace.description:
Never sent: no job goes on in place now. Declared only because the
TestFlight builds 20261015 and 20261015.3 read it, which the hub's wire
check holds to (packages/hub/scripts/openapi.ts); it goes in the change
that expires them.

summariserInstanceId.description: Absent when the source is short enough that nothing is summarised.

waiting.description:
While `waiting`: what for, in the machine's words (`waiting for work in
flight to end: 1 command running`), since when it has run (epoch ms;
null when not known), and the latest moment it goes on, ending that
work (core `RESTART_WAIT_CAP_MS` from when it began to wait).

ContinueStep.description:
The steps of continuing a session from a summary, in order: read its
transcript, summarise it, start its fresh conversation. Until the last
one is done it goes on in the conversation it has.

ControlPayload.description:
`control`: invoke a named method on a live session, or on the machine when
`instanceId` is absent. The method is one of the neutral names in harness.ts
({@link CONTROL_INTERRUPT}, …) plus {@link RESOLVE_PERMISSION}; the reply
comes back as a `control_result` frame carrying the same `requestId`.

Machine-scoped, `method` names either a session-catalog operation — routed to
whichever harness owns the id (`harness`, or merged across all when listing)
— or a machine feature (`installTool`, the fleet controls). With
no `instanceId` and no `harness`, `listSessions` merges every harness.

from.description: The instance a fleet-originated control claims as its caller; the hub honours the call only when the target is that instance's own delegate.

harness.description: The harness the machine-scoped call is addressed at; session calls route by instance.

error.description: A refusal's words, as said; {@link refusal} is what a reader decides on.

failed.description: `listSessions` only, and only when some harness's listing threw: those harnesses, whose sessions `result` leaves out.

kind.description: No `instanceId` when the call it answers was machine-scoped.

refusal.description: Why the machine's agent refused the call, typed; absent on an answer, and on a refusal the hub made itself.

down.description: A preview's start the machine refused: the hop that is down (core preview/protocol.ts `PreviewStartDown`). A daemon from before it said one says it in its words alone (preview proxy.ts `startRefused`).

unanswered.description: `listSessions` only, and only when some harness did not list in time: those harnesses, whose sessions `result` leaves out.

broken.description: What a decision page's program left broken on the picks and the links; absent when nothing.

cards.description: A decision page's cards' links, by id (`[question](cawco:decision/<artifact>/<card>)`): what the agent names each by.

decisions.description: A decision page's decisions, by id, in page order.

dropped.description: Components a decision page's program names that the library does not have: dropped, never drawn.

errors.description: A component canvas's compile errors, from the modules its states files import.

held.description: Your change waits as this next version: your parent had opened the artifact, and their panel keeps the version they opened until they call artifact_show.

hint.description: A component canvas's next reads, one line.

host.description: Host mode's `name[:port]` beside `origin`: a bridge for readers before it (core `PreviewAddress`).

link.description: Its link, `[title](cawco:artifact/<id>)`: what the agent names it by to the person.

marked.description: Made again under its name: what it changed, each by its link (`[label](cawco:change/<artifact>/<anchor>)`).

moves.description: A component canvas's flow moves, each with the animations it fired.

name.description: Its slug, what every artifact tool takes.

note.description: A canvas made with nothing to draw says so.

opened.description: Whether a view the person is looking at has it on screen ({@link Opened}).

origin.description:
A draft canvas's: its session's preview origin (core `PreviewAddress`),
where a client loads the canvas at `/__cawco/canvas/<id>/`: its port on
the hub's host, and (host mode) a whole origin of its own too, which a
client picks by where it reached the hub (core `previewRoute`).

render.description: What a browser drew of a component canvas (the panel's, else the daemon's): each frame's state, and what it loads.

route.description: Its live document on the hub's preview listener.

routes.description: Each card's route by the project's Who decides, by id, a line after its link; absent when no card carries a kind.

sheet.description: A sheet as its stage reads it: its stories with their args, its meta, and each component's props.

stage.description: A sheet's stage, or a served preview's server, as it stands once started.

tailnet.description: A draft canvas's origin on the tailnet name while the hub serves HTTPS there (core `PreviewAddress`).

title.description: What it is named by to the person.

weight.description: A folder preview's: what it loads at most, from its folder's files.

why.description: Why it is not on screen, one sentence; only with `opened: false`.

wrote.description: The element ids a canvas's create wrote.

CutCommand.description:
A shell command a session's process was running when it died: the command
as the model asked it, and the end of what it had printed by then, when
its harness kept any (Claude Code spools a running command's output:
agent claude.ts `cutCommands`; pi and OpenCode keep none, and their
commands are read off the session's own tool calls: agent session.ts
`#shells`). The hub says each one interrupted, with that output or that
none was kept, in the turn it hands back and in the item's report when
the death fails it.

output.description: What it printed: empty when it printed nothing, or when none was kept ({@link unkept}).

unkept.description: Its harness keeps no output of a running command (pi, OpenCode).

DamagedHubRecord.description:
A record of the hub's own that it read at start and found damaged: the
feature it belongs to is off until the person resets it (hub
`notices.ts`, `binary-updates.ts`). Nothing reads it as empty meanwhile.

DamagedRow.description:
What the hub lays over a session row whose record, or whose workspace's
record, is damaged on its machine ({@link DamagedRecordReport}): the file,
why, and the way out that removes it (`archive`: archive workspace
`workspaceId`; `end`: end the session).

DecidesTable.description: A project's table as the hub reads it.

from.description: Where each kind's member came from: the project's decides.md, its area's, or the fleet's (core areas.ts).

problems.description: decides.md's problems, the project's and its area's; the table is then every kind → `you`.

yours.description: Paths whose change needs a card the person picked (enforced later); empty when none.

DecisionAnswer.description:
One choice a page asks the person (a decision page's question, or a
`data-cawco-choice` an HTML page declares), as they answered it: not yet
(`open`, perhaps with a note), with options (`picked`), picked then
unpicked (`cleared`), or with an option a revision took out (`gone`).
`earlierRevision`: answered on a revision before the one shown now.

question.description: Its question; a choice an HTML page declares has none.
Its question; a choice an HTML page declares has none.
Its question; a choice an HTML page declares has none.
Its question; a choice an HTML page declares has none.

settled.description: Who settled it for the person (`settle`), why and its sources; absent for his own pick.

DecisionLink.description: Another of the project's decision pages, named on a page's row.

DecisionOption.description: One option of a card, as the page labelled it.

builds.description: What it means building or changing (the Option's `builds`); absent when it says none.

cost.description: What picking it costs the person (the Option's `cost`); empty when it has none.

keycap.description: Its digit in the card: the kit numbers options 1, 2, 3… in page order.

line.description: The line under its label; empty when it has none.

DecisionPageRead.description: A page opened in the Decisions tab: its summary, its record and its last send.

artifactId.description: Its artifact; null for a page whose artifact the hub no longer holds.

decided.description: Cards decided in its record; 0 before it is decided.

sentAt.description: When the person last sent (I'm done picking, a comment), ISO; null before.

tasks.description: Tasks filed from it ({@link DECIDED_FIELD} naming it).

updatedAt.description: When it was built, picked or sent last, ms epoch.

DecisionPageSummary.description: A page as the Decisions tab lists it: its facts, the pages it links to, and its questions and answers for search.

after.description: The pages one of its decisions comes after, in the order its cards name them.

answers.description: What its record says was decided, for search: each card's chosen options by label, and the why behind its pick ({@link pickRecord}); none before it is decided.

artifactId.description: Its artifact; null for a page whose artifact the hub no longer holds.

decided.description: Cards decided in its record; 0 before it is decided.

questions.description: Its cards' questions, in page order.

tasks.description: Tasks filed from it ({@link DECIDED_FIELD} naming it).

unlocks.description: The pages with a decision that comes after one of its own.

updatedAt.description: When it was built, picked or sent last, ms epoch.

askedOf.description: The session asked to make its tasks; null when none was (Make tasks not pressed).

madeAt.description: When its picks were recorded: the Send that decided it, or the pick since that moved them, ISO.

DecisionSent.description: What the hub answers a send on a page: who heard it.

instanceId.description: The project's conversation it went to, when it went there.

DecisionWriter.description: The session that wrote a page.

ended.description: It takes no input now: what the person does on the page goes to {@link heardBy}, else to the project's Caw (hub artifacts/taker.ts).

heardBy.description: Who hears the person on the page instead while it takes none: the session that delegated it. Absent with `ended`: Caw.

kind.description:
Hub-originated: a project's decision pages changed (one was built,
picked on or sent, its record written, its graph edited): read them
again.

graph.description:
Always false: no client draws the decisions as a graph. Sent only
because TestFlight ios 20261018 requires the field to read the list; it
goes once that build is no longer installable, 2027-01-16 (bash
apps/apple/scripts/testflight.sh --expire 20261018).

problems.description: What could not be read, one sentence each.

DeclaredStep.description: A step as the project declares it.

inputs.description: The paths whose change makes it run; absent: it always runs.

name.description: What the report calls it.

needs.description: The capability of the machine it runs on; absent: the workspace's own.

stopsRest.description: A failure leaves the steps after it unrun.

targetMap.description:
Its target map (`targets:`, hub app-targets.ts): it runs only for a diff
that changes what the map's targets compile, given the targets to build
in its command's `{targets}`; absent: `inputs` decides.

timeoutSec.description: Seconds before it is killed; the gate's default when absent.

DelegateBudget.description: A type's spending limit: any of cost, turns and time, per a period.

DelegateEvent.description:
One line of what a delegate and its parent said to each other through the
hub — a `delegate_events` row (packages/hub `db/schema.ts`), summed up per
delegate over `POST /api/delegate-summaries` ({@link DelegateSummary}),
paged over `GET /api/delegate-events` and pushed as a `delegate_event`
frame. The hub is the system of record: the transcript markers say the
same things, but only for a reader who was watching, and only as text to
be parsed back.

payload.description: The tool input as the harness asked it — `{filepath, diff}`, `{questions}`, …

headline.description: The delegate's one-or-two-sentence outcome, when it finished with `finish_item`.

notice.description:
The hub's own word about the delegate's work, not the delegate's
report (core injected.ts `reportMarker`, its outcome `notice`):
its workspace held, or retired with its commits in a carry (hub
workspaces.ts `workspaceNotice`). Absent on a report.

outputs.description:
The files its finish copied into its project's folder, as paths
from the folder's root (`assets/tsk-12/plan.md`); absent when it
handed in none.

DelegateEventBase.description: What every kind of {@link DelegateEvent} carries, whichever it is.

createdAt.description: When the hub recorded it, as JSON carries a date.

id.description: The hub's row id — what a fold deduplicates on and orders by.

instanceId.description: The delegate the traffic is about — never the parent, on any of the kinds.

requestId.description: The permission request an ask and its answer share. Null on a report.

status.description: An ask's own state; null on an answer and a report, which settle nothing.

kind.description: Hub-originated: delegate traffic; `instanceId` is the delegate's.

DelegateSummary.description:
What a delegate's card in its parent's transcript draws of its traffic
with that parent, as `POST /api/delegate-summaries` answers it: the newest
report whole, the asks still waiting whole, and how many of each there
were. The rest of its events stay on the hub; the card draws none of them.

asks.description: How many asks it routed to the parent, answered or not.

pending.description: Its asks still waiting on an answer, oldest first.

payload.description: The tool input as the harness asked it — `{filepath, diff}`, `{questions}`, …

report.description: Its newest report, or null before its first.

headline.description: The delegate's one-or-two-sentence outcome, when it finished with `finish_item`.

notice.description:
The hub's own word about the delegate's work, not the delegate's
report (core injected.ts `reportMarker`, its outcome `notice`):
its workspace held, or retired with its commits in a carry (hub
workspaces.ts `workspaceNotice`). Absent on a report.

outputs.description:
The files its finish copied into its project's folder, as paths
from the folder's root (`assets/tsk-12/plan.md`); absent when it
handed in none.

through.description:
The highest event id the summary counts. A pushed `delegate_event` at or
below it is already in here; one above it came after.

DelegateType.description: One named preset. `name` is the key a `delegate` call's `type` asks for.

account.description:
The account its sessions prefer, when placement allows it (the machine,
project and task allow it, and it is not benched or past its reserve).
Absent: the provider's strategy chooses.

connections.description:
The connections (Projects spec §5.5) its sessions may call, by name: the
hub lists each one's tools to them as `conn__<name>__<tool>` and runs
every call itself, so no key reaches the session. A project type file
says `mcp: [x-brand]`.

description.description: What the calling model reads to decide whether this is the right type.

effort.description: How hard the model thinks: the same {@link EffortLevel} scale every other effort control uses.

mayStart.description:
The delegate types its sessions may start, by name ({@link MayStart}):
`["any"]` every type, an orchestrator's; any other list keeps them leaves
that may start those types alone; empty (and absent) none. A `delegate`
call's `may_start` sets it for one delegate, never past what its caller
