may start itself ({@link narrowMayStart}).

name.description: Unique across the fleet; what a `delegate` call's `type` param names.

role.description:
The toolset its sessions run in ({@link SESSION_ROLES}): a project type's
`role:` (delegates/*.md). Absent: a delegate's.

startingSet.description:
The skills and MCP servers its sessions start with, and no others
({@link StartingSet}). Absent: everything installed, as before any set.

DesignCard.description: A component in the library, as the map answers it: counts, or its card.

drawn.description: Frames a browser drew of its states (rest and forced), from the stage's reports.

moves.description: Flow moves its states files declare (`from` + `play`), detailed only.

props.description: Its props as docgen reads them, for one component's card only.

DesignLink.description: Where a component is used, or what it renders: the other component, and the call site when a draw saw it.

DesignMap.description: A page of the design map.

dir.description: The folder the page covers, from the toolchain root.

root.description: The toolchain root, from the clone's root.

steer.description: What to do when the page was cut, one sentence.

DesignOfferState.description: Where a project's design offer stands (`GET /api/projects/:id/design-offer`).

answer.description: `open` while unanswered; `built`: Build filed the task; `dismissed`: Not now.

DeskAlertFrame.description:
The socket frame that shows something that needs the person on the
desk they are at, in place of a phone push (hub push.ts): the tab named
`to` shows it as a desktop notification, and answers with a
{@link DeskAck}. Its words are the real ones: it never leaves the
person's network.

collapseId.description: The notification's tag: a newer one under it replaces the older.

path.description: Where it opens when that is a place of the dashboard's own (a decision card), as its path; null: by `session`.

renotify.description:
A newer alert under its tag alerts again rather than replacing the older
in silence: an artifact's (one tag per artifact, hub push.ts `pinAsked`).

session.description: Where it opens: the session it is about; null opens Needs you.

to.description: The tab to show it: the one in use, by its presence id.

DeviceKind.description: The kind of client a pairing is for.

DiscoveredMcpView.description: A machine's own server as a read says it.

managed.description: Whether cawco wrote it — an unmanaged row is one worth adopting.

shadowedBy.description:
Set when a nearer scope defines the same name and wins. Claude Code's own
precedence is local > project > user, and a fleet server quietly shadowed
by a checkout is the kind of thing a reader should be told, not debug.

DiscoveredSkill.description: One skill a machine really has. `plugin` skills come from an installed plugin.

description.description: The SKILL.md front matter's `description`, when it has one.

path.description: Absolute path of the skill's directory, for the reader and for adoption.

DispatchView.description: A project's dispatch: its settings, and what the dispatcher would do now.

budget.description: What an attempt may spend where its task and its delegate call say nothing; null: no limit.

conversationInstanceId.description: The project's Caw session, once the hub has started one.

dispatch.description: Whether the hub starts attempts at ready tasks on its own.

frontier.description: The tasks it would start next, in order.

lands.description: Where an attempt lands when its task and type say nothing.

paused.description: Why it would start nothing now even with a ready task; null when it would.

queued.description: Tasks whose `runs:` hook start waits for a slot, oldest first.

runsOn.description: Where an attempt runs when its task says nothing (runs-on.ts); null: any machine with a checkout.

EffortLevel.description:
How hard the model thinks, and how much it spends doing it: Claude Code's
effort scale, in its own order. Hand-written rather than tunnelled from the
SDK — nothing in this file imports a harness SDK, and `@cawco/core` has no
dependencies at all — but it is the SDK's `EffortLevel` verbatim, so the
claude adapter hands it straight on.

Effort is not only thinking depth. A lower level also buys fewer and more
consolidated tool calls, less preamble and terser confirmations; a higher one
spends tokens in all of those places. A harness with no such knob reports
`effort: false` rather than mapping onto this.

EndedBy.description:
Who ended a session's process ({@link AccountMove} `ended`): a person (the
dashboard's Stop), a session (its parent's `stop_delegate`, or its project's conversation's), the
hub's own work (`why`: a work item over, a project
forgotten), or a signal no part of CawCo sent (`outside`), after which the
turn it cut is handed back when there was one (`resumes`).

Envelope.description:
Every message on every hop. `payload` is whatever the verb carries — a neutral
message, a harness option object, a control call — passed through. The hub
routes on the envelope fields and peeks only what harness.ts names.

requestId.description: The `requestId` when the payload correlates to a permission or control reply.

endReason.description: Internal end-reconciliation evidence; never relayed to a client.

kind.description: Hub-originated routing failures (e.g. target machine offline).

lastErrorKind.description: A failed session's typed kind, when what failed typed it (core `KindedError`); `message` is its words.

modeAsk.description: A start that found no permission mode to start its session on: the page asks for one (core `ModeAsk`); `message` is never shown where this is read.

verb.description: The whole agent↔hub↔dashboard protocol. Adding a verb is a design decision.

ErrorSaid.description: One section's problem in an answer (`errorsSaid`).

kind.description:
What a canvas's section can't draw for, as the stage host keeps it until
it clears: the canvas page's own failure kinds (stage-host canvas
runtime.ts `SectionFailure`). `missing`: the states file isn't there,
cleared once it is written. `compile`: a module the stage couldn't
compile, cleared once it compiles again. `page`: its module didn't load
in the page (an import that names an export its module lacks, a throw as
it ran), as the page posted it ({@link PostedReport} `unloaded`), cleared
once a page loads it or its section module is served again.

lastDeliveryAt.description: When it last delivered an event to its routine; null when it never has.

mode.description: The mode its event starts the project's conversation in when it has none; null: its routine's.

ExternalActor.description: Who wrote or opened something on a source.

avatarUrl.description: Their picture on the source; null when it gave none.

login.description: `bewinxed` on GitHub; a Linear user's name. A comment's heading names them by it.

memberId.description: The fleet member they are, once a login → member map exists (tsk-138); null until then.

name.description: Their display name, when the source gives one apart from the login.

url.description: Their page on the source; null when it gave none.

ExternalComment.description: A comment written on an outside source and carried onto a task.

at.description: When it was written on the source, ms epoch.

direction.description: `in`: written on the source, added to the task; `out`: written on the task, posted to the source.

editedAt.description: The source's last edit of it, ms epoch; null when never edited.

externalId.description: The source's own id for it: GitHub's comment number, Linear's uuid.

url.description: Where it reads on the source: the item's URL with the comment's anchor.

ExternalRef.description: One external item a task links, as the board draws it.

id.description: The source's own id: GitHub's node id, Linear's uuid; empty until the item was read.

problem.description: Why the last read of it stopped short, in the source's words; null when it went through.

state.description: Its state as the source last said it; null until the item was read.

stateName.description: The source's own word: "Open", "Closed", "In Progress"; empty until read.

syncedAt.description: When the hub last read it from the source, ms epoch; null before it first did.

title.description: Empty until the item was read.

updatedAt.description: When the source last changed it, ms epoch; null before it was read.

ref.description: The hub's reference to its bytes: `/api/files/<sha256>`.

leftOut.description: Each online machine whose last listing of its stored sessions left a harness out.

next.description: The cursor for the next page; null on the last.

query.description: The words as the hub read them, after any kind words.

timing.description: What the hub took to answer, ms: names and transcripts apart.

artifactKind.description: Which kind of artifact: a preview, an HTML page, a canvas, a sheet.

handle.description:
What a mention of it carries, which the hub resolves to exactly it:
`<dir>#<id8>` for a conversation, the hostname for a machine, `tsk-142` for a task, the id for anything else.
Null for what nothing can name (a conversation the hub never started).

id.description: The object's own id: an instance id, `project:tsk-142`, a sha, a path.

lastActivity.description: When it last moved, ms epoch; null when nothing says.

matched.description: Which recognisers matched; empty for a kind word alone.

picksToMake.description: A decision with no pick of yours yet.

project.description: Its project, when it has one.

score.description: Its rank among this answer's results; higher first.

secrets.description: The secrets its own words hold; absent when none, or while secrets are not hidden.

seen.description: Whether you have opened it at its current revision.

title.description: What it is called, in its own words (a title, a name, a hostname).

FindChange.description: A commit a delegate's work item made, or a file it changed.

handle.description:
What a mention of it carries, which the hub resolves to exactly it:
`<dir>#<id8>` for a conversation, the hostname for a machine, `tsk-142` for a task, the id for anything else.
Null for what nothing can name (a conversation the hub never started).

id.description: The object's own id: an instance id, `project:tsk-142`, a sha, a path.

landed.description: Its work item has landed on the branch it lands on.

lastActivity.description: When it last moved, ms epoch; null when nothing says.

matched.description: Which recognisers matched; empty for a kind word alone.

project.description: Its project, when it has one.

score.description: Its rank among this answer's results; higher first.

secrets.description: The secrets its own words hold; absent when none, or while secrets are not hidden.

title.description: What it is called, in its own words (a title, a name, a hostname).

what.description: A commit's subject; a file's path.

cwd.description:

FleetAgent.description:

a page of markdown, and an editor that has to fetch it again is a round trip

FleetFetchFrame.description:
Hub-originated: a download at the hub began (`fetching`) or landed. A fetch
runs after the request that asked for it has answered, so this is how
every dashboard learns what came of it. Exactly one of the four is set:
- `skill`, `plugin`: a fetch of a fleet row's files, the row whole as
  `/api/fleet` reads it (files, or the sentence it failed with);
- `marketplace`: a read of a marketplace source (its name and offers);
- `link`: a link of a marketplace source, linked or refused.

check.description:
The check of every skill's and plugin's source for what it holds now:
under way, or done (each row it read came as its own frame).

link.description:
A link of the marketplace at `source`, asked for: under way (`fetching`),
linked (`marketplace`, the row), or refused (`error`).

marketplace.description:
A marketplace source as the hub read it: what its `marketplace.json` calls
it and what it offers, or why it could not be read. The hub reads it after
the request that asked has answered (`fetching`), and the read that lands
is a `fleet.fetch` frame.

plugin.description:
One installed plugin. `id` is the CLI's own `plugin@marketplace` form.

`hash`, `bytes` and `error` are what the HUB resolved this row to, and they
ride the dashboard's read only — the copy a machine is sent carries the
files themselves ({@link FleetPluginPayload}) and has no use for the
bookkeeping. `error` is a hub-side failure and a different fact from a
machine's `failed` in {@link FleetSyncReport.plugins}: one says the bytes
were never fetched, the other says a machine would not take them.

removed.description:
The row was removed while it was fetched; its `error` says so. With
`link`: a refused link was let go, and leaves the list.

skill.description:
A skill row as the hub stores and the dashboard reads it: where it came
from and what the hub resolved it to. The files themselves stay out of
this shape — a catalog read should not weigh megabytes.

`source` forms the hub's resolver accepts. Installer CLIs are deliberately
never run: an installer is a wrapper around "copy files into
`~/.claude/skills/<name>`", and cawco does the copy itself.
- `skills:owner/repo[@skill][#ref]` — a skills.sh-style slug (what the
  user would have typed after `bunx skills add`). The repo tarball is
  walked in the CLI's own discovery order, except `.claude/skills/` wins
  over `.agents/skills/` — cawco wants the Claude-tuned variant.
- `github:owner/repo[/path][@ref]` — the repo tarball, `path` pointing at
  the skill directory.
- `npm:package[@version]` — the registry tarball, for the few packages
  that embed `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (most installer packages carry no
  content — their CLIs fetch from GitHub at runtime).
- a plain URL to a `SKILL.md` (single-file skill).

FleetHarnessConfig.description:
One row. A `claudeSettings` row carries `settings`, merged into its
sessions' flag settings under CawCo's own. An `opencodePlugins` or
`piExtensions` row carries one of `module` (the module's source, written
into a file of CawCo's on each machine) or `package` (an npm package,
`<name>@<version>`, installed by each machine's sync).

areaId.description:
The hub `areas` row this is bound to, in place of one project: every
project in that area as the hub reads it (core areas.ts). A machine is
sent it under each such project it holds, as that project's own row
(hub project-placements.ts); a project's own row of the same key wins.
One of `projectId` and `areaId` is required unless `user`, never both.

cwd.description:
The folder this copy is written into: set by the machine as it places a
project's row at one of the project's places there (agent
fleet-place.ts), never by the hub, which sends each row once.

enabled.description: A disabled row stays at the hub and is placed nowhere.

module.description: An OpenCode plugin's or pi extension's source, as one ES module.

name.description: Unique within its kind: the key its writes take.

package.description: An OpenCode plugin's or pi extension's npm package: `<name>@<version>`, an `npm:` prefix allowed.

placeId.description:
The place this copy is for ({@link placeKeyOf} of its folder), on a
copy the machine placed: its converge keys what the copy came to under
`<key>@<placeId>`, and its report says it per place
({@link FleetSyncReport.placed}).

projectId.description: The hub `projects` row this is bound to. One of it and `areaId` is required unless `user`.

scope.description:
Where a fleet row applies, in Claude Code's own vocabulary:

- `user` — every machine, every project. The default, and what most rows
  want.
- `local`, `project` — one project ({@link FleetPlacement.projectId}),
  or every project in one area ({@link FleetPlacement.areaId}):
  the hub sends the row once to a machine that holds the project
  ({@link MachineFleetConfig.projects}), the machine places a copy at each
  checkout and workspace clone of it there, and each session in that
  folder takes it. An MCP server, a hook, Claude Code
  settings, an OpenCode plugin and a pi extension reach the folder's
  sessions through CawCo's own files and their launch (agent
  fleet-mcp-set.ts, fleet-harness-set.ts), never a file in the checkout.
  A skill is placed in `<cwd>/.claude/skills/` under either scope, kept
  out of the checkout's status.

settings.description: Claude Code settings, as its settings files hold them.

(`updated`), held what the fleet already has (`unchanged`), or could not be
fetched (`failed`, the machines keeping the copy they had). The versions
are the ones each copy declares, when it declares one; the hashes are the
copies' content hashes.

at.description: When it landed, epoch ms.

FleetReportFrame.description:
Machine-originated: the machine's fleet report (what `fleetStatus`
answers), sent unasked when a harness's reading of a fleet MCP server moved
with no fleet change: a server OpenCode held failed connected when CawCo
started it again. The hub keeps it as `agents.fleet`, as it keeps a sync's.

convergedGeneration.description: The generation whose converge has ended on the machine (core `FleetAck`).

generation.description:
The generation of the fleet's desired state the converge that wrote it
reached: the fleet MCP changes the deltas up to it carried are the
sessions' to take now. Null for a report read again unasked, which
landed no delta.

FleetScope.description:
Where a fleet row applies, in Claude Code's own vocabulary:

- `user` — every machine, every project. The default, and what most rows
  want.
- `local`, `project` — one project ({@link FleetPlacement.projectId}),
  or every project in one area ({@link FleetPlacement.areaId}):
  the hub sends the row once to a machine that holds the project
  ({@link MachineFleetConfig.projects}), the machine places a copy at each
  checkout and workspace clone of it there, and each session in that
  folder takes it. An MCP server, a hook, Claude Code
  settings, an OpenCode plugin and a pi extension reach the folder's
  sessions through CawCo's own files and their launch (agent
  fleet-mcp-set.ts, fleet-harness-set.ts), never a file in the checkout.
  A skill is placed in `<cwd>/.claude/skills/` under either scope, kept
  out of the checkout's status.

FleetSkillMeta.description:
A skill row as the hub stores and the dashboard reads it: where it came
from and what the hub resolved it to. The files themselves stay out of
this shape — a catalog read should not weigh megabytes.

`source` forms the hub's resolver accepts. Installer CLIs are deliberately
never run: an installer is a wrapper around "copy files into
`~/.claude/skills/<name>`", and cawco does the copy itself.
- `skills:owner/repo[@skill][#ref]` — a skills.sh-style slug (what the
  user would have typed after `bunx skills add`). The repo tarball is
  walked in the CLI's own discovery order, except `.claude/skills/` wins
  over `.agents/skills/` — cawco wants the Claude-tuned variant.
- `github:owner/repo[/path][@ref]` — the repo tarball, `path` pointing at
  the skill directory.
- `npm:package[@version]` — the registry tarball, for the few packages
  that embed `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (most installer packages carry no
  content — their CLIs fetch from GitHub at runtime).
- a plain URL to a `SKILL.md` (single-file skill).

areaId.description:
The hub `areas` row this is bound to, in place of one project: every
project in that area as the hub reads it (core areas.ts). A machine is
sent it under each such project it holds, as that project's own row
(hub project-placements.ts); a project's own row of the same key wins.
One of `projectId` and `areaId` is required unless `user`, never both.

bytes.description: Decoded size of the resolved files, for the dashboard to show.

checkError.description: Why the last read of the source for what it holds failed.

checkedAt.description: When the source was last read for what it holds, epoch ms.

choices.description:
When the last fetch found several skills in a source that named none:
the ones it could have meant, to pick from with `@<name>`.

cwd.description:
The folder this copy is written into: set by the machine as it places a
project's row at one of the project's places there (agent
fleet-place.ts), never by the hub, which sends each row once.

error.description: Why the last resolve failed, when it did.

fetching.description:
The hub is fetching it now. `hash`, `bytes` and `error` are the last
fetch's until this one lands, which a `fleet.fetch` frame announces.

hash.description: Content hash of the resolved files; absent until a resolve succeeds.

lastRefresh.description: What the last fetch of a row that had files came to.

latestHash.description: The content hash the source held when last read.

latestVersion.description: The version the source's copy declared when last read.

placeId.description:
The place this copy is for ({@link placeKeyOf} of its folder), on a
copy the machine placed: its converge keys what the copy came to under
`<key>@<placeId>`, and its report says it per place
({@link FleetSyncReport.placed}).

projectId.description: The hub `projects` row this is bound to. One of it and `areaId` is required unless `user`.

scope.description:
Where a fleet row applies, in Claude Code's own vocabulary:

- `user` — every machine, every project. The default, and what most rows
  want.
- `local`, `project` — one project ({@link FleetPlacement.projectId}),
  or every project in one area ({@link FleetPlacement.areaId}):
  the hub sends the row once to a machine that holds the project
  ({@link MachineFleetConfig.projects}), the machine places a copy at each
  checkout and workspace clone of it there, and each session in that
  folder takes it. An MCP server, a hook, Claude Code
  settings, an OpenCode plugin and a pi extension reach the folder's
  sessions through CawCo's own files and their launch (agent
  fleet-mcp-set.ts, fleet-harness-set.ts), never a file in the checkout.
  A skill is placed in `<cwd>/.claude/skills/` under either scope, kept
  out of the checkout's status.

updateAvailable.description: The source holds other content than the fleet's copy.

version.description:
The version the fleet's copy declares: a skill's SKILL.md front matter
`version`, a plugin's `plugin.json` `version` (else its marketplace
entry's).

FleetSyncReport.description:
A machine's answer to `syncFleetConfig`, and what `agents.fleet` stores:
every desired entry, by the same keys the config used.

at.description: When the sync ran, ms epoch.

harnessConfig.description:
The fleet's Claude Code settings, OpenCode plugins and pi extensions,
by `<kind>:<name>`: what the sync wrote or installed for each, as
sessions take it at their launch. A project's are in {@link placed}.

have.description:
What this machine holds on its disk once the sync is done, by hash — the
content-carrying rows only, hashed as the hub hashes them. It tells the
hub whose content moved, so running sessions reload.

hooks.description:
The fleet's hooks, by the same id the hub keeps them under (a project's
are in {@link placed}). Claude Code's report says what its sync
registered; OpenCode's and pi's whether CawCo runs the hook there at all,
`unsupported` with why for an event or handler that harness has no point
for (core `hookUnsupported`). A machine's merged report holds each hook's
worst, every harness's word in its `detail`. `failed` covers three
different machine-local facts — a hand-edited script, a validation the
hub already passed but this row failed again, or a project hook with no
checkout here — and `detail` is what tells them apart.

mcpByHarness.description: Per-harness runtime truth, before the machine row's worst-state aggregation.

memory.description:
The user-scope memory (CLAUDE.md). Absent when neither the fleet nor this
machine's record has one; `failed` is how a machine says its own copy was
edited and was not overwritten.

detail.description: What the write or the CLI said — the tail of it.

memoryDocs.description:
The linked documents, by the same path the set keyed them under. Absent
from a harness's own report when it converges none; one drifted document
says so on its own row, with the main file still `applied` beside it.

memoryHook.description:
Never sent. The retired model-memory hook's row, kept in the wire schema
only while an installable TestFlight build reads it (hub scripts
wire-compat.ts); it goes with the last of them (20261018).

detail.description: What the write or the CLI said — the tail of it.

placed.description:
Each project row's state at each of its places on the machine
({@link FleetPlacedStates}): its checkouts and its workspaces' clones,
which only the machine knows. The hub keeps one state per row, the
worst of its places, naming the place.

skills.description: Absent from a harness's own report when it converges none.

toolchain.description:
The CLIs this sync leaned on, so a failure can be attributed to a binary
rather than to the machine as a whole. Absent from a machine that found
nothing to report.

FleetToolchain.description: The CLIs a machine's sync leaned on, by the name they are known under.

claude.description: Every `claude` this machine has; the one the sync ran is marked `used`.

FleetWatchNotice.description:
A needs-you notice from fleet watch: a triage told you, or a session in a
project whose Caw is off showed two signals (no model is woken there).
Kept by the hub until you act on the session or it moves on.

at.description: ms epoch the hub raised it.

body.description: Why, in a sentence or two: the triage's words, or the signals.

title.description: The line: its signals, joined with " · ".

FleetWatchNoticesFrame.description: Hub-originated: every open fleet-watch notice, whole, on each change.

FleetWatchSettings.description: Fleet watch's settings and facts, as Settings reads them.

jev.description: Jev answers fleet watch's question: it has a route (a TypeSafe key, or OpenRouter).

quietTurns.description: Finished turns in a row that changed no file.

sameCall.description: The same tool call (name and normalised input) this many times in a row.

sameError.description: The same tool error, normalised, this many times in the session's recent turns.

stallMinutes.description: Minutes a running turn streams nothing while its process lives.

path.description: From the folder's root, `/` between parts.
The file, or `""` for the whole folder.
The folder listed, from the root; `""` is the root.

truncated.description: True when the listing stopped at its cap before the last entry.

FolderWeight.description: What a folder preview loads at most: its files, their bytes, and of those its JavaScript's and its WebAssembly's; and its start page's desk captures (core `deskCaptures`).

captures.description: `` on the start page whose file is wider than `DESK_CAPTURE_WIDTH`.

ForgottenBrings.description: What bringing a forgotten project back brings, counted.

account.description: The account its sessions start on, by id; null: the fleet's routing, or none kept.

browsers.description: Its browsers, each stopped with its profile (its sign-ins) kept on its machine.

folder.description: Its folder on the hub, history and all: its task files, stages, pages' sources, memory and design.

memoryDocs.description: Memory documents scoped to it alone.

places.description: Its places: its folder on the hub and its checkouts.

rows.description: Every row it brings, of any table.

sessions.description: Sessions started from it, counted its own again.

settings.description:
Its row and settings as they were. False for a project forgotten before
the hub kept them: its folder alone comes back, under a new row that
takes the name the restore gives it.

tasksIn.description:
A live project some of its tasks already live in, under that project's
numbers: a folder from before the hub kept records that may have been a
duplicate folded into it (hub project-merge.ts) but can't be told for
sure. Null for every other.

ForgottenFolderHints.description:
What a folder forgotten before the hub kept records says about the
project, read off its files: the hub kept nothing else of it. Its task
count is {@link ForgottenBrings.tasks}.

changedAt.description: When a file in it last changed, ms since the epoch; null when it holds none outside git's own.

heading.description: The first heading of its AGENTS.md, but the stub's own `AGENTS.md`; null when it has none.

newestTask.description: Its newest task, open or archived, by number; null when it has none.

stages.description: Its stages as its stages.md names them; none when it has no stages.md or it does not read.

ForgottenPlace.description:
A place of a forgotten project on disk that deleting it with its files
(`POST /api/projects/:id/delete`, `fromDisk`) removes: a checkout on a
machine, or its folder in the hub's trash.

kind.description: `checkout`: a folder on a machine; `hub`: its folder in the hub's trash.

machineId.description: The machine's id; `hub` for the hub's own trash.

machineName.description: The machine's name as the hub holds it now; its id when the hub holds none.

within.description: The live projects whose checkout holds this folder: they lose these files too (place-nesting.ts). Empty for the hub's own.

by.description: The presence id of the client that forgot it; null when none said, or before the hub kept it.

forgottenAt.description: When it was forgotten, ms since the epoch.

hints.description:
What its folder says about it, for one forgotten before the hub kept
records (`name` null); null for every other.

name.description: Null: forgotten before the hub kept its name; a restore names it.

places.description:
Every place deleting it with its files removes, as the delete itself
reads them (hub project-trash.ts `diskPlaces`): its folders in the
hub's trash, then its checkouts on machines still in the fleet.

Form.description: A story's form: a preset's name and width, or a width of its own (`custom`).

FramePayload.description:
`frames`: everything a session produces, flowing agent→hub→dashboard. The
`frame` kind is a neutral message; `raw` on it carries the harness's own
event verbatim.

FrameState.description:
What a browser drew of one frame: `unseen` until one drew it since its
file last changed; `unshown` when the page did not show it at its width (a
phone's canvas shows one frame at a time), so it is neither drawn nor
empty: `empty` is a frame shown that drew nothing.

FramesAlike.description: Rest frames of one states file that draw the same picture at one width and scheme: {@link framesAlike}.

FsEntry.description: One dirent of an `fs list`. `size` is 0 for a directory.

FsMedia.description: What an `fs media` read answers with: the file's bytes, base64, and what they are (a picture or a video).

FsPayload.description:
`fs`: the machine's files, for the cwd picker and light markdown editing
(NEW.md §6) — not a file transfer. `list` answers with {@link FsEntry}[],
`read` with the file's text, `write` with the byte count it wrote, `media`
with an {@link FsMedia} — the one binary the tunnel carries, so a picture or
video an agent pointed at can be looked at without the agent spending tokens
on it.

content.description: `write` only: the text the file is replaced with.

path.description: Absolute; or, with `root`, relative to that root on the machine.

root.description:
`claude-home`: `path` is under the machine's user layer, Claude Code's
own dir (`~/.claude`), as the machine itself places it (core paths/claude.ts
`claudeHome`): no caller has to know a machine's home to reach it.

asked.description:
The `output_path` asked for, when the image was saved beside it under
its format's extension instead ({@link IMAGE_EXTENSIONS}).

model.description: The provider's model that made it.

notes.description: What the provider said of the run that the caller should know, in words.

GhSignIn.description: A machine's gh account the hub can make a connection from: Sign in to GitHub lists each.

machine.description: The machine as a sentence names it.

GitHubCursor.description: Where one GitHub resource's poll stands: its ETag, its high-water mark, and its counts.

since.description: The newest `updated_at` taken in, ms: events at or after it are looked for.

GithubProject.description:
A GitHub Project (v2) a GitHub binding carries its stages on, through the
Project's single-select field named Status (PRD §5.2: "With GitHub, stages
map onto a Projects single-select field"). Issues' open and closed carry
only open against done or dropped; Status carries every stage.

fieldId.description: Its Status field's node id; null when the Project has no single-select Status.

id.description: GitHub's node id for the Project.

map.description: Each stage's Status option by the stage's name, as set in the binding's form; null leaves Status alone for that stage. A stage missing here takes the option named as it.

options.description: Its Status field's options, in GitHub's order.

GithubProjectChoice.description: A GitHub Project a connection reaches, offered in the binding's form.

linked.description: Linked to the bound repository on GitHub: the form's first pick.

GithubProjectsView.description: What a GitHub connection reaches of a repository owner's Projects: its Projects, or GitHub's refusal in its words.

refused.description: GitHub's words when the connection may not read the owner's Projects; null when it may.

HarnessCapabilities.description: What a harness can do, so the dashboard gates features instead of guessing.

effort.description: The reasoning-effort scale, at spawn and mid-session.

fleet.description: The harness applies the hub's fleet config (MCP/skills/memory/agents) to its own files.

fork.description: Fork a stored session into a new one.

tagSession.description: The scratch-tag the catalog filter reads.

HarnessFailed.description: A harness whose `listSessions` refused (threw): left out of the listing with its error, not read as having none.

HarnessKind.description: The harnesses cawco can spawn sessions on. Adding one is a new adapter.

HarnessNote.description:
A notice the harness put in the user's role, as its agent's normaliser
read it (agent claude-transcript.ts `harnessNoteOf`): Claude Code's
`<task-notification>` block (`task-notification`) and its `[SYSTEM
NOTIFICATION …]` line, and a whole `<system-reminder>` block
(`system-reminder`). `title` is what a fold says closed, `status` the
task's (`completed`, `failed`, `stopped`; empty when it said none), `body`
the rest, as markdown. Never the reader's words.

toolUseId.description: A task notification's Task call, when it names one.

HarnessOffer.description: A harness on the fleet, as the page draws setup from it.

machines.description: The online machines it runs on, by name.

HarnessReport.description: What a machine knows about one harness: is it installed, can it work, what can it do.

accounts.description:
Claude only: every account's config dir on the machine
(`~/.cawco/accounts/<id>/claude`) and what `claude auth status` said of
it there. The hub reads it as where each account is signed in. The
machine's own `~/.claude` is never read.

authReason.description:
Why a session of this harness cannot start here, without credential
data: pi's sign-in unavailable or unchecked, or OpenCode's server
refusing to start (and not tried again until its inputs change). The
home says it as this machine's word.

modelNames.description:
pi only: the model each bare model id pi offers resolves to, by pi's own
resolver (`resolveCliModel`) with this machine's accounts counted as
signed in, as `provider/id`. A name pi cannot resolve is absent. The hub
reads the provider, and so the account, of a session started on one of
them here. `default` depends on the session's directory and is asked
per start ({@link CONTROL_PI_DEFAULT_MODEL}).

models.description:
The models this harness offers on this machine.

It rides the machine's report for the same reason {@link * HarnessCapabilities.permissionModes} does, and not the {@link * CONTROL_SUPPORTED_MODELS} control beside it: the catalog is a property of
the installed CLI and the account behind it, identical for every session on
the machine and knowable with none running. Asking a session for it made a
fleet-wide fact inherit one session's lifecycle — a machine with nothing
running had no catalog at all, so its model picker was empty and no session
could be named or shown an effort scale.

Absent (not empty) from a harness whose catalog could not be read, which
then says why ({@link modelsUnread}), and from Claude, whose catalog is
each account's (the hub's account catalogs); empty means it was asked and
offered nothing.

modelsUnread.description:
Why this harness's catalog could not be read on this read, in the
machine's words: OpenCode's server would not start or answer, pi's
registry failed. Set exactly when an installed harness that reports its
catalog has no {@link models}; a picker says it instead of an empty list.

refused.description:
Why the machine refuses every start of this harness's CLI, its sentence
in {@link authReason}: `not-installed`, or `version` (not a version the
harness's catalog entry runs: below Claude Code's or pi's floor, not
OpenCode's one version, or no version said). Claude's gate is agent
claude-version.ts `claudeToStart`; OpenCode's and pi's tools.ts
`toolGate`. Absent when it runs. Where the dashboard puts the refusal in
place of what it blocks, with the catalog's install of the harness's
tool ({@link HARNESS_TOOL}) as its one press (`HarnessBlock`).

signInFaults.description:
OpenCode only: each of the machine's own OpenCode sign-ins (not a CawCo
account) whose provider refused it the last time a session here used
it, until a turn on that provider succeeds. The home says each on the
machine's row, with the fix ({@link opencodeSignInFaultWords}).

unreadAccounts.description:
Claude only: the account dirs (`~/.cawco/accounts/<id>/claude`) Claude
Code gave no answer for on this read: its `auth status` ran out of time
or printed nothing it could mean. Neither signed in nor out: the hub
keeps what it last had for each, and does not read them as gone.

version.description: The CLI/SDK version, when it can be read.

HarnessUnanswered.description: A harness whose `listSessions` did not answer within its bound: left out of the listing, not read as having none.

HeldAccount.description: Another account and why it didn't take a held session, or that it could ({@link HeldReason}).

backAt.description: When it takes sessions again, epoch ms, when a reading says (benched, at its limit, past its reserve).

HeldReason.description:
Why another account didn't take a session held at its limit, or, for one
that could, that it could (`fits`). In order of the hub's rules: not signed
in on its machine, not one its project or task allows, benched, past its
reserve, its limits never read, at its own limit, kept out of the pinned
strategy's backups, a move already landing there while its window isn't
measured in dollars (`alone`), too little left for this move (`room`:
what it has left and what the move takes, percent of its window), or
running out within the wait the policy allows with it (`runsOut`).

HeldSendFrame.description:
Daemon-originated: a send the machine was handed and no process took: it
found no live process for its session, or the process it was handed to went
away (slept, exited, failed, relaunched, refused by the session keeper)
before reading it. Whole, as it was sent, under the hand-off it was given
(`SendPayload.delivery`); the hub owes it to the session's next process.

HeldWork.description:
What a held workspace holds that is nowhere else, as its machine read it
once its boundary was closed (schema.ts `workspaces.holding`), and where
it is.

excluded.description:
The untracked paths git ignores through no `.gitignore` the repository
tracks: by a line of the clone's `.git/info/exclude`, or a `.gitignore`
that is itself untracked, each as `git status --ignored=matching` names
it, relative to the clone (a folder ends in `/`). The paths `skip`
names, and what CawCo writes into a clone and lists there itself (its
deny paths' stand-ins, the placed skills and memory, its stage), are not
among them. On 2026-10-17 a delegate kept a design page's source out of
its landing this way, and retirement deleted it. Absent when none.

heldAt.description: When its machine read it, ISO.

holds.description: What it holds, in words: "2 commits on no remote, 3 changed files, 1 stash".

refused.description:
Set when CawCo does not run git in the clone, so nothing of it was read
and `ahead`, `dirty` and `stashes` are 0: why, as agent workspace.ts
`gitRefusal` says it (its `.git` no folder of its own, or a key its own
config sets past core safe-git.ts's allowlist). Only the person, or a
session continuing it, can change that, so the workspace is held until
one does, not tried again each sweep: on 2026-10-25 a clone whose config
held git-lfs's `lfs.<url>.access` was archived and refused every minute.

size.description: The clone's size on disk, in words.

strays.description:
Set when the clone's folder is there and its `.git` is no repository
git can read: how many entries down its tree are not CawCo's (agent
stand-ins.ts `straysIn`, which names each by its path relative to the
folder). CawCo's are a deny path's stand-in exactly as made, a mount
point a sandbox left on a deny path, a `.git/config` holding only
git-lfs's `[lfs] repositoryformatversion = 0` marker, a project skill
exactly as CawCo placed it (agent fleet.ts `placedAsMade`), and a
dir (`.git`, `.claude`) holding only those. None is a husk, a deleted
clone a sandbox refilled, which holds nothing; any keeps the folder.

HomeCredential.description: One credential in a harness's own store a CawCo account can hold.

provider.description: The account provider it is for.

storeProvider.description: The provider's id in that store, as the store names it (`openai` in OpenCode's for ChatGPT).

HomeLogin.description: Who a machine's own `~/.claude` is signed in as, by its `claude auth status`.

identity.description:
Who an account is: an email in an organization, the organization known by
its id (`orgId`), never its name, which is a display name: an org renamed
is the same org, and two orgs can share a name. Claude: as `claude auth
status --json` reports it (`email`, `orgName`, `orgId`). ChatGPT: the
access token's claims, read on the machine — the email
(`https://api.openai.com/profile`.email) and, as `organization` and its
id, the ChatGPT account id (`https://api.openai.com/auth`.chatgpt_account_id),
the workspace the subscription bills. Another OAuth provider: the email its
credential names, if any, and its provider id. A key: its last four
characters (`…a1b2`) and, as `organization` and its id, a fingerprint of
it (`key:` and the first 16 hex of its SHA-256), so the same key on two
machines is one account and the key itself never leaves them.

kind.description:
How the account signs in. Claude: a subscription (`claude auth login`) or a
Console organization (`claude auth login --console`). Any other provider:
its own OAuth sign-in through pi-ai (`oauth`), or a key (`api_key`).

HomeStore.description: Where a credential moved into an account came from: a harness's own store on the machine.

agent.description: Which subagent runs it. Absent inherits Claude Code's default.

if.description:
A single permission rule narrowing when this runs, like `Bash(git *)`.
Only consulted on tool events; on any other event a handler carrying one
never runs at all, which is why {@link hookProblem} refuses the pairing
rather than letting it be saved as a hook that silently does nothing.

timeout.description: Seconds before it is cancelled. Claude Code's defaults apply when unset.

command.description:
Absent when the hook carries a {@link FleetHook.script} — the daemon fills
it in with the path it wrote, because that path is machine-local and the
fleet row must not contain one machine's home directory.

if.description:
A single permission rule narrowing when this runs, like `Bash(git *)`.
Only consulted on tool events; on any other event a handler carrying one
never runs at all, which is why {@link hookProblem} refuses the pairing
rather than letting it be saved as a hook that silently does nothing.

timeout.description: Seconds before it is cancelled. Claude Code's defaults apply when unset.

HookDraft.description: A hook as the editor holds it, before the hub assigns identity and hash.

areaId.description:
The hub `areas` row this is bound to, in place of one project: every
project in that area as the hub reads it (core areas.ts). A machine is
sent it under each such project it holds, as that project's own row
(hub project-placements.ts); a project's own row of the same key wins.
One of `projectId` and `areaId` is required unless `user`, never both.

cwd.description:
The folder this copy is written into: set by the machine as it places a
project's row at one of the project's places there (agent
fleet-place.ts), never by the hub, which sends each row once.

enabled.description:
A disabled hook is simply not written to any machine. Claude Code itself
has no way to disable one hook while keeping it, so this is cawco's
to provide: the row stays, the registration goes.

force.description: Set on a targeted push only: overwrite a machine copy that drifted.

name.description: What the reader calls it. Unique across the fleet.

placeId.description:
The place this copy is for ({@link placeKeyOf} of its folder), on a
copy the machine placed: its converge keys what the copy came to under
`<key>@<placeId>`, and its report says it per place
({@link FleetSyncReport.placed}).

projectId.description: The hub `projects` row this is bound to. One of it and `areaId` is required unless `user`.

scope.description:
Where a fleet row applies, in Claude Code's own vocabulary:

- `user` — every machine, every project. The default, and what most rows
  want.
- `local`, `project` — one project ({@link FleetPlacement.projectId}),
  or every project in one area ({@link FleetPlacement.areaId}):
  the hub sends the row once to a machine that holds the project
  ({@link MachineFleetConfig.projects}), the machine places a copy at each
  checkout and workspace clone of it there, and each session in that
  folder takes it. An MCP server, a hook, Claude Code
  settings, an OpenCode plugin and a pi extension reach the folder's
  sessions through CawCo's own files and their launch (agent
  fleet-mcp-set.ts, fleet-harness-set.ts), never a file in the checkout.
  A skill is placed in `<cwd>/.claude/skills/` under either scope, kept
  out of the checkout's status.

script.description:
A command hook's script body. CawCo writes it to a file on every machine
and points the registration at that path, so the hook travels — a machine
that has never seen this hook still runs it correctly. Absent means the
handler carries its own `command` and the reader is on their own for
getting that command onto each box.

HookEvent.description: Every lifecycle point a hook can attach to.

if.description:
A single permission rule narrowing when this runs, like `Bash(git *)`.
Only consulted on tool events; on any other event a handler carrying one
never runs at all, which is why {@link hookProblem} refuses the pairing
rather than letting it be saved as a hook that silently does nothing.

timeout.description: Seconds before it is cancelled. Claude Code's defaults apply when unset.

if.description:
A single permission rule narrowing when this runs, like `Bash(git *)`.
Only consulted on tool events; on any other event a handler carrying one
never runs at all, which is why {@link hookProblem} refuses the pairing
rather than letting it be saved as a hook that silently does nothing.

timeout.description: Seconds before it is cancelled. Claude Code's defaults apply when unset.

if.description:
A single permission rule narrowing when this runs, like `Bash(git *)`.
Only consulted on tool events; on any other event a handler carrying one
never runs at all, which is why {@link hookProblem} refuses the pairing
rather than letting it be saved as a hook that silently does nothing.

timeout.description: Seconds before it is cancelled. Claude Code's defaults apply when unset.

HookVersion.description:
One superseded version of one hook, as a listing reads it — without the
material. A hook is kept every time it is saved or deleted over one that
already existed, so this is a full edit history (`GET /api/fleet/hooks/history`).

createdAt.description: When it was kept, ISO, as the answer carries it.

source.description: `fleet` for the hub's own row; `machine:<machineId>` for an edited script a forced push took off that machine.

HubAuthFrame.description:
What every paired screen keeps current (`verb: "frames"` from the hub):
the mode, the pairings waiting on the person, and the machines waiting to
be admitted. Sent whenever any of them changes.

HubAuthMode.description: Which way the hub admits callers.

HubAuthState.description:
What `GET /api/auth` answers: the mode, what this request is, and, for a
paired device, which one. Any client reads it to know whether it must pair.

device.description: The paired device this request came from; null for anything else.

HubReach.description: The hub's own try of the origin's ping, now: answered by CawCo's listener, or why not.

HubRestartFrame.description:
Hub-originated: the hub is about to restart for an update, or no longer
is. Sent to every dashboard the moment its own machine says it is
installing (binary-update.ts `#tellHub`, before the helper restarts it),
to each that connects while it does, and with `restart: null` when the
install ends without restarting it. `withinMs` is relative, so no two
clocks are compared: the dashboard makes it a deadline on its own, and
reads the hub as on its way back, not unreachable, until it passes.

version.description: The build it restarts onto, when the machine named one.

withinMs.description: How long from now it answers again, or the build before it does: the update's trial (UPDATE_TRIAL_MS).

ImageSettings.description:
The fleet's image default (hub `image_settings`, `GET`/`PUT
/api/image-settings`): the provider a call that names none goes to, and
that provider's model (null: its default). No row reads as
{@link DEFAULT_IMAGE_SETTINGS}, which is today's behaviour.

InboundVia.description: How an inbound event reached the hub.

IngestMark.description:
The hub's word on how far it has ingested one instance: the last line it
turned into a frame. Handed back on the register ack so a reattaching agent
replays exactly the gap the hub names — the mark is the hub's own, so the
agent's death loses nothing it needs.

IngressView.description: What a project's ingress is: its GitHub poller, routes, connector polls and newest events.

repo.description:
Read by nothing here: {@link repos} as one line, for the shipped apps
that show it (TestFlight builds before 2026-11-03); it goes once none
is installable.

repos.description: The GitHub repositories it polls, `owner/repo`: every one the project links.

resources.description: Read by nothing: kept empty for the shipped apps that declare it; it goes with {@link repo}.

state.description: What is true of it, in a sentence: polled, or why not.

Install.description: One install, as the hub keeps it and every dashboard reads it.

address.description: The command route's hub address, as the line names it.

checks.description: The checks the installer has passed, and the one it failed.

command.description: The command route's one line, while its code works.

hostname.description: The name the fleet shows the machine by, once it is known.

keys.description:
The keys an SSH add wrote to the machine, which stay there whatever its
outcome (the installer's undo never touches them), kept over a Retry:
`hub`, the hub's SSH key a password sign-in put in its
`~/.ssh/authorized_keys`; `machine`, the key the hub gave it to prove
(`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cawco/machine-key`).

machineId.description: The machine it joined as, once known.

problemStep.description: The step it failed or stopped on.

returning.description: A machine already in the fleet this install brings back: its row grows into the install's.

tail.description: The output's last lines, for the window's well.

target.description: `user@host`, or a Host from the hub user's `~/.ssh/config`; empty for the command route.

InstallDraft.description: What the person filled in before anything started: kept by the hub, never a password.

code.description:
The command route's one-time code, minted by the hub as the route is
chosen so the line can be shown before it is copied; it works from the
moment Copy command starts its install. Never sent by a dashboard.

route.description: Null until a route is chosen (Route, the window's first step).

InstallMark.description: One step as it ran: when it started, and when it ended (null while it runs).

InstallSignIn.description: How an SSH install signs in: the hub's key, a password once, or a key the person put there.

InstallStarted.description: What `POST /api/installs` answers: the install, and whether it was one already running for that machine.

InstallState.description:
`running` while it goes; `failed`, `stopped` and `lost` stand until the
person acts on them; `joined` once the fleet lists the machine online, its
fleet sync is placed and its harness CLIs run.

InstallsFrame.description: The frame the hub sends every dashboard when an install or the draft changes.

rev.description:
The hub's count of changes to the installs and the draft, from the
clock at its start so a restarted hub's run past its last's: a read or
frame older than one already taken is passed over, whichever way each
travelled (the socket's frames, a request's answer).

InstallsRead.description: `GET /api/installs`, and the `installs` frame every change sends.

rev.description:
The hub's count of changes to the installs and the draft, from the
clock at its start so a restarted hub's run past its last's: a read or
frame older than one already taken is passed over, whichever way each
travelled (the socket's frames, a request's answer).

accountId.description:
The account the session runs on (`instances.account_id`): placed once as
it starts and kept for its whole life. Null on a harness without accounts
and on a session from before accounts existed.

chosenEffort.description:
The effort the operator chose for the session: its spawn's level, or the
last `setEffort` sent it. The hub starts every process of the session at
it, whatever brings it back; a reading never moves it. Null: nobody
chose, and the harness runs its model's default.

clean.description:
Started clean ({@link SpawnPayload.clean}): written by its first spawn
and kept, so every launch of it is clean and a comparison can tell it
from a session started with its context.

continuedInto.description:
The session a continuation moved this one's work item to: this one never
runs again ({@link relaunchOf} refuses it), and what is sent to it goes
there. Null on every other session.

createdAt.description: When the hub first opened its row: when it was started.

cwd.description: The directory the session was launched in; see `launchDir`.

damaged.description:
Its record, or its workspace's, is damaged on its machine
({@link DamagedRow}): laid over by the hub from the machine's last beat,
never stored. `lastError` says the same in words.

delegateType.description: The delegate type its spawn named; null: none.

delegateTypeProject.description: The project whose catalog that type came from; null: the fleet's.

derivedTitle.description:
The name the session's first user message gave it, derived once by the hub.
A listing already answers {@link title} with this when nothing named the
row, so a reader never watches the label change as the transcript arrives.

doneAt.description:
When the person pressed Done on it (an archive), on the hub's clock: off
the sidebar's Recent list until they write to it again. Null otherwise.

effort.description:
The effort the session actually sends, as its agent last read it back from
the harness ({@link import ("./harness").EFFORT_READ}): a level, `none` when
it sends no effort, null until the first reading lands. What its chip
shows; never what a launch of it asks for ({@link chosenEffort}).

harness.description: Which harness owns {@link sessionId} — what a resume and a catalog read route on.

held.description: First-hand custody on the current agent connection, never stored liveness.

kind.description: `mainline`, `scratch` for a spin-off, or `summariser`, never on the board.

lastError.description: What killed the session, on a row the agent reported as `error`: words a person reads.

lastErrorKind.description:
What `lastError` was, typed where it was found; null when no producer
typed it. What every decision about the row reads, `relaunchOf` first.

launchDir.description:
Whether `cwd` is the launch directory: `known`; `unread`, still to be read
from its machine; `unknown`, its machine has no record of its conversation,
so `cwd` may be a folder its CLI wandered into and the session is named by
its title (hub `sessionLabel`) and cannot be resumed.

mayStart.description:
The delegate types a session may start, by name. `["any"]` ({@link * ANY_TYPE}) is every type: the session orchestrates. Any other list, the
empty one included, makes it a leaf for every role rule (its toolset, its
memory, its budget): a leaf may start the types it names and nothing else,
and the hub refuses any other start before anything spawns.

origin.description:
Who started it ({@link SessionOrigin}), as the hub stamped it at its
start. A row the hub sends always has it.

owedMove.description:
The account a person moved it to that it moves to at its next launch,
as the hub keeps it (its `owed_moves`), until the move lands: what it
waits on, its turn's end, the background work its process holds ending,
or its machine connected again. Absent when it owes none.

parentInstanceId.description:
The session that started this one (`delegate`, `start_session`), which every rail nests it under; absent on a
session a person started. A delegate is told from a session merely
started by {@link workItemId}, never by where it stands.

parentToolUseId.description: The delegating tool call, so the parent transcript can render the round trip.

permissionMode.description:
How the session answers tool permissions and which model answers, as of its
last spawn, switch or `init`. Null on a session that has never said.

projectId.description:
Its one project, written by the hub as it started: the project it was
started in, its parent's for a delegate, Caw's work or a check, else
the project whose place holds its folder most closely. Null when none
does. The rails list a session under this project and no other.

queuedSends.description:
The sends waiting for it (accepted, not yet read by its session; a keep-
alive ping aside): one starts its next turn. Laid over by the hub from
its send records, never stored; absent at none. The sidebar counts a
session with one as still working.

role.description:
The toolset it runs in, when its spawn named one; null: derived from
how it started.

runningDelegates.description: Hub-derived count of live delegated work items, including descendants and checks.

seenAt.description:
When the owner last looked at it (its tab in front, after it ended) or
archived it off Finished, on any device, or the end of a turn that had
nothing for them when nothing before it was unseen. Null on one never
seen.

sessionId.description: The harness's own session id, once the session has named itself.

stalled.description:
The session is stopped at its account's limit (or on its refused
sign-in), in words, as the hub's at-limit controller holds it (hub
at-limit.ts `stall`): what happened and when it carries on; `until`,
epoch ms, the moment it does. Absent while it runs. Its row, its head and
its transcript show it as an error with the way out: another account
from its menu.

startingSet.description:
The skills and MCP servers it started with ({@link * SpawnPayload.startingSet}): written by its first spawn and kept, so every
launch of it starts with the same set. Null: everything installed.

title.description:
What the session is called: the owner's rename, else the name the session
gave itself (`set_title`) or was spawned under, else {@link derivedTitle}.

titleSource.description:
Who gave the session its name: `owner` (a dashboard rename, which the
session's own `set_title` cannot replace) or `agent`. Null while nobody has.

turnEndedAt.description:
When its latest turn ended, on the hub's clock, as `seenAt` is: the
two together say whether it ended since the owner last looked. Null on
one whose turn never ended.

wakesItself.description:
Its latest turn ended with work of its own that will start it again
(harness.ts `waitsOnItself`: a background command, a monitor, a wake-up
it set itself). The sidebar counts it as still working.

workItemId.description:
The work item this session runs: every delegate is one, and a session
never runs more than one. Null on a session nobody delegated, and on a
delegate from before work items existed.

workspaceId.description:
The workspace of its own its work item runs in (a delegate's clone), as
the board reads it off that item: what the session menu's Archive
workspace names (dashboard LiveSessionMenu). Null on a session with no
work item.

wroteAt.description:
When the person last wrote to it (a send of theirs the hub accepted,
harness.ts `byPerson`), on the hub's clock. Null when they never did.

InstanceStatus.description:
What a session row is doing, right now, as the hub last heard it.

- `starting` — a spawn went out and hasn't been confirmed live yet.
- `running` — the owning daemon currently lists the instance.
- `sleeping` — no live process, but it runs again: on the session id its
  harness picks back up from, or fresh under its id when it never named
  one ({@link relaunchOf}). `sleeping` rows carry `lastError: null` — nothing
  went wrong, there's just nothing running.
- `stopping` — an end (stop, discard, or a delete that waits on its
  process) is recorded and owed to its machine, which has not yet
  confirmed the process is gone. It may still be running. Its machine's
  confirmation files it `stopped` (or `discarded`); an away machine leaves
  it here until it is back and confirms. For everything that asks whether
  the person ended it (filters, the Finished list, wake and resume
  gating), it is ended; for everything that asks whether a process
  remains, it is not gone yet.
- `stopped` — deliberate: the operator (or a `stop` call) ended it, and its
  machine confirmed the process gone.
- `error` — an actual failure. `lastError` is required here, and this is
  where {@link RESTART_LOST} still lands (`lastErrorKind` `restart-lost`): a
  restart with nothing to resume from is a real loss, not a nap.
- `unknown` — the machine that owns this row can't currently be reached, so
  the hub can't say which of the above is true.
- `discarded` — a spin-off torn down on purpose; gone for good.
- `moving` — its project is moving to its machine for it (move.ts): the hub
  holds the row from the move's start, under the id the session starts
  under, and the move's start takes it on to `starting`. No process, and
  none is claimed: a failed move files it `error`, a cancelled one drops it.

agents.description: Changed machines only; omitted when no machine moved.

formerIds.description: Present when it moved: every former id, by its id now ({@link InstancesFrame.formerIds}), whole.

kind.description: Hub-originated: only changed rows and metadata; pulses travel separately.

noticesDamaged.description: Present when it moved: the damaged notices record, or null once it is reset.

previewSettings.description: Present when it moved: the fleet's preview mode ({@link InstancesFrame.previewSettings}).

formerIds.description:
The ids sessions had before the hub folded each one's continuations
into it (a continuation anything but the person's own Continue asked
for, and those of hubs before migration 0128): former id → its id now. A
tab or link that names a former id is that session.

hubRun.description:
This hub's run, one value per hub start: the numbering every stream on
this socket counts in. A newest transcript page names the run its `seq`
came from (`TranscriptPage.hubRun`); a page of this run resumes its
stream here from that `seq`, and one of another run is read again.

kind.description: Hub-originated: the complete board on every connection, including reconnects.

moves.description: Every project move the hub is carrying; each change after this arrives on the `moves` frame.

noticesDamaged.description:
The hub's notices record, when it found it damaged at start: notices
are off and `noticesSeen` is not a record of anything until it is reset
(hub notices.ts). Null when the record reads whole.

noticesSeen.description: The notice ids a person acknowledged, on any tab or device (hub notices.ts).

previewSettings.description:
The fleet's preview mode (Settings › Previews): a switch moves every
preview origin, so a decision page loaded before it loads again, its
embeds at their new origins.

Interaction.description: The states the canvas derives from a component's CSS, never authored: `rest` is the story as mounted.

IssueTracker.description: A tracker that is an outside service.

JoinAddress.description: One address a machine could reach this hub on.

label.description: Where it came from: `Tailscale`, `Tailscale DNS`, or an interface name.

url.description: `http://host:port`, the hub's REST base as seen from that address.

addresses.description: Tailscale first, then every non-internal IPv4 the hub's machine has.

sshPublicKey.description: The public key the hub's SSH adds sign in with, or null when it has none.

KeptProcess.description:
A process in a session keeper's unit that neither the keeper nor one of
its sessions runs: while one is there, the keeper is not stopped (agent
service-manager/keeper-job.ts), and the next look after it ends stops it.

Kind.description: A kind of choice: built in, or one he added.

example.description: The one line agents read to file a choice.

id.description: `look`, `behaviour`, `scope`, `approach`, `rules`, `tools`, or the slug of one he added.

LandsMode.description:
Where a work item's work goes once it finishes (hub/src/landing.ts):
`main` onto the repository's default branch, `branch` to a branch of its
own on origin, `pr` to that branch with a pull request, `none` nowhere (the
work is not commits; its outputs are the deliverable).

LawBroken.description: One law the hub caught broken, as every dashboard is told it.

at.description: When it was first caught broken since the hub started, ms since the epoch.

count.description: How many times it has been caught broken since.

lastAt.description: When it was last caught broken, ms since the epoch.

words.description: The facts that broke it, the last time.

LawsBrokenFrame.description:
Hub-originated: every law the hub has caught broken since it started,
whole, on each break, and to each dashboard as it connects. Sent apart from
the board, because the board's own frame may be the one a law failed.

LfsOfferState.description: Where a place's offer of Git LFS stands (`GET /api/lfs-offers/:id`, hub lfs-offers.ts).

answer.description: `open` while unanswered; `tracked`: its files are committed through LFS; `dismissed`: Not now.

commit.description: The commit that took them through LFS; null until then.

root.description: The folder's root on its machine.

rows.description: What is offered, a row per pattern.

LimitWindow.description:
One plan window, whoever meters it. `group` names how long the window runs:
`session` is a 5-hour window (Claude's `five_hour`, OpenCode Go's `rolling`),
`weekly` runs 7 days, `monthly` runs one calendar month to `resetsAt`.
`percent` is the share USED, 0–100 (it can pass 100).

ListedBrowser.description:
One browser of the fleet as the hub lists it (`GET /api/browsers`, and
{@link BrowserListFrame}): the row its machine last reported, kept by the
hub, with the machine's name and what the machine says of it now (`why`,
`progress`, `origin`, from its latest frame).

lastUsedAt.description: ms epoch of the last agent connection or viewer.

origin.description: The origin of the page the person's view shows; absent while it shows none.

progress.description: How far an image build is, while `state` is `pulling` or `building`.

projectId.description: The project of a `project:` key; null for a machine's own browser.

takeover.description: Who holds it privately: the asking workspace, `""` when nobody asked; null while nobody does.

dashboardPort.description: The dashboard's port: the one the name's address carries.

host.description: The hub's machine, by its hostname.

name.description: The `.local` name the hub holds, while `held`.

url.description: The dashboard at the name, with its port (`http://cawco.local:3455`), while `held`.

LocalNameState.description:
Where the name stands:
- `held`: the hub answers `name` on its networks (`cawco.local`, or
  `cawco-2.local` when another hub there answers the first);
- `absent`: it answers none (mDNS off, no network other devices share, or
  the name still being probed).

MachineCapability.description: Optional machine tools. Reporting never installs or impersonates a tool.

addresses.description: `public-address` only: the machine's global unicast addresses, outside private, link-local and CGNAT ranges.

installCommand.description:
What installs it here. Empty when nothing may: a copy came some way
CawCo has no method for, and another would be a second copy (`reason`
says so).

media.description: `container-runtime` only: what the runtime forwards to the browser's media port. Short of `udp+tcp`, `reason` says how to get both.

missing.description:
`workspace` only: each tool a delegate's workspace needs that the
machine lacks (core workspace-needs.ts). While it is not empty the
machine refuses every delegate before anything starts, in `reason`'s
words, and `installCommand` installs them all.

nat.description:
`public-address` only, on a machine with none of its own: the public
address its router maps it to, as a STUN binding answered it, and its
address on the router's network (core stream-relay.ts `STUN_SERVER`).

MachineGoLimits.description: One machine's OpenCode Go plan, read with that machine's Go key.

MachineHookScript.description:
A fleet hook's script as one machine really has it, whoever last wrote it.
What {@link READ_HOOK_SCRIPT} answers with.

MachineMemoryDoc.description: One linked document as a machine really has it, whoever wrote it.

MachineMemorySet.description:
A machine's own memory set: the user CLAUDE.md and whatever is under
`~/.claude/memories/`. What {@link READ_MEMORY_FILE} answers with, and what a
peek and an adoption read.

MachinePath.description:
An absolute, normalised path on one machine (see the module). On the wire
it is a plain string: the brand is the compiler's alone.

MarketplaceLink.description:
A link of the marketplace at `source`, asked for: under way (`fetching`),
linked (`marketplace`, the row), or refused (`error`).

marketplace.description:
One linked plugin marketplace. `source` is whatever
`claude plugin marketplace add` accepts — `owner/repo`, a git URL, a
marketplace.json URL — passed through verbatim.

MarketplacePluginInfo.description: One installable plugin, as a linked marketplace's `marketplace.json` lists it.

MarketplaceRead.description:
A marketplace source as the hub read it: what its `marketplace.json` calls
it and what it offers, or why it could not be read. The hub reads it after
the request that asked has answered (`fetching`), and the read that lands
is a `fleet.fetch` frame.

name.description: What it calls itself: the only name it can be linked under.

Member.description: One member of Who decides: built in, or one he added.

builtIn.description: `you`, `caw`, `advisor`, `practice`, `asker`, or the slug of a member he added (a delegate type's name).

delegateType.description: An agent (built-in Advisor and Common practice included): the fleet delegate type it runs as.

hear.description: How he hears about its answers; null for You, Caw and The agent, which have none.

hue.description: One of the eight identity marks (1–8); null for Caw's flock and You.

job.description: One line under the name: what it does with a decision.

pose.description: Caw's flock: the pose it wears; null for the rest.

reach.description: A person or channel: how it is reached. Null until that slice.

subject.description: In a sentence: "Roost iOS sends scope to the advisor".

MemberType.description: Who decides a kind. The five built in are constants; the rest are rows.

MemoryDocRow.description:
One document the main memory links, as the dashboard reads it. Like a
subagent's file and unlike a skill's, the content rides the listing: a
document is a page of markdown, and an editor that has to fetch each one
again is a round trip for nothing.

scope.description: The sessions it is loaded into; absent is a linked document under `~/.claude/memories/`.

updatedAt.description: When it was last stored, ISO, as the answer carries it.

MemoryScope.description:
Which sessions a fleet memory document reaches. No scope at all is a
linked document under `~/.claude/memories/`, read on purpose. A scope
makes it instructions every matching session loads at its start; each
field narrows, and the fields are ANDed:

- `role`: the sessions of that role;
- `delegateTypes`: the sessions started as one of those delegate types;
- `model`: the sessions whose model id contains it, in any case (`opus`
  covers every dated build of it, as a rule's model scope does);
- `projectIds`: the sessions in a checkout or workspace of one of those
  projects. With nothing else, the document is written into each such
  place as `.claude/rules/cawco/<path>` ({@link FleetPlacedMemoryDoc}).

A document scoped by role, type or model reaches its sessions as they
launch, from the hub ({@link SessionInstruction}), in the instructions a
compaction keeps.

`briefer` turns the scope around: the document is guidance for writing a
brief, and reaches the session that calls `delegate`, never the delegate.
`delegateTypes` and `model` then name the delegates it is about (none:
every delegate); the hub hands it to the caller once before the first
such delegate goes out, and again after the caller's next compaction
(hub briefings.ts). It takes no `role`, `projectIds` or `areaIds`.

`areaIds` names areas (core areas.ts): a document scoped to an area is
scoped to every project in it as the hub reads it, a project moved in or
out taking it or leaving it then ({@link inScopedProjects}).

areaIds.description: Never empty when present: every project in each area, as read.

model.description: A model id, or part of one; never blank when present.

projectIds.description: Never empty when present: no project is `projectIds` left out.

MemoryVersion.description:
One superseded version of the fleet's memory, as a listing reads it —
without its content (`GET /api/fleet/memory/history`).

createdAt.description: When it was kept, ISO, as the answer carries it.

path.description: Which document of the set it was a version of; absent is the main one.

source.description: `fleet` for the hub's own row; `machine:<machineId>` for a copy a forced push took off that machine.

ModeAsk.description:
A send or a start that has to start its session again (a wake, a rewind)
and finds no permission mode it can start it on: its row records none and
none was ever chosen for its harness on its machine (the hub's
`reviveMode`), or the one it would start on is one its machine doesn't
take (`refused`). Not a refusal to show: the page asks for a mode where
the person acted, starts the session again on it, and does what was asked.

refused.description: The mode it would have started on, which its machine doesn't take; absent when none was named at all.

ModelInfo.description: One model a harness offers. `value` is the wire id; `resolvedModel` the alias.

contextWindow.description:
The tokens one request to the model may send, as the harness reports it:
opencode's provider `limit.input` where it gives one, else its
`limit.context`; pi's `Model.contextWindow`; and for claude the
`modelUsage` window the hub last observed. Absent means unknown — never a
guess.

defaultEffort.description:
The effort the CLI applies when a spawn omits effort, measured by the
harness. Null when the model takes none; absent when not measured.

released.description: ISO date the model was released, when the catalog source says.

supportsEffort.description:
Whether this model has an effort scale, and which of its stops it reaches.
The pair is the *only* thing that decides what an effort control offers —
`xhigh` and `max` are model-dependent, and a hardcoded list of which models
have them is a list that is wrong by the next release.

supportsThinkingOff.description:
Whether the model's thinking can be turned off, as Claude Code's model
list says (its initialize answer carries it; the Agent SDK's
`ModelInfo` does not name it yet).

ModelTurnUsage.description:
What one model spent in one turn. `cacheWrite` is every cache write;
`cacheWrite1h` the part of it written with a 1-hour lifetime, absent when
the harness does not split it. `costUsd` is the sum of each request's own
price (`pricedRequest`, at its prompt's tier and its time), null when
the model's provider lists no price for it; a summed turn is never priced.

MomentAuthor.description: Who a transcript's words are (the index's `author`): only `owner` is "said by me".

MoveAsk.description:
What a move does, as the person reads it before "Move it" (the owner's
pick D "Plain + details"): in New session's step 2, which the modal
morphs to on "Move & start", and on the approval card of a move started
anywhere else.

bigFiles.description: The large files that go to LFS with the yes.

details.description: The Details fold: the git terms of what "Move it" runs, one per line, for mono.

gitInit.description: The folder is no repository: "Move it" runs `git init` and one commit.

key.description:
What the person says yes to, when the move needs a yes (the folder is
no repository, or big files would go into history): New session sends
it back as {@link MoveRequest.approved}. Absent when no yes is needed.

lines.description: The lines under the title, in order.

title.description: "Move ~/anbar to obelisk?"

MoveError.description: A job's failure: the step it failed at, in words, and the tool's own last line.

detail.description: The tool's own last line (git's, git-lfs's), any credential removed.

MoveEstimate.description:
What the New session modal reads when a machine without the folder it
moves is picked:
`GET /api/projects/:id/move-estimate?machine=<target>[&from=<place>][&path=]`.

ask.description: What "Move it" does, for New session's step 2; set when a move is needed and can run.

display.description: The destination as the person reads it, under the machine's home as `~`: `~/cockpit`.

lfsBytes.description: Bytes of large files after the clone.

needed.description: Whether a move is needed: false when the target already has a checkout of the folder's repository.

needsApproval.description: Whether `approval` is a step: no repository yet, or files over 50 MB would go raw.

path.description: The destination: the place it has there (`needed: false`), else where it would go.

refused.description: Why it can't move, as the modal's reading line says it.
