uncommittedFiles.description: Files with uncommitted changes on the source (tracked and untracked, not ignored).

MoveJob.description:
A move job as every dashboard and the apps follow it: on the `moves`
frame, in the `instances` frame's `moves`, and at `GET /api/moves`.

ask.description: Set when `approval` is a step: what "Move it" does, for its card and its step's words.

askId.description:
While `approval` waits on a yes nobody gave in New session (a
delegate's, a task's or the API's move): the ask parked through the
same channel as every permission ask (dashboards, push), on
the session's own row ({@link targetInstanceId}, which reads "Needs
you"), an `AskUserQuestion` whose options are "Don't move" and "Move
it", answered like any question at `/api/pending`.

bytes.description: Bytes the clone fetches, as the source's repository measured them.

error.description: A job's failure: the step it failed at, in words, and the tool's own last line.

from.description:
Where the clone comes from: the hub (a project with no outside remote)
or the project's outside remote, by host ("github.com"), which names the
step ("Fetching from GitHub").

install.description:
Never sent: a move installs nothing. Declared for the shipped apps whose
client reads it (TestFlight 20261015.3 to 20261018); it goes once none
is installable.

kept.description: What a Cancel left on disk, in words, once cancelled.

lfs.description: The large files: how many, and their bytes; set when `lfs` is a step.

lfsFile.description: While a file of at least {@link LARGE_FILE_BYTES} is in flight: the largest one.

moved.description: Once started: what moved, for the ready line ("cockpit to obelisk · snapshot cawco/move/gearbox").

progress.description: Bytes so far of the step in flight (`clone`, `lfs`).

snapshot.description: Set when `snapshot` is a step: the branch the hub holds the work on, and how many files were uncommitted.

stayed.description: Once started: what stayed, for the ready line ("your .env and ignored files stay on gearbox").

steps.description: The steps this job runs, in order: the pane draws the ones ahead muted.

stoppedAt.description: Once cancelled: the step it stopped at.

targetInstanceId.description:
The session the job starts, under this id from the start: its row is on
the board from then (status `moving`, named by its New session title or
its first prompt's words), and the start takes the same row on.

MoveLargeFile.description: One file of a job's approval ask that goes to LFS: its path and size.

MoveProgressFrame.description:
Daemon → hub: how far the step in flight is. `file` only while a file of
at least {@link LARGE_FILE_BYTES} is in flight (the largest).

MoveStage.description: Where a job stands: at one of its steps, or settled.

MoveStep.description: A stage the job does work in.

MovesFrame.description: Hub → dashboards and apps: every move job, whole, on each change.

NamedAccount.description: An account as a transcript line names it, as it was when the line was written.

compactSummary.description:
This message is a compaction's summary, not an answer: opencode writes
its summary in the assistant's role (`summary: true` on the message).
Its text is the compaction's brief ({@link SessionMessage.compactSummary}).

contentOffset.description: Blocks already published for this message, preserving row ids across incremental settlement.

error.description:
The harness's word that this message is not the model answering but a
failure written in its place — Claude's synthetic `authentication_failed`,
`rate_limit`, … (measured on CLI 2.1.280: "Not logged in · Please run
/login" arrives as one, before an `is_error` result).

failedSends.description:
Set by the hub on an error message ({@link error}) that answered sends
the session had just read: they failed with its words, and their rows
carry them, so it draws no row of its own.

raw.description: The harness's own event, verbatim, for renderers that need more than this.

timestamp.description:
When the harness stored this record, ISO-8601: the clock its row shows,
live as after a reload ({@link SessionMessage.timestamp}). Claude's
stream carries its record's own; opencode's is its message's
`time.created`; pi's is its entry's. Absent on a frame the harness
stores no record for.

source.description:
The picture as the harness takes it (`base64`), or as the hub's
transcript and `send` records carry it: a reference into its media
store (`url`), fetched when the picture is shown.

questionResult.description: The answer payload of an `AskUserQuestion` tool result, normalised by the harness adapter.

NeutralRawMessage.description: A frame that has no neutral meaning yet, forwarded whole for a future renderer.

atLimit.description:
pi and OpenCode: the provider refused the turn at its account's limit,
by the structured refusal its harness handed over (core
`atProviderLimit`). Claude's is its assistant frame's `error`.

cache.description: Prompt-cache tokens the turn read from / wrote to, when the harness reports them.

compactsAt.description:
Where its harness compacts the session on its own, in tokens of context,
as its settings and its model stood at the turn's end: Claude Code's
auto-compact point, pi's `contextWindow - reserveTokens`, OpenCode's
window less its buffer (the agent's harnesses/compaction-points.ts).
Absent when the harness compacts on its own at no point it says, or
the agent did not say one.

contextTokens.description:
pi and OpenCode: the tokens the turn's last request sent (uncached input
plus cache reads and writes, as the harness reports that request's
usage), which is the session's context as it stood. Claude's is read off
{@link promptCacheUsage}.

cut.description:
With {@link serverStopped}: the shell commands the turn was running as
its server stopped, read off the session's own tool calls (agent
session.ts `#shells`), each said interrupted in the turn handed back.

failedSends.description:
The sends this error failed, set by the hub: read, and answered by nothing
but this error. Their rows carry the error, so it draws no line of its own.

lastRequestAt.description: Agent receive time of the last main-loop requesting status, epoch ms.

recovered.description: Read from stored history during recovery, rather than a newly completed turn.

serverStopped.description:
OpenCode: the server the turn ran in stopped before it finished
(`session.execution.interrupted` reason `shutdown`, or a reattach that
finds the turn unfinished): cut, not ended, so the hub hands it back.
`errors` carries the same in words (core `SERVER_STOPPED_MID_TURN`).

timestamp.description: When the harness stored what it closes on ({@link NeutralAssistantMessage.timestamp}).

turnUsage.description:
OpenCode and pi: the turn's tokens by model, summed over its assistant
messages and any compaction it ran. Claude's are read off the change in
its cumulative `modelUsage` by the hub.

wakes.description:
What the session has arranged to wake itself as the turn ends, set by
its harness's adapter on every result it reads ({@link TurnWakes}). The
hub pushes a finished turn to the person only when the session waits on
nothing of its own (push.ts `turnEnded`).

NeutralSessionInfo.description: A stored session as the catalog lists it. `harness` says who owns the id.

firstPrompt.description: The first prompt as its harness listed it, raw: kept for the shipped app; a reader names the session by {@link firstTitle}.

firstTitle.description:
The first prompt as a title, derived once where the listing is answered
(agent session.ts, core `deriveTitleFromFirstMessage`): what a reader
names a session with no given title by, never parsing the prompt itself.

startedBy.description:
Who started it, where its harness records that. Claude Code writes its
`entrypoint` on every record of a transcript: the terminal, the desktop
app and the VS Code extension are a person's; `sdk-ts`, `sdk-py`,
`sdk-cli` (`claude -p`) and every other are a program's (agent
claude.ts `startedBy`). Absent where nothing recorded says: a Claude
transcript from before the field, and every OpenCode and pi session
(OpenCode's database holds the same fields for a typed session and
for `opencode run`; pi's session header names its folder and its
parent, never what started it). A list of a person's work draws a
stored transcript only when this says `person` (dashboard
recent.svelte.ts); search finds every one.

wroteAt.description:
When the person last sent a prompt in it (ms epoch), read from the
transcript at its source: Claude's last `user` record that holds a
prompt, not a tool result; OpenCode's last `user` message; pi's last
`user` message. Absent when it holds none. What a stored transcript is
placed by, as a listed session is by its `wroteAt`: an agent's reply
never moves it, where {@link lastModified} moves on every write.

NeutralStatus.description: A session's own word on what it is doing right now.

NeutralSystemMessage.description:
A `system` frame. One loose interface rather than a subtype union: the folding
layer switches on `subtype` and reads the fields each subtype carries, and a
harness that emits a subtype nothing here names degrades to a generic line.

compact_error.description: A failed compaction's words; {@link compact_failure} is what a reader decides on.

compact_failure.description: How a compaction failed, typed ({@link CompactionFailure}); with `compact_result: "failed"`.

failure.description:
How a compaction failed, as its harness typed the error it failed on:
`kind`, the harness's own sort of it (OpenCode's error `type`, as
`provider.timeout`), or `unknown` when it gave none; `status`, the
provider's HTTP status when there was one; `message`, its words as said.

asked.description: A session asked for it, not its account's limit: true on every line written now.

asks.description: It restarted from the person's own messages alone: nothing was summarised.

by.description:
Who asked for it, as the line's detail names them: a session by its
name, or a comment on a task. Absent on a line a hub stored before
continuations stayed one session.

kind.description:
The session went on in a fresh conversation of its own, seeded with
a summary of the one before (or the person's own messages alone,
`asks`), on `to` from `from` (null on a harness without accounts):
a continuation anything but the person's own Continue asked for,
which stays one session (hub `foldContinued`). The line stands
between the two conversations.

move.description:
It went on from a summary as its move to `to`, as the policy says
({@link Compaction} `summary`): at its account's limit (`limit`:
the window that refused it and when that resets, or its refused
sign-in), or ahead of one (`ahead`: its account's forecast run-out,
its extra usage, or a person's move, `because`). Absent: a session
or a task asked for it.

because.description:
Why a session moved other than at a limit refusing a turn of it
({@link AccountMove} `moved`): its account was forecast to run out at
`runsOutAt` (a rebalance between turns), its cache was cold at its wake,
so the move re-read nothing extra, Claude Code refused `from`'s
credential for good (`refused`: the hub signed it out there), or a turn
of it ran on `from`'s extra usage past its plan, which says to move then.

preparedAtPct.description:
Null on every line written now (no summary is written ahead of a
limit any more), and never shown. Sent only because the TestFlight
builds 20261015 to 20261018 require it, which the hub's wire check
holds to (packages/hub/scripts/openapi.ts); it goes in the change
that expires them.

writtenOn.description: The account whose summariser wrote the summary it went on from; null when nothing was summarised.

asked.description: Moved because a person asked (`POST /api/instances/:id/account`), not at a limit.

because.description: Why it moved other than at a limit ({@link MoveBecause}); absent: its account's limit refused a turn, or a person asked.

compact.description:
Moved to another organization with a context of the policy's
`moveWholeUnderK` or more, compacted natively ({@link Compaction}):
it files its open items, then its harness's `/compact` runs, as its
first steps on `to`, or on `from` before the move
({@link compactFirst}). The line is said again under its id as that
goes.

compactBy.description: The harness whose own `/compact` runs, when it is not Claude Code's: what its compaction keeps is less.

compactFirst.description:
The compaction runs on `from`, warm, and the move follows it: the
policy's `beforeMove`. Absent: it runs on `to` after the move.

cost.description: What the re-read cost on `to`: a percent of the window it is counted against, named as `windowWords` names it; absent when unpriced.

ended.description:
What the move ended with its old process: work it held for later (its
background tasks, its one-time wake-ups), which no resume on another
account brings back. The session is told on arrival what ended.

relaunched.description:
Its process ended on `to` before it took a step of the compaction,
and the hub started it again there to take it.

removed.description: Moved because a person removed `from` (`DELETE /api/accounts/:id`): every session on it moves off.

resetsAt.description: When that window resets, epoch ms; null when nothing said.

sameOrganization.description: Both accounts in one organization: its prompt cache came along.

signedOut.description: Moved because a person signed `from` out on its machine (`DELETE /api/accounts/:id/machines/:machineId`): every session on it there moves off.

signedOutOn.description: With `signedOut`: that machine, as it was named then.

summaryRefused.description:
The policy said to go on from a summary, which could not be written
for this move, in the hub's words: its harness's `/compact` ran
instead.

window.description: The window that refused it, as core usage/windows.ts `windowWords` names it.

action.description: What failed: a move whole (`move`), or, in a stored line, a continuation from a summary (`continue`).

asked.description: The session asked for it (`continue_session`), not its account's limit.

kind.description:
Moving it whole to `to` failed at `step`: it goes on in its
conversation, still on `from`. (`continue`, a continuation from a
summary, and `asked`, are history only: lines a hub stored before it
compacted natively.)

reason.description: What the hub got from the step that failed.

signedOut.description: It was moving off `from` because Claude Code refused `from`'s sign-in: `from` has no reset to wait for.

waits.description:
Only work its process holds for later kept it (a background task, a
one-time wake-up), and no person waits on it: the move goes when that
work ends, or once it has been held {@link RESTART_WAIT_CAP_MS},
ending it.

kind.description:
The session's process was ended, and by whom: a stop someone asked
for, or a signal from outside CawCo. A stop is never a failure; the
line says what starts it again.

cost.description: What the re-read will cost on `to`: a percent of its window; absent when unpriced.

kind.description:
A move whole the policy chose for a context large enough to compact
({@link Compaction} `whole`): it goes at `at` by itself, from `from`
to `to`, unless a person stops the session before then.

Claude Code refused `account`'s credential for good and no other
account can take the session: it stays, and what it is sent waits at
the hub, until `account` is signed in again or another comes free.

A work item's session whose project has Caw off: nothing wakes a
model there, so nothing carries it on past `account`'s limit,
neither a move nor a resume at the reset. A person sends it on.

resetsAt.description: When that limit resets, epoch ms; null when nothing said.

account.description: The account it is held on, at its limit.

accounts.description:
Every other account of its provider and why it didn't take it, or
that it could ({@link HeldAccount}): what a person reads, so a line
never says no account has room beside one that has. Absent on lines
stored before holds named them.

frees.description:
Another account that frees before `account` resets: it moves there
at `until`. Absent: `until` is `account`'s own reset.

until.description: The earliest moment an account takes it again, epoch ms: the line counts down to it.

permissionMode.description:
How a session answers tool permissions. The union is Claude Code's, plus
`fullSend`, CawCo's own: bypass, with every approval approved for the
session (the owner, 2026-10-22: "FULL SEND LITERALLY MEANS FULL SEND"):
on Claude Code the host answers the checks and ask rules the CLI still
raises in bypass, and on every harness the hub approves CawCo's admin
writes (hub asks.ts). A question to the person still asks; a
fleet-denied tool still never runs. Each adapter maps `fullSend` onto its
harness; none hands it to an SDK as is.

result.description:
task_notification: the report a finished task handed back. Claude's live
frame carries none; its stored notification (`<result>`) does.

retry.description:
provider_retry ({@link PROVIDER_RETRY}): the provider's own message,
when the harness makes its next attempt (ms epoch) if it said, and
`atLimit` when the refusal it retries is the account's limit (core
`atProviderLimit`).

storedAs.description:
stored ({@link MESSAGES_STORED}), or read: the id the harness stores each
send under, by the send's uuid, where the harness keys its own record
differently (opencode's message id, pi's entry id). The hub keeps it on
the send's record, so a history read finds the send again.

whole.description:
held ({@link MESSAGES_HELD}): `held` is every send the harness has been
handed. Said by an agent taking over a process that outlived the one
before it, off the process's own output: a send from before then that is
not in it never reached the process.

compactSummary.description:
This message is a compaction's summary, in the harness's own words: pi
reports one when a compaction ends. Claude's needs no flag — it opens
with words the transcript knows it by.

message.description: `harnessNote`: the message is a notice of the harness's, typed where its normaliser read it ({@link HarnessNote}).

harnessNote.description:
A notice the harness put in the user's role, as its agent's normaliser
read it (agent claude-transcript.ts `harnessNoteOf`): Claude Code's
`<task-notification>` block (`task-notification`) and its `[SYSTEM
NOTIFICATION …]` line, and a whole `<system-reminder>` block
(`system-reminder`). `title` is what a fold says closed, `status` the
task's (`completed`, `failed`, `stopped`; empty when it said none), `body`
the rest, as markdown. Never the reader's words.

reminder.description:
CawCo's word to the agent about this send (where it came from, which
skill applies), kept apart from `message` so the sender's words are the
whole of the message: the hub folds it into a `<system-reminder>` block
after them each time it hands the send to its machine (hub server.ts
`presenced`), and no row, record or Find draws it.

replaces.description:
A retry: the uuid of the failed send this one is sent in place of. The
hub marks that record `replaced` ({@link SendRecord.replacedBy}).

timestamp.description: When the harness stored it ({@link NeutralAssistantMessage.timestamp}).

ObservedRateLimitInfo.description:
The `rate_limit_info` payload, structurally. Not imported from the agent
SDK: `unifiedWindows` is marked `@internal` there, so it is stripped from
the published `.d.ts` even though the CLI emits it.

OnCap.description:
What reaching a project's spend cap does (Projects spec §5.3): `pause`
starts no new attempts at its tasks, `quiet` books what would wake its Caw
without a turn, `both` does both. The fleet has a default (Configure,
Spend); a project may set its own.

OpenCodeGoLimits.description:
The OpenCode Go plan's three windows, read from
`GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage` with the machine's `opencode-go`
key. Absent (null) on a machine with no Go key. `stale` is set when a read
failed and the last good windows are served with the error attached.

OrphanedComments.description: The person's comments on a step whose words no write of the session's has kept: the step's words, and the comments.

step.description: The words of the step they were written on.

OwnerDevice.description: A paired device, as `GET /api/devices` lists it. Its token never leaves the hub but once.

PageAnchor.description:
What a page's mark stands on: the element, by where it is written, its
selector and its text. An element inside a same-origin frame names the
frames it stands in, outermost first, each by its selector in the document
that holds it; its selector, source and text are read in the innermost
frame's document.

box.description: The element's box in the page when it was anchored, px: what the moved tray shows.

chain.description:
On a sheet: the components the element stands in, innermost first, each
where it is used (Svelte's `__svelte_meta.parent` component entries, or
a stamped component root's call site), then the story that mounts them.

embed.description:
The artifact whose frame holds it, when that frame shows one (a decision
page's Preview, dashboard decisions host Preview.svelte
`data-cawco-artifact`): a component canvas, a dev server's preview, a page.

file.description:
Where it stands in a file that is no HTML page, shown by CawCo's file
viewer (file-spot.ts): a point on the image or on a PDF's page, a text's
line or lines, or the file as a whole. The element is the viewer's spot
for it; this is what finds it again and what the agent is told.

frames.description:
The frames it stands in, outermost first, each by its selector in its
parent's document; none at the top. A frame of another origin is read
through its own overlay (@cawco/preview overlay embeds.ts), and the
selector, source, text, chain and sheet are read in the innermost frame's
document either way.

name.description:
What a person calls the spot, read off the element as the page drew it
(@cawco/preview overlay spot-name.ts: its label and what it is, "Search
comments field"): the pin's name (core pin-name.ts), never a
component's name or its text run together.

page.description:
Named by its place alone: the hash of the document it stands in, as it was
served when the anchor was read. While the document is that one, the words at its place have changed
only by the page's own running, so the element there is the mark's
({@link findAnchor}); a revision may have put another there.

sheet.description:
On a component canvas: its states file (from the toolchain root), the
story whose frame holds the element, and the frame's state: the
interaction it is forced into, its scheme and its width (px; null when it
fits its content).

text.description: The element's text, at most {@link COMMENT_LIMITS.anchorText} characters.

PageBroken.description:
What a decision page's program leaves broken on the person's picks and
the project's links between pages, for its writer to put back or tell
the person.
Each list only when it has something.

after.description: Decisions it lacks (taken out, or never written) that another page comes after, with the `page#card`s that do: no link is made for them.

options.description: Options taken out that the person picked, by decision: the pick is kept, and its card says the option is gone.

picked.description: Decisions taken out that the person picked: the pick is kept, on no card.

unlinked.description: Its `after`s naming no decision of the project's: no link is made for them.

PageError.description: Where a page's code threw, 1-based, the file from the toolchain root when it is the project's.

kind.description: An element's file that failed to load: the element, and the address it asked for.
A dial of `cawcoDials(panel, config)` the panel doesn't draw: its path in the config, and its kind as written (core dial-config.ts `unread`).
An uncaught error or rejection: its message, and where it was thrown when the browser says (the file as a path on the page's origin, else its address).

source.description: Its line's words, when it was thrown in the page's own document: what to find it by in the page's source.

PageLinks.description: What a page's program links to: all its frame may learn the faces of, and ask its host to open.

artifacts.description: The artifacts its Canvas and Preview pieces show, by id.

PairingRequest.description: A pairing waiting on the person, as every paired screen shows it.

name.description: "Chrome on Linux", "CawCo on iPhone", "cawco relay".

PairingStart.description:
A client waiting to be paired (RFC 8628 §3.2's device authorization
response): what it shows (`userCode`), what it polls with (`deviceCode`,
kept by that client alone), how often, and for how long, and where the
person approves it.

hubId.description: The hub asked (its `/health` `hubId`): a device that scans the code knows it is its own hub's.

verificationUri.description: Where the person approves it (§3.2 `verification_uri`): the dashboard's Configure › Devices.

verificationUriComplete.description:
The same with the code and the hub in its query (§3.2
`verification_uri_complete`: "includes the user_code ... designed for
non-textual transmission"): what a QR beside the code carries, so a
paired device's camera names the hub and the pairing in one scan.

ParkedAsk.description: A parked ask as the hub holds it and every screen reads it (`/api/pending`): an `Envelope` whose payload is its permission request.

PendingAccountSignin.description:
A sign-in a machine has started for an account and not finished: the link
or device code it showed, kept by the hub until it ends or lapses
(`expiresAt`, epoch ms), so a screen that reloads or reopens shows that
same link or code again instead of starting another.

PermissionChange.description: One file or document the call changes: both sides, for the diff renderers.

after.description: The text the proposed side ends with.

before.description: The text as it stands now ("" when there is none yet, or the call does not say).

path.description: What changes, named as the person knows it: `CLAUDE.md`, a memory path, a file path.

PermissionField.description: One input field, as shown: its value written out, secrets already hidden.

PermissionMode.description:
How a session answers tool permissions. The union is Claude Code's, plus
`fullSend`, CawCo's own: bypass, with every approval approved for the
session (the owner, 2026-10-22: "FULL SEND LITERALLY MEANS FULL SEND"):
on Claude Code the host answers the checks and ask rules the CLI still
raises in bypass, and on every harness the hub approves CawCo's admin
writes (hub asks.ts). A question to the person still asks; a
fleet-denied tool still never runs. Each adapter maps `fullSend` onto its
harness; none hands it to an SDK as is.

asker.description: The session that asked, by the name the board gives it ("Caw" for a project's conversation).

changes.description: The changes the call makes, each drawn as a diff. Empty when it changes no text.

command.description:
The shell command a shell call runs, whole and out of a boundary's
rewrite: shown under the summary on every surface, one line until
opened. Absent for any other call.

detail.description: The line under the summary: how much changes and where ("3 lines changed in Working style").

fields.description: The rest of the input worth reading, secrets hidden. What the summary and the diffs already say is left out.

project.description: The project the asker works in, by name; absent for a session in none. The card's head reads "Caw · cockpit".

setTables.description:
What a change to a starting set does to it, each side a table the hub
fills from the count of calls (hub unused-trim.ts `standing`): what
joins it (a set that is new or gains items), then what leaves it (a
trim). Absent when the call changes no starting set, or moves nothing
in or out of one.

askId.description: The hub's own ask this frame stands for (core asks.ts), absent on a session process's own prompt.

browserAsk.description: A browser ask's browser, reason and origin; absent on every other ask.

connectAsk.description: A connect ask's server, reason, address and access; absent on every other ask.

originInstanceId.description:
The session whose conversation made this ask, when the ask is not
parked on that session's own row (a memory curator run's proposal,
parked under its own id on machine "hub"). The ask is drawn and answered
in that session's pane, at `toolUseId`, as its own asks are.

presentation.description:
What the ask says on every surface, read once by the hub as it parks it
(permission-presentation.ts): the daemon's leg does not carry it, and the
hub fills it before anything else reads the frame.

processGeneration.description: The launch that raised this request; daemon replays retain it verbatim.

raisedAt.description: When the hub first parked this ask, ms epoch. Absent only on the daemon-to-hub leg.

requestKind.description: `tool` for a permission, `question` for an AskUserQuestion-shaped prompt.

routedTo.description: `parent` when the ask is left to the session's parent, not the person.

sourceFacts.description: Where an install the ask proposes fetches from (hub source-facts.ts).

toolUseId.description: The tool call the ask gates, as its transcript message names it.

answer.description: What won, and where, when the ask was answered (`outcome: answered`) and the hub knows.

kind.description: An ask is over, whoever settled it; every client removes its parked card.

processEnded.description:
A cancelled ask's process ended with it open: nobody answered it, and the
hub keeps a permission prompt for the session's next process (hub asks.ts
`keep`) instead of taking it off every screen.

reason.description:
Why a cancelled ask went unanswered, when the hub could say: it could not
show it at all (an ask from a session or launch it holds no live row for).
Such an ask was never parked on any screen, so this frame is the only
word a transcript gets of it.

toolName.description: The asking tool, for the line a screen writes about an ask it never held.

PermissionUpdate.description: A permission the SDK suggests persisting, so "always allow" has something to write.

PersonFrame.description: Hub-originated: the person and the machines that count, whole, on each change.

PersonRead.description:
`GET /api/person`: the view, and the machine the asking browser is on, as
the hub ties it by the address the request came from (hub
notifications.ts `machineAt`); null when no one machine is. Each browser
reads its own: the `person` frame, the same to every dashboard, never
carries it.

awayAfterMs.description: The away clock, ms: the person's setting, else {@link AWAY_AFTER_DEFAULT_MS}.

manual.description: The person turned Appear away on.

on.description: A chat they are in, the first of those in sight where they are (hub notifications.ts `chatsOn`); null when elsewhere or away.

since.description: Away: since their last input or the lock, epoch ms; null when here, or no device has ever said.

PersonView.description: The socket's `person` frame, and `GET /api/person` beside its {@link PersonRead}: the person, their away clock, and the machines that can count toward it.

awayAfterMs.description: The away clock, ms: the person's setting, else {@link AWAY_AFTER_DEFAULT_MS}.

manual.description: The person turned Appear away on.

on.description: A chat they are in, the first of those in sight where they are (hub notifications.ts `chatsOn`); null when elsewhere or away.

since.description: Away: since their last input or the lock, epoch ms; null when here, or no device has ever said.

PhoneDone.description: What the hub did for a phone request.

elements.description: The page's elements under it (a comment: the one tapped); a canvas's, by id.

heard.description: What of it the session was last told ({@link pinSaid}); the hub stamps it on delivery.

ink.description: The stroke group it stands on, when it stands on ink.

movedAt.description: Its element is gone from the page since then; it waits in the moved tray.

notSent.description:
The last delivery that carried it reached no one: when, and why in words
(the hub's reason). The hub writes it; the next delivery that carries
the pin clears it ({@link pinHeard}).

number.description: In order of creation, per artifact, from 1.

point.description: Where on its element a tapped pin stands: fractions of the element's box.

resolvedBy.description: Who resolved it: the person, or the agent (comment_resolve), whose resolve is an answer.

seenAt.description:
When the person last looked at it: its thread opened (a press, a chip,
a step) or a Send of the page. An agent's entry or resolve newer than it
is a new answer ({@link newAnswer}). Kept in the doc, so it holds on
every device he opens the page on.

sentAt.description: When it was first delivered to the session.

title.description:
What it stood on when it was made, in words (core pin-name.ts), kept as
its title: a revision that rewrites its element moves its anchor's text,
and that text is what changed ("after"), never the pin's name.

PinnedElement.description: An element under a pin, as the overlay describes it, without its markup.

PlaceKind.description:
What a place is: a checkout on a machine, or the project's folder on the
hub (its
`machineId` is `"hub"` (db `HUB_PLACE_MACHINE`) and its path `projects/<id>`, relative
to the hub's data folder; every project has one from the moment it is
made).

PlaceLfsRow.description:
Files a place's first commit left out for their size alone, by the
pattern Git LFS would track them under, as `git lfs migrate info` rows
read (extension, count, size): `*.<ext>` for a file with an extension,
its own path from the place's root for one without. git-lfs-faq(7):
"we recommend using patterns rather than `--above`".

count.description: How many of the left-out files it covers.

paths.description: Those files, from the place's root.

PlacePath.description:
Where a place is: a folder on its machine, or (kind `hub`) the project's
folder on the hub. A plain string on the wire, as both sides are; a union
left unnamed reaches the API's schema as an anyOf its clients wrap.

PlaceProject.description: A live project, as a folder's neighbour is named.

PlacementStrategy.description: How a provider's new sessions choose among its accounts.

PlacesHeard.description:
How the machine holding a conversation's transcript took the places read:
it answered; it did not answer in time, or is not connected; or it
answered that it has no such read, its agent older than the hub's places
control (`transcriptPlaces`), which an update brings.

PlanChange.description: A person's change, recorded on the plan in their words and told to its receiver.

at.description: When the person made it, ISO 8601.

step.description: The step it changed (the step added, for `add`).

toldAt.description: When it went to {@link to} in a message, ISO 8601; absent while it waits.

undelivered.description: Why it reached no one, when nothing could take it.

was.description: The step's words before the change; for `add`, the step it follows ("" at the top).

words.description:
The person's words: the new words, the added step, the comment; `done` or
`not done` for a tick; `up` or `down` for a move; "" for a removal.

PlanComment.description: The person's comment on a step, in their words.

at.description: When they wrote it, ISO 8601.

PlanDelta.description: Hub → a session's followers: the change from `rev - 1` to `rev` (AG-UI STATE_DELTA).

PlanFollow.description:
Client → hub: the sessions whose plan this socket follows beside the ones
it streams (the app's project page), the whole set each time.
One newly in the set is answered with its snapshot; deltas follow.

PlanReceiver.description:
Who hears a change to a session's plan: the session itself, the session
that delegated it (a delegate's plan is its parent's to pass on), or the
project's Caw (a task attempt's plan: he dispatched it).

PlanResync.description: Client → hub: "my copy has a gap; send the plan whole".

PlanSnapshot.description: Hub → a session's followers: the whole plan (AG-UI STATE_SNAPSHOT).

awayUnseen.description:
The spec's away notes (its `## Since HH:MM (you were away)` section,
core injected.ts `awayNotesOf`) changed since the person last saw them:
opened the plan, or had them recapped. `since` is the section's HH:MM.
Absent once seen, and while the spec has none.

changes.description: The person's latest changes to it, newest last.

needs.description:
The plan's own needs: each artifact of the session's in Needs you, by
id, that no open step's `waitsOn` names ({@link planNeedsOf}). One a
step names shows on that step. Absent when there are none.

orphanedComments.description: The person's step comments whose step's words are gone from the list, oldest step first. Absent when none.

source.description:
Always `cawco`: the steps are CawCo's list on every harness. Still sent
because the apps on TestFlight 20261015 through 20261018 decode it as
required (hub openapi.ts's wire check); it goes in the change that
expires those builds.

spec.description: The session's spec, once it has written one.

steps.description: CawCo's list: `todo_write`'s session scope, on every harness.

taskId.description: On a task attempt: the task.

todos.description: On a task attempt: the task's to-dos, nested and ticked as its file has them.

PlanSpec.description: The session's spec, as it last wrote it.

at.description: When it was written, ISO 8601.

PlanStep.description: One step of a session's plan: an ACP plan entry, with an id and a nesting depth.

comments.description:
The person's comments on it, oldest first. A session's write keeps them
on the step of the same words, wherever it stands; with no such step
they go to the plan's {@link SessionPlan.orphanedComments}.

depth.description: Nesting by indent: 0 for a top-level step, one more than its parent's for a sub-step.

id.description: Stable within one list: the writer's, the step's place, or `you-…` for one the person added.

waitsOn.description:
What it waits on, set by the session (`todo_write`'s `waitsOn`): a
task, a card, a pin, a pull request, a run or a session, as a task's
`waits_on` keeps it (wait-targets.ts), settled by the hub's one resolver
(hub task-waits.ts). The hub drops it once it settles.

PresenceDevice.description: One device as the person's presence menu lists it: a machine whose agent reads its desktop.

counts.description: It counts toward whether you're here: the person turned it on (off until they do).

id.description: The machine's id.

name.description: The machine's name, as the fleet shows it.

state.description: What its desktop says now; null when it hasn't said for {@link MACHINE_TTL_MS}.

PreviewAddress.description:
Where a session's preview is served, as the hub reports it: its own port,
which the hub listens on in either mode, and in host mode the whole origin
the fleet's pattern names it by too. Which one a client loads is its own
choice, by where it reached the hub ({@link previewRoute}).

origin.description: Host mode's whole origin for the session.

port.description: The session's own preview port, listened on in either mode.

tailnet.description:
The session's origin on the hub machine's tailnet name, while the hub
serves HTTPS there (core tailnet-https.ts): on the tailnet addresses the
port answers HTTPS alone.

PreviewDown.description:
A preview whose page nothing serves: the hop that did not answer, as the
proxy's own page names it in a `<meta name="cawco-preview-down">` (core
`preview-proxy` `downResponse`), so the pane beside the conversation can
draw what happened instead of the proxy's page. `server`: the dev server
on the session's machine is not answering its port, or the server CawCo
runs for it (a sheet's stage, a served preview's command) didn't start,
the stage's words for why in {@link PREVIEW_WHY_META}. `machine`: the
machine's preview listener is not answering the hub, or the machine is
away. `workspace`: the port is a workspace's, and no boundary of that
workspace runs, so nothing in its network can answer. `reach`: the
machine could not open the way to the server (its listener did not start,
or the bridge into the workspace's network did not open); the page names
why in {@link PREVIEW_WHY_META}. `closed`: the session shows no preview
now (it was closed, or the session ended). `gone`: the workspace that
served it is not on its machine any more (archived, discarded), so this
version of it can't be shown again; only its session making it again
brings it back. `error`: every hop answered, and the page's server
answered its load with an error status and nothing the browser can draw
(a route that isn't there any more answering an empty 404, a plain-text
500); an HTML error page is the page, served as one: the machine's listener
answers the load with its own page in place of the server's (agent
preview.ts), the status and the error's first line as its why
(`errorLineOf`), never the browser's own error face. `crashed`: the page
loaded, but a script of its threw before its load and it shows nothing:
its overlay names it, the thrown message as its why (@cawco/preview
overlay embeds.ts `tellDrawn`).

artifact.description:
The artifact the session's panel shows (Projects spec §5.10), with its
title, the head's name, and its ask, the head's line under it, from the
first frame, while its page is still on its way. `name` is its slug,
never shown; no ask on one made before asks were kept.

artifacts.description:
Every artifact the session holds, by id, newest first: republished when
one is removed, so a panel's open list drops it at once.

origin.description:
Host mode's whole origin for the session (`scheme://name[:port]` from
the fleet's pattern, whose scheme is how those names are served, not how
the client reached the hub), beside `port` ({@link PreviewAddress}).

port.description:
The session's own preview port, listened on in either mode: a client
that reached the hub by any address but one under host mode's domain
loads the preview from it ({@link previewRoute}).

project.description:
The project whose origin serves what the panel shows: a project's page
(Projects spec §5.8), served on its project's origin alone, at
`/__cawco/page/<artifact id>/` there ({@link projectPagePlace}). Then
`port`, `origin` and `tailnet` are that origin's. Absent for
anything served on the session's own origin.

revision.description: Identifies one successful open, including a rebuild of the same source.

show.description:
Identifies the show: new with each show of an artifact (artifact_show,
artifact_create, the person's own open), kept while that show is only
published anew at a new `revision` (an update's re-show, the preview
mode set again). A tab's Close holds until it moves (dashboard
preview/closed-here.ts).

source.description:
What an artifact shows (Projects spec §5.10): a dev server or a folder on
the session's machine (a preview), or a page the hub built and keeps under
its data dir at `artifacts/<id>/` and serves itself, named by the page's
name. A dev server or folder may name `path`, the page inside it the
preview opens at (`/motion/updates`); the root when absent.

serve.description:
A workspace preview's server (core `stage.ts` {@link ServeSpec}): the
command the workspace's stage runs and keeps up on `port`, in `cwd`
from the clone's root. A request for it wakes it when it sleeps.

stage.description:
A sheet's: the workspace's stage serves the port (core `stage.ts`),
its toolchain root `dir` from the clone's root and the sheet's story file
`file` from that root. A request for it wakes the stage when it sleeps.

workspace.description: The workspace whose dev server it is: it runs in that workspace's own network.

stage.description:
A sheet's stage, or a workspace preview's server (`serve`), as its doc
keeps it (`meta.stage`), the frame published
again at the same revision on each change: for a panel that holds no doc
of its own (the app's), as the dashboard's pane reads it from the doc.

tailnet.description: The session's origin on the tailnet name while the hub serves HTTPS there ({@link PreviewAddress}).

PreviewSettings.description:
How previews are reached, fleet-wide (Settings › Previews, Caw's
`admin_previews_write`): `port`, one port per session from the hub's range,
which needs no setup; or `host`, an origin per session from `pattern`
(`https://`, then a host name whose first label holds `{session}`, standing
for the session's id, or `{port}`, for the preview port it keeps, so one
name per port of the range serves every session), for a fleet behind DNS
or a proxy that routes them to the hub's first preview port. `passDomain`:
the domain the names stand under, which the browser's pass is set on
({@link PREVIEW_PASS_COOKIE}).

PreviewTicket.description: A ticket into the previews for the device or browser that asked: single-use, and spent by `expiresAt` (ms epoch).

ProblemStatus.description:
Every status the hub answers a problem with: a refusal's, never a 2xx. A
problem passed on is said again at one of these, never at `number`:
Elysia keys a status it only knows as `number` `default`, which Eden's
client reads as a possible answer (a 2xx, or an empty body), where one of
these is its refusal.

ProjectCap.description:
A project's spend cap as it stands now: what the period has spent
against it, and what reaching it does. Spend is every session of the
project's (its Caw and its attempts) since the period began.

from.description: Where its amount and period came from: the project's own or its area's (core areas.ts).

inherited.description:
`onCap` is not the project's own (`onCapFrom` is its area or the fleet).
Read by the shipped apps and dashboard tabs on an older wire; `onCapFrom`
says where it came from.

onCap.description: What reaching it does: the project's own, else its area's, else the fleet's.

reached.description: Spent at or past the cap. Read with `resetsAt`: past it, the cap is not reached.

resetsAt.description: When the next period begins, ms epoch; the cap counts from zero then.

startsAt.description: When this period began, ms epoch.

cap.description: Its project's cap as it stands now; null once it has none.

kind.description: Hub-originated: a project's spend against its cap moved, or the cap did.

ProjectConversationView.description: A project's conversation, as `GET`/`PATCH /api/projects/:id/caw` answer it.

attemptsHearComments.description: Whether the person's comment on a task reaches its attempt, live or ended (hub jev-tasks.ts).

hearsTasks.description:
Whether the conversation reads what the person writes on the project's
tasks: a comment, a to-do or a task they add (hub task-input.ts). On or
off, like the rest of their words.

instanceId.description: The conversation's session, once the hub has started one.

mode.description:
The permission mode the hub starts the project's conversation in, the
project's own; null: the fleet's, else the one the person last chose
for its harness on that machine. A routine's or an event route's own
wins over it.

model.description: The model Caw's session runs; null: its harness's default.

problem.description: Why Caw could not start now, on or off, or why its last start failed; null when he could.

running.description:
What Caw started that still runs, as his off control lists it, each lead
row followed by its delegates: the sessions his work items run, and his
own turn while an event started it. Turning him off with any of these
running names which stop; the rest finish.

spendUsd.description: Dollars every Caw session of the project has cost.

starting.description:
His conversation is being started now (a project just made with Caw: its
create answers once the project is made, and his start carries on).

startingId.description:
The session his start is making, minted before its spawn is asked for,
while that start runs: his panel draws it as his conversation from the
first moment, its transcript read once the start has named it. Null
while no start runs.

ProjectDeleted.description: What a delete removed, on the hub and on each machine (by its name).

folder.description: Its folder on the hub went.

rows.description: Its rows, every one a forget would have kept.

ProjectGate.description:
A project's gate: `none` with no gate.md; `declared`, its steps (none
when its block names none); `unreadable`, what is wrong with it.

kind.description: Hub-originated: the session's standing offer, or null once it was answered.

ProjectOfferReason.description:
What made the hub offer to make a plain session a project (project-offers.ts);
`caw` when nothing did: Caw proposed it in conversation and you said yes.

ProjectOfferSummary.description: "Make this a project": offered once, on a plain session that outgrew itself.

line.description: One sentence naming why, ending in the question.

ProjectRestored.description: A restore's answer: the project back, and what came back of it.

left.description: Rows left out, by table: a row made since holds their key, or what they named went since.

ProjectSpend.description:
What a project has spent, as `GET /api/projects/:id/spend` answers it, in
dollars, read now. Each part is its sessions' usage as their machines
reported it: its conversations', its attempts' and every other session's.
The parts add up: `monthUsd` is the conversations' month, every attempt's
month and the others' month. Days and months are the hub's own (its
zone, as every "today" CawCo shows). What a project's cap counts.

attempts.description: Every task attempted this month, newest activity first: its attempts' month summed.
How many attempts the task has had.

lastAt.description: When its newest attempt was made or ended, ms epoch.

type.description: The delegate type its newest attempt ran, if one was named.

budget.description: What an attempt may spend where its task says nothing; null: no limit.

cap.description: The project's spend cap; null: it has none, and no limit.

caw.description: The project's conversations: what their sessions reported.

fleetOnCap.description: What reaching a cap does when the project sets nothing: the fleet's default.

monthStart.description: The first of this month, ms epoch.

others.description: Every session of the project that is neither its Caw nor an attempt.

ProjectStarter.description:
One starter: a sentence the person would say to Caw, put in the composer
when pressed (nothing is sent), the glyph for its kind of work, why it is
offered, and what it comes from.

reason.description: Why it is offered: one plain sentence, at most 14 words and 120 characters, with no ids, slugs or shorthand (hub starter-asks.ts `reasonRefusal`); `sources` name what it comes from.

ProjectStopFrame.description:
Hub-originated: one session a project's forget asked to stop
(`POST /api/projects/:id/stop`) has stopped, as its machine confirmed, or
could not be stopped, with the hub's reason, or (`deferred`) its machine is
away: its stop is recorded and is carried out when the machine registers
again. Never sent `stopped` for the request itself: a session is stopped
only once its machine says so.

error.description: Why it could not be stopped (`failed` only).

ProjectView.description:
A view as `GET /api/projects/:id/views` lists it: kept (`views/<name>.oui`)
or a draft (`views/drafts/<name>.oui`), its program as written, and the
components it names that CawCo's library does not have, which are left out
when it is drawn (the hub's parse, the same one the dashboard renders with).

dropped.description: Components the program names that the library does not have, by name: dropped, not invented.

kind.description:
Hub-originated: the projects changed (one was made or forgotten, or a
place was added or removed: a checkout joined, a delegate's workspace
opened or was archived): read `/api/projects` again.

Promoted.description: What `artifact_promote` answers: the project folder's commit, and the folder it wrote.

PropKind.description:
A prop's type in Storybook's SBType names (`argTypes[name].type.name`),
which decides its control: `enum` the variant control, `boolean`,
`string` and `number` their fields, `slot` content that is a pin
(`Snippet`, `ReactNode`, a Vue slot), the rest read-only. A `token-*`
kind is a prop typed with one of the design system's generated token
types ({@link TOKEN_TYPES}): its options are the system's names.

PropMeta.description:
One prop of a component as its framework's docgen reads it, in
Storybook's argTypes/PropertyMeta shape (spec §6): Svelte's by
svelte2tsx and TypeScript's checker, Vue's by vue-component-meta,
React's by react-docgen (react-docgen-typescript where a type is past
it).

defaultValue.description: Its default as the source writes it, like `"neutral"`; null when it has none.

options.description: An enum's values, or a token kind's names, in the order its type lists them.

ProposedBlock.description:
A draft view standing on a page as a proposed block: where it asked to
stand, and who drafted it. Keep places it there; Remove discards the
draft. It is no tab while it stands.

by.description: Who drafted it: "Caw", or a session's name.

position.description:
Its place in the page's order (every block of the page, hidden ones
included, counted from 0), or null: the page's end.

ProviderChoice.description:
One row of the account picker: a provider and one way its accounts sign
in. A provider that takes both OAuth and a key is two rows, as Claude is
(a subscription, and a Console organization).

harnesses.description: The harnesses that use an account of it.

kind.description: The account kind this row adds.

limits.description: Whether CawCo reads its limits ({@link LIMITED_PROVIDERS}).

provider.description:
Who bills the account: a provider id. `anthropic` is a Claude subscription
or Console organization, for Claude Code alone: Anthropic's terms keep its
OAuth tokens out of every other product. Any other is a provider pi or
OpenCode speaks, by pi-ai's id for it (`openai-codex` for a ChatGPT
subscription, `github-copilot`, `opencode-go`, `zai`…), or OpenCode's own
id for one pi-ai has no provider for (`zai-coding-plan`, a configured
`litellm`) — see {@link ProviderInfo}.

ProviderForecast.description:
A provider's accounts as a forecast: each account's windows, and which
account carries a person's new sessions (`yours`) and a session's
(`delegates`) from now to the relay's horizon.

provider.description:
Who bills the account: a provider id. `anthropic` is a Claude subscription
or Console organization, for Claude Code alone: Anthropic's terms keep its
OAuth tokens out of every other product. Any other is a provider pi or
OpenCode speaks, by pi-ai's id for it (`openai-codex` for a ChatGPT
subscription, `github-copilot`, `opencode-go`, `zai`…), or OpenCode's own
id for one pi-ai has no provider for (`zai-coding-plan`, a configured
`litellm`) — see {@link ProviderInfo}.

ProviderRouting.description:
One provider's routing. `yours` places the sessions a person starts;
`delegates` the ones a session starts.

provider.description:
Who bills the account: a provider id. `anthropic` is a Claude subscription
or Console organization, for Claude Code alone: Anthropic's terms keep its
OAuth tokens out of every other product. Any other is a provider pi or
OpenCode speaks, by pi-ai's id for it (`openai-codex` for a ChatGPT
subscription, `github-copilot`, `opencode-go`, `zai`…), or OpenCode's own
id for one pi-ai has no provider for (`zai-coding-plan`, a configured
`litellm`) — see {@link ProviderInfo}.

ProviderSigninChallenge.description:
A provider sign-in begun: a device code to enter on any device, where, and
until when (`expiresAt` from the provider's own device-code expiry); or,
for a provider with no device code, a link to authorise at, after which
the person pastes the code or redirect URL it ends on.

ProviderSigninResult.description:
How a provider sign-in (or a key) ended. `signed-in`: as `identity` (its
`email` said again for a screen; null when the provider names nobody), on
`plan` (ChatGPT's usage endpoint's `plan_type`, else the token's own claim;
null when nothing said). `mismatch`: it signed in as someone other than the
account already is, so the machine signed that store out again. `expired`:
the code lapsed before it was entered. `pending`: not entered yet; ask
again.

identity.description: Null when the provider's credential names nobody.

joined.description: Signed in as an account that already exists: it is that account's now.

kind.description: Daemon-originated: a session's coarse now-state, throttled to about once per second.

pruned.description: The pairing is gone (401 or 410) and the device with it.

status.description: HTTP status, or 0 when Cawrier could not be reached.

QuestionClosed.description: What `question_close` answers: the question, by its link, as it stands now.

QuestionsMovedFrame.description:
Hub-originated: a session closed one of its questions to the person
(`question_close`, taken or withdrawn): what a session's tree asked him
moved without anything in Needs you moving, so a screen listing a
session's questions (core session-questions.ts) reads them again.

RebalanceNotice.description:
What adding an account (or one coming back from its bench) set moving on
one machine, for the Accounts page: the running sessions moved between
turns off accounts forecast to run out, and the held sessions re-decided
at once. Kept by the hub until acknowledged (`id` is its notice id).

came.description: The accounts that came: `added`, newly signed in there; `back`, their bench ended.

held.description: The held sessions looked at again, by the account each was held on.

continued.description:
Always 0: nothing continues from a summary at a limit now. Sent only
because the TestFlight builds 20261015 and 20261015.3 require it, which
the hub's wire check holds to (packages/hub/scripts/openapi.ts); it
goes in the change that expires them.

running.description: Running sessions moved off an account forecast to run out, by account and target.

cacheKept.description: The cache came along (one organization, and a carry there keeps it).

left.description: Planned and owed to their turn's end: mid-turn, or their process still running, when looked at.

RecordCard.description: One card of a decided page's record.

chosen.description: Options picked, by id; empty when it was left open.

dials.description: Its dials' values, in order: a panel named as the card.

note.description: The person's note; empty when none.

settled.description: Who settled its pick when the person did not (core decides.ts): absent for his own.

still.description: The mockup's still in the chosen state, by its mockup's built output; null when there is none.

kind.description: Recovery found no live handle; stored conversations remain resumable.

RefusalVerdict.description:
What a check of an account Claude Code refused account-wide came to
(`POST /api/accounts/:id/refusal-check`, and the hub's hourly look):
`back` on every machine (`machines`) its refusal had signed out;
`refused` still, in `reason`'s words; `none`, no verdict (`why`), and it
stays out; or `not-refused`, nothing to check.

kind.description: Daemon-originated: one send did not go; its record fails and the session goes on.

domain.description:
The domain the asking page reached CawCo through, seen through a proxy
(a tunnel, Cloudflare): the lead line, the name's suggestion and the
take-over's entry name it. Null by IP, the tailnet or a name of the hub's.

RelayChoice.description: One machine step 1 offers when two or more could run the relay.

address.description: Its public address: an interface's, the hub's view of it, or STUN's.

lan.description: Behind a router: its address on the router's network, for the forwards.

RelayCreated.description: What creating a relay answers: the relay, and the routes a conversation may propose for it.

suggestedRoutes.description: Event routes for the project's routines, to propose to the owner (event_route_create), never made here.

RelayFrame.description: Daemon-originated: the stream relay on this machine, whole, on each change.

command.description: The command `why` names as its fix, word for word inside it: shown as code.

hostname.description: The DNS name its certificate is for, while one stands.

progress.description: How far an image pull is, while `state` is `pulling`.

reach.description: The relay's machine's own addresses, read as it goes live: where another fleet machine's browser reaches it without the internet.

why.description: Why it is `failed`, in DESIGN.md's error formula ({@link RELAY_FAILURES}).

RelayJourneyView.description:
The journey as the hub holds it, whole: what `GET /api/stream-relay`
answers (with the asking page's {@link RelayAnswer.domain}) and every
`stream_relay.journey` frame carries, so every place that draws the card
shows the same ticks.

answered.description:
The relay was offered and answered (Set up, or Later): the first-run
row's relay step stands ticked (home FirstRun), set up or not.

asks.description: Needs you holds its row: set up, not put away (Later, Done for now), and not yet live and proven from outside.

candidates.description: How many machines could run it, for the row's meta before a pick.

done.description: Live and proven from outside: the row's tick.

machine.description: The machine picked, or null before a pick.

open.description: Someone set it up (the setup card, Settings, a take-over through a domain); false before.

revision.description:
Its place in the hub's order of views: a page keeps none older than the
one it holds, since an act's answer can arrive after a frame computed
later.

steps.description: Every step that applies, in order, with where each stands.

summary.description: The relay once it has gone live, as Settings shows it; null before.

urls.description: The relay's URLs, for this screen's proof; empty while it is not live.

RelayMachine.description: The machine the relay runs on, as step 1 found it.

address.description: Its public address: an interface's, the hub's view of it, or STUN's.

lan.description: Behind a router: its address on the router's network, for the forwards.

RelayPortChip.description: One port's last STUN answer, as Settings' chips show it.

RelayPortName.description: One port the hub's health check asks, by its chip's words.

RelayPorts.description: What the relay's machine has bound: its plain listener on UDP and TCP 3478, and its TLS listener on TCP 5349 while a certificate stands.

tls.description: A certificate stands and TCP 5349 is bound: the TLS listener answers.

RelayReach.description:
The relay's machine's own IPv4 addresses (agent media-forwarding.ts
`machineAddresses`): its LAN ones (RFC 1918) and its tailnet ones
(100.64/10). Another fleet machine's browser names the relay at one of
them before its public address (agent relay-urls.ts), through the listener
published on every address.

RelayRuntimeNeed.description:
A VM's port forwarder that carries less than UDP and TCP (Colima's ssh
one carries TCP alone), with the sentence and the command that switch it
to one that carries both. Every port the relay takes is above 1024, so no
runtime, rootless or in a VM, must be let bind it.

command.description: The fix, one line for a terminal.

why.description: What is short and how to change it, in the error formula's words.

RelayStep.description:
One step on the path, by what it is and where it stands. A step that does
not apply to this machine is not in the list (the router on a machine with
a public interface, the runtime where its engine runs on the machine
itself, the certificate with no name).

state.description: `needs`: no Cloudflare token reaches the name's zone yet, and the step asks for one.

tokenWhy.description: Cloudflare refused the token pasted here: its words, under the token field.

why.description: Its failure, in the error formula's words.

state.description: `needs`: two or more machines could run it, `choices` the ask; `none`: no machine can.

answers.description: What the name answers instead, for `elsewhere`.

askedAt.description: When the hub last asked DNS (ms epoch), while it checks.

finding.description: What the name check last found while the name stands.

name.description: The name suggested, or the one that stands; empty when none is known yet (the field asks for one).

tokenWhy.description: Cloudflare refused the token, or the record: its words, the token field open under "Let CawCo add it".

at.description: When (ms epoch).

device.description: The device that proved it, or failed it.

outside.description: The device that failed it was outside the relay's network.

ports.description: The ports that answered it, "udp 3478, tcp 3478, tls 5349".

refused.description: It failed by a refused credential (a 401), not by no answer.

state.description: `inside`: it answered from a screen on the relay's own network only; `checking`: this screen asks now (drawn by the screen itself).
`needs`: the forwards to make, until a proof from outside answers; `done` once one has.

need.description: `needs` only: the forwarder to switch, as the machine's runtime read it.

command.description: The command `why` names as its fix, word for word inside it.

RelaySummary.description: The relay once it has gone live: Settings' summary.

endsAt.description: When the certificate ends (ms epoch), with a name.

name.description: Its name, or null when the name was skipped.

progress.description: How far an image pull is, while it pulls.

proven.description: Who proved it from outside and when, or null while nobody has.

whyCommand.description: The command `why` names as its fix.

RelayTry.description: A credential for this screen's proof (`GET /api/stream-relay/try`): good for 60 s.

RelayView.description: One relay as the hub answers it (times in ms epoch). Never its secret.

hasSecret.description: Whether a secret is set, and who made it: never the secret.

host.description: The machine whose Tailscale serves it: the hub's.

inbound.description: How events reach the project while it is or isn't live, in a sentence.

publicUrl.description: The public URL, once Funnel says it is live.

reason.description: The exact step or command when it isn't live; null when it is.

registered.description: Whether GitHub's webhook was registered by the hub (and is deleted with the relay).

repo.description: GitHub: the repository, `owner/repo`, whose webhook it is; null for other providers.

testedAt.description: When the provider's test delivery arrived.

schemaVersion.description: Database migrations this build carries; a build with fewer than the database holds is never installed.

sequence.description: First-parent commit count of the built commit; only grows, and no path installs a lower or equal one.

sessiondProtocol.description: The capability required by this build's agent from its process keeper.

Removed.description: What `artifact_delete` and the panel's Remove answer: the artifact removed, and what the session's panel shows now, or null for nothing.

removed.description: The artifact the call named, as it was resolved before it went.

RenderedBy.description: Which browser drew a canvas: the person's panel, or the stage's own.

RestartHold.description: One kind of work a restart would cut now, and what each piece is (a session, a call).

RestartHoldReason.description:
Kinds of work a restart of the agent or the hub would cut. A turn is not one:
the session keeper runs it, and the next agent takes it over where it stands.

- `custody`: the agent is still taking over the sessions the keeper holds.
- `starting`: a session start the agent is in the middle of.
- `image`: an image generation the agent is running.
- `workspace`: a delegate's workspace the agent is cutting or archiving.
- `command`: a command the hub asked the agent to run (a merge check).
- `tool-call`: a tool call the agent relays to its hub.
- `hub-tool-call`: a CawCo tool call the hub is answering, from any machine.
- `write`: a message or an answer the agent is handing to a harness.
- `opencode`: an OpenCode server operation the agent runs (a config apply,
  a session opening, an MCP change, a handoff between server generations).
- `opencode-send`: messages the agent holds for OpenCode, not yet handed over.

ResultArtifact.description: One thing an attempt handed in, as the review draws it.

RetiringKeeper.description: A keeper of an earlier build still holding sessions while the current one takes every new start.

kept.description: Processes in its unit CawCo did not start, while they keep it from going: its hand-over finishes once they end.

notAnswering.description:
It is there and gave no welcome on the updater's last look: it is left
as it is, and `sessions` is what it held when it last answered (0 when
it never did).

sessions.description: Its sessions, and any other process it holds (a workspace's boundary, an OpenCode server).

Revised.description:
What a decision page's revision (`statements`) answers: what it changed,
not the page. The person's picks are read with `artifact_read`.

broken.description: What it left broken on the picks and the links; absent when nothing.

cards.description: The cards it put in or rewrote, each by its link (`[question](cawco:decision/<artifact>/<card>)`), by id.

decisions.description: Its decisions now, by id, in page order.

dropped.description: Components the library does not have, dropped and never drawn.

held.description: Your change waits as this next version: your parent had opened the artifact, and their panel keeps the version they opened until they call artifact_show.

marked.description: What it changed on the page, each by its link (`[label](cawco:change/<artifact>/<anchor>)`).

moved.description: Decisions the revision added or took out, by id; a removed one's pick is kept.

routes.description: The route of each card it put in or rewrote, by the project's Who decides, by id; absent when no card on the page carries a kind.

statements.description: Statements by name: new, rewritten, and dropped because nothing reaches them.

RoutineMadeIn.description:
Where a routine was made: the session whose `routine_create` call made
it, and how its notice names that session.

RoutineRunState.description:
Where a routine's run is: queued behind a live run (an event's run, which
starts when the runs before it end), being started, running, ended, or
skipped (nothing started).

RoutineRunView.description:
One run, as the hub's routes and tools answer it (times in ms), with what
actually ran it: a delegate run's work item, or a conversation run's
session.

instanceId.description: A conversation run's session, once its harness read the run; null for a delegate run.

workItemId.description: A delegate run's work item; null for a conversation run, and before its work began.

RoutineSchedule.description: A routine's schedule as the person reads it: its cron in words, in its zone, and its next run.

nextAt.description: When the next scheduled run is due, ms epoch; null for a routine that is off.

RoutineTarget.description:
What a run starts: a fresh delegate, a fresh orchestrator (a session that
may delegate, in the project's checkout: routines.ts `fireOrchestrator`),
a message to the project's conversation, Caw, the project's memory curator
(memory.ts), a delegate in the `curator` role that only the hub makes, or
the unused skills and servers routine (hub unused-trim.ts), a delegate in
the `trimmer` role that only the hub makes too.

RoutineView.description: A routine, as the routes and tools answer it (times in ms), with its newest runs.

madeIn.description: Where a session made it; null for yours, the hub's, and those made before the hub kept where.

madeWhy.description: What the making turn said just before its call, one paragraph; null when it said nothing or a session did not make it.

mode.description: The mode a conversation run starts the project's conversation in when it has none; null: the project's.

nextRuns.description:
Its runs ahead, as the scheduler will start them (`nextRunsOf`): the next
week's, at most 288, epoch ms; a paused routine's too.

schedule.description: Its schedule in words, and its next run.

name.description: What the rule is called in the list, and in the reply the session reads.

pattern.description: The phrase to watch for, a regular expression, or a yes/no question, as `matchKind` says.

repeat.description:
Fire again on every later match. Off makes the rule fire once per session
and then go quiet.

reply.description: What the session is sent when the rule fires.

wholeWord.description: Phrase mode only: refuse matches that sit inside a longer word.

RuleDraft.description: A rule as it arrives from the dashboard, before the hub gives it an id.

name.description: What the rule is called in the list, and in the reply the session reads.

pattern.description: The phrase to watch for, a regular expression, or a yes/no question, as `matchKind` says.

repeat.description:
Fire again on every later match. Off makes the rule fire once per session
and then go quiet.

reply.description: What the session is sent when the rule fires.

wholeWord.description: Phrase mode only: refuse matches that sit inside a longer word.

RuleMatchKind.description:
How {@link Rule.pattern} is read.

- `phrase` / `regex` — text to find in what the session said.
- `meaning` — a yes/no question the hub puts to TypeSafe's Jev (directly
  with a TypeSafe key, or through OpenRouter) about what the session said; the rule fires when the answer
  is yes. Decided by the hub asynchronously, so nothing here matches it.

RuleScope.description:
What narrows a rule from "every session on the fleet" to some of them. Every
field is optional and they are ANDed; an empty scope is the default and means
everywhere. `model` is a substring test, so `opus` covers every dated build
of it.

areaId.description:
The area it fires in (core areas.ts): every project in it, as the rule
is read; with `projectId` too, a session must be in both.

delegateType.description: The delegate type the session was started as, by name.

harness.description: The harnesses cawco can spawn sessions on. Adding one is a new adapter.

role.description: Orchestrators (sessions holding `delegate`) or leaves, as fleet memory reads a role.

RuleStats.description: What the list needs to show about a rule without loading every session's state.

pending.description: Sessions that fired this rule and have not yet finished a turn without it.

RuleTiming.description:
When the reply is delivered.

- `turn` — the session has stopped and is idle, so the reply wakes it into a
  new turn. This is the one that makes a session keep working.
- `message` — queued the moment the assistant message that matched is
  complete; the session reads it at the next turn boundary without being
  interrupted.
- `immediate` — sent the moment the phrase appears mid-stream; the session
  reads it at its next step, a command it is running moved to the
  background.

RuleWatch.description: Which part of the session's output a rule reads.

RunningSession.description: One running session of a project, in tree order (parents first).

offline.description:
Its machine is not connected: it cannot be stopped now, and stops when
its machine is back.

parentId.description: The nearest running session it is a delegate of; null for a top session.

title.description: Its name as the rails give it (null: nobody named it; the client names it by its folder).

SchedulePreview.description: A schedule read back before it is kept: its runs ahead and its words.

ScratchWorktree.description: Creation provenance, stored by the agent and carried durably on its hub row.

SecretSet.description: A secret as a read says it: set. Never a string, so it is never a value that could be saved back as one.

SectionUndrawn.description:
A section a stage's render did not draw: its states file, whether the
render's sweep took it (a state read takes its own section alone), where
the sweep stood in it when the limit came (null: not begun), and its
first story, whose state read draws this section alone.

SendBack.description:
Where Send back puts a task waiting on you, and who takes it up there
(hub stages.ts `sendBackOf`).

kind.description: Hub-originated: a send's record, as it stands after its latest change.

SendMode.description:
How a send asks to be read: as a turn of its own, or as a note the next
turn folds in (`shouldQuery: false`). Into a running turn, either is read
at its next step, a command it is running moved to the background.

SendPayload.description: `send`: one turn of input for a live session's prompt stream.

attachments.description:
Text the user pasted rather than typed, kept out of `message` so the agent
can fold it into the turn as quoted material the model won't mistake for
the sentence around it; and files, by the hub's reference, which the
agent fetches onto the session's machine and names by path in `message`.

delivery.description:
This hand-off of the send to its machine, stamped by the hub each time it
hands the send on. A machine handing the send back (`held_send`) names
it, so a hand-back a later hand-off overtook is not owed twice.

from.description: The instance a fleet-originated send claims as its caller.

images.description: Images the turn carries: base64, with no `data:` URI prefix.

message.description: The user turn, under the uuid it keeps everywhere it is shown.

provenance.description:
Which page and tab sent it (the dashboard's `submitCommand`): the page's
client id and its tab's presence, which the hub's send line names, so a
send that landed on the wrong session is read against what its own tab
showed.

SendRecord.description:
THE ONE RECORD OF A SEND. The hub writes it when it accepts the send and is
its only writer after that: every change is stored, then sequenced into the
session's stream as a `send` frame, and a history read serves it beside the
entries. Every screen draws the send from this, live and after any reload.

acceptedAt.description: ISO-8601: when the hub took the send. The only clock its row shows.

anchor.description:
A failed send the harness never stored: the uuid of the last thing the
session said before it failed — an assistant frame, or a send it read.
Its row goes right after that. Absent when the hub knew of nothing the
session had said: its row then goes after the last row dated before
`acceptedAt`, or first when none is.

body.description:
Exactly what the sender submitted: its words, its pictures (as the hub's
media references) and pastes, and who it is from. What the agent adds on
the way to the harness (a worktree line) is not in it.

harnessId.description:
The id the harness stored the send under, where that is not its uuid:
opencode's message id, pi's entry id, and — for a send Claude joined into
another's record ({@link SessionMessage.joined}) — that record's uuid.

modeAsk.description: No permission mode to wake its session on: the page asks for one, and it goes again ({@link ModeAsk}).

readAt.description: ISO-8601: when its reader read it; absent until then.

reason.description: Why it failed, in the harness's words or the hub's.

refusal.description:
What refused it, when the hub did: the facts a screen offers the way
back from ({@link SendRefusal}). `reason` says it in words.

replaces.description: The failed send this one was sent in place of.

SendState.description:
Where a send stands, as the hub alone decides it: waiting for the harness
(`pending`), taken up by it (`read`), never going to be (`failed`, with
why), or sent again as another send (`replaced`).
