SentMessage.description:
A message sent to a session, by the reader or by cawco. `uuid` is its one
identity from the press to a reload: the dashboard's command id for a
reader's send, minted where the hub builds its own. The hub keeps one
{@link SendRecord} under it, and every copy of the message on every screen
is drawn from that record.

ServerStageState.description: A workspace preview's server: the command its preview names (`serve`).

dir.description: Where it runs from the clone's root ("." for the root itself): a sheet's toolchain root, a server's `cwd`.

message.description: Why it is in `error`, one sentence; none otherwise.

SessionAccountRead.description:
What a session's Claude Code says of its account at initialize, as it
starts: who it is signed in as (absent when nobody is) and its plan. Not
its models: Claude Code lists them relative to the session's own model (a
model it does not know is added as a "Custom model" row, an explicit id
replaces the alias row that runs it), so they are no account's catalog.

identity.description:
Who an account is: an email in an organization, the organization known by
its id (`orgId`), never its name, which is a display name: an org renamed
is the same org, and two orgs can share a name. Claude: as `claude auth
status --json` reports it (`email`, `orgName`, `orgId`). ChatGPT: the
access token's claims, read on the machine — the email
(`https://api.openai.com/profile`.email) and, as `organization` and its
id, the ChatGPT account id (`https://api.openai.com/auth`.chatgpt_account_id),
the workspace the subscription bills. Another OAuth provider: the email its
credential names, if any, and its provider id. A key: its last four
characters (`…a1b2`) and, as `organization` and its id, a fingerprint of
it (`key:` and the first 16 hex of its SHA-256), so the same key on two
machines is one account and the key itself never leaves them.

SessionAttachment.description:
One attachment a session's conversation carried, as Files lists them
(`GET /api/instances/:id/attachments`, newest first): a text pasted at
length, a file the hub stores, or a picture, read off the whole
transcript on the hub, whatever pages a reader has loaded.

at.description: When its message was, ISO-8601; null when the harness gave no time.

content.description: A text's words, for reading it in place.

id.description: Its message's id and its place within that message: the same however the list grows.

messageId.description: The message it rode, for Show in conversation (`?at=`).

name.description: A file's or text's name; a picture's is its place among the conversation's pictures ("Picture 3").

ref.description: Where the hub serves a file (`/api/files/<sha256>`); absent when the harness's copy names only part of its hash.

who.description: Who sent it: the person, or the session's agent.

SessionInstruction.description:
One scoped document a session launches with ({@link sessionTakes}): the
hub picks them for the session as it grants its launch
(`LaunchGrant.instructions`), and the harness puts each in its own
instructions, the part of every request a compaction keeps: Claude Code's
system prompt append ("System prompt and output style | Both still
apply", code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window, What survives
compaction), an OpenCode instruction entry ("6. Session-specific
instruction entries supplied through the API", among the initial
instructions, opencode.ai/v2/docs/instructions), a pi context file ("System
messages are prompt state, not conversation; the compaction entry carries
their replay", pi-coding-agent 1.0.1 compaction.js).

path.description: The document's path in the fleet's memory, which names it to the session.

SessionOrigin.description:
Who started a session, stamped by the hub as it starts from who asked,
never from what the start carried: `person`, a person's own start (the
New session form, a move); `delegate`, a `delegate` call (a work item,
a routine's run and a design check among them); `project`, started by
its project's events (the session they reach); `check`, an agent's `start_session`, a start
from a page in an agent's own browser, and the hub's own workers. Only a
person's sessions stand at a project's top in the rails; every other one
nests under the session that started it.

SessionPlan.description:
What `GET /api/instances/:id/plan` answers, and what the live frames keep
a client's copy equal to.

awayUnseen.description:
The spec's away notes (its `## Since HH:MM (you were away)` section,
core injected.ts `awayNotesOf`) changed since the person last saw them:
opened the plan, or had them recapped. `since` is the section's HH:MM.
Absent once seen, and while the spec has none.

changes.description: The person's latest changes to it, newest last.

needs.description:
The plan's own needs: each artifact of the session's in Needs you, by
id, that no open step's `waitsOn` names ({@link planNeedsOf}). One a
step names shows on that step. Absent when there are none.

orphanedComments.description: The person's step comments whose step's words are gone from the list, oldest step first. Absent when none.

source.description:
Always `cawco`: the steps are CawCo's list on every harness. Still sent
because the apps on TestFlight 20261015 through 20261018 decode it as
required (hub openapi.ts's wire check); it goes in the change that
expires those builds.

spec.description: The session's spec, once it has written one.

steps.description: CawCo's list: `todo_write`'s session scope, on every harness.

taskId.description: On a task attempt: the task.

todos.description: On a task attempt: the task's to-dos, nested and ticked as its file has them.

SessionPulse.description:
A coarse, now-state the rail draws without frames: what a session is doing
right now, folded on the daemon from the frames it is already pumping. It is
the *fallback* the dashboard reads for sessions it has not subscribed to —
open sessions still render the richer frame-fed state. `activity` is the same
three words the fleet view uses; `busy`/`runningSubagents` keep the finer
signals separate so a reader can still tell "blocked" from "working".

activity.description: Coarse now-state the rail draws without frames.

at.description: ms epoch of the last frame that changed this pulse.

currentTool.description: The tool the main loop is inside, addressed as the transcript addresses it.

SessionStreamEvent.description:
One event on a session's canonical stream. `seq` is hub-assigned, monotonic
per session, starting at 1 — and NO GAP is ever delivered: a client that
observes `seq > lastSeq + 1` re-subscribes with `afterSeq = lastSeq` instead
of applying the delta.

sessionId.description: The instance id — what the dashboard calls a viewId.

SessionStreamFrame.description:
What a session's stream carries: the changes each frame made to its
transcript, as the hub built them (`transcript-types.ts`), and its preview's
state. Raw frames never reach a dashboard; the hub folds them.

SetChangeTable.description:
One side of a change to a starting set, row by row, the never-called
first, then the longest unused. What joins is drawn with every session's
calls on the fleet; what leaves, with the set's own sessions' calls.

days.description: The window the count covers, in days.

set.description: The set, as the person knows it: "Cawco-Dev's starting set", "the build type's starting set".

SetItemRow.description: One skill or server a change moves into or out of a starting set, with the calls behind it.

lastAt.description: Its last call in the window, ms epoch; null when no session counted called it.

name.description: A skill as a listing names it (`plugin:skill`), a server by its fleet name.

sessions.description: How many of the sessions counted called it in the window.

SettingSource.description: Where a setting in effect came from: the project's own, its area's, or the fleet's.

SettingsInEffect.description:
A project's settings in effect, each with its source:

- `account`: the account its sessions start on when a start names none;
  null from the fleet is the fleet's routing.
- `accountAtLimit`: what its sessions on that account do at its limit, from
  whoever set the account (the fleet's is `wait`, with no account to wait on).
- `cawMode`: the permission mode its conversation starts in; null from the
  fleet is the mode last chosen for the harness on that machine.
- `cap`: what it may spend in a period; null from the fleet is no cap.
- `onCap`: what reaching the cap does.

account.description: A setting in effect, and where it came from.

accountAtLimit.description: A setting in effect, and where it came from.

cap.description: A setting in effect, and where it came from.

cawMode.description: A setting in effect, and where it came from.

onCap.description: A setting in effect, and where it came from.

Settled.description: What `settle` answers: the card, the option it holds now, and who settled it.

SettledBy.description: A pick the hub wrote for a card from `settle`: by which member of Who decides (core decides.ts), why, and on what sources.

name.description: The member's name as it was then: "Advisor".

runs.description: What it ran on then: "Claude Code · Opus 5.5"; null when nothing names it.

session.description: The session that settled it, by id.

sources.description: Links it rests on; common practice's name one at least.

SheetImport.description: One of a story file's imports, as its sheet's weight names it.

brings.description: The modules it imports directly that bring the most, each with all it brings: where its weight enters.

file.description: The module it resolves to, from the toolchain root.

specifier.description: As the story file writes it, like `#lib/cawco/client.svelte`.

via.description:
The modules under it where most of its weight enters, from the toolchain
root, each bringing at least half of the one before: a fixture's
`home/CawPanel.svelte`, then what that brings. Empty when it is its own
weight or spreads it evenly.

SheetMeta.description: What a story file's default export says every story shares: its args, and the component each mounts unless it names its own.

component.description: The component, from the toolchain root; null when the meta names none the stage could resolve.

title.description: CSF's `title`, the section's path (`Settings/Pairing`); null when it has none.

SheetRead.description: A sheet as its stage reads it: its stories, its meta, and the props of each component they mount.

SheetStageState.description: A sheet's stage: the project's own dev toolchain on its toolchain root.

dir.description: Where it runs from the clone's root ("." for the root itself): a sheet's toolchain root, a server's `cwd`.

message.description: Why it is in `error`, one sentence; none otherwise.

SheetWeight.description:
What a sheet loads, read from the stage's Vite module graph from its story
file: the project's modules (its source and any package Vite serves file
by file) and Vite's prebundled deps apart, which the browser keeps by
their `?v=` address. `heaviest` is the story file's imports that bring
the most project code, each with all it brings that no earlier import
did: the import to cut. Vite transforms a module when a page asks for it,
so a sheet has a weight once a view has loaded it.

budget.description: The budget a component's states file keeps (the component-canvas skill's); a screen is judged against the page's ceiling instead.

bytes.description: Project code: its modules and their transformed bytes.

cut.description: Where to cut, one sentence: the import, or the seam in the component when it is the component's own; null under budget.

Shown.description: What `artifact_show` answers: {@link Opened}, with the artifact's link, `[title](cawco:artifact/<id>)`, which the agent names it by and its tool row draws.

ShownFile.description: A file a sent turn names, as its transcript row shows it.

ref.description: Present when the line named the whole hash (the hub's own record).

SignInFault.description: One of a machine's own sign-ins its provider refused ({@link HarnessReport.signInFaults}).

at.description: When the refusal came, epoch ms.

provider.description: The provider's id in the harness (`anthropic`).

words.description: What the home says, whole: what was refused, and the fix ({@link opencodeSignInFaultWords}).

expiresAt.description: When the provider's page stops taking this sign-in's answer, epoch ms.

SigninKind.description:
How an account of a kind signs in on a machine. `paste-code`: a link to
authorise at, and a code pasted back (Claude Code's `claude auth login`).
`device-code`: a code entered on any device at the provider's page while
the machine waits. `api-key`: a key typed once in the dashboard and relayed
to the machines picked.

SigninState.description: Where an account stands on one machine.

SkillVersion.description: One superseded version of one skill, as a listing reads it — without its files.

createdAt.description: When it was kept, ISO, as the answer carries it.

source.description: `fleet` for the hub's own row; `machine:<machineId>` for an edited copy an overwrite took off it.

SlashCommand.description: What the composer's `/` menu renders. Replaces the SDK's `SlashCommand`.

builtin.description:
Claude Code's own command, as its SDK marks it (`SlashCommand.builtin`,
claude-agent-sdk 0.3.296): "Rows can share a name: when a marked row
carries it, /name runs that one, and an unmarked row is the one /name
runs only when no marked row shares its name." Absent on every other
harness.

kind.description: What the harness says this is, when it knows. Absent → derived from the name and the session's skill list.

SourceFacts.description:
Where an install fetches from, as the hub read it when the call was
proposed (hub source-facts.ts): a skill's source, a marketplace's.

at.description: The source as read: `github.com/owner/repo`, `npm package`, `/path on machine`.

since.description: When it first came out: the repository's creation, the package's first publish (ISO).

skill.description:
A skill read from a folder on a machine before the person is asked: what
its SKILL.md declares and every file the install carries, by path.

files.description: Every file, by path, with the hash of its content.

hash.description: The hash of every file together: what the approval pins.

unknown.description: Why there are no facts: a source that carries none, or the registry's answer.

weeklyDownloads.description: The package's npm downloads in the last week.

Sourced.T_1.description:
What reaching a project's spend cap does (Projects spec §5.3): `pause`
starts no new attempts at its tasks, `quiet` books what would wake its Caw
without a turn, `both` does both. The fleet has a default (Configure,
Spend); a project may set its own.

SpawnPayload.description:
`spawn`: start a session on a harness. `harness` chooses the adapter; `options`
rides through to that adapter verbatim — only the callbacks the agent must own
itself (`canUseTool`/permission hooks, abort) are filled in on arrival, since
functions do not survive the wire. `resume` is the harness-neutral way to
re-open or fork a stored session; `persistSession: false` asks for a session
that is never stored (a spin-off's transcript).

account.description:
The account the session must run on, picked by whoever started it (the
dashboard, `delegate`, `start_session`). The hub refuses a pick the
session's machine, project or task does not allow, and never forwards
this field: what reaches the machine is {@link accountDir}.

accountDir.description:
The account the hub placed the session on, and so the store it runs
from on the machine: Claude Code in the account's own
`~/.cawco/accounts/<id>/claude`, never the machine's `~/.claude`; pi on a
runtime whose `openai-codex` sign-in is the account's
`~/.cawco/accounts/<id>/pi/auth.json`; OpenCode in the account's own
server, whose `XDG_DATA_HOME` (and so OpenCode's own store, holding the
account's credential alone) is `opencode-accounts/<id>` beside the
session credentials, hidden from every workspace boundary.
A launch learns it as it starts, from the hub's {@link LaunchGrant}, and
runs on that alone; a reattach is sent it, as the account its process
already runs on. Never set by a client. A Claude launch without one (or
a {@link homeLoginMove}) is refused on the machine; a pi or OpenCode
launch without one runs from the machine's own stores.

bootstrap.description:
Start from a repository instead of a directory that is already there: the
agent clones `repo`, a git URL on any host ({@link isGitUrl}), with plain
git into a subdirectory of `baseDir` and runs the session in the clone.

clean.description:
Start the session clean: its model sees the harness's own base prompt,
the tools it needs to work in CawCo and its first message, and none of
the instruction context (the fleet's and the repository's instruction
files, CawCo's memory documents and server instructions, skills,
plugins, hooks and the harness's own memory). A starter asks for it (the
New session form, `delegate`); the hub keeps it on the session's row
({@link InstanceRow.clean}) and puts it, with {@link fence}, on every
spawn of that row, whatever the caller sent. A harness that cannot start
clean is refused (core `cleanStartRefusal`).

delegateType.description:
The delegate type it was started as: its name, and the project whose
catalog it came from (none: the fleet's). The hub keeps both on the row.

denyTools.description:
Tools this session may never call, beyond whatever the harness already
denies. Set by a resolved {@link DelegateType}'s own `denyTools`; the
claude adapter merges it into the `disallowedTools` it already assembles.

effort.description:
How hard that model thinks, and how much it spends doing it. Hoisted for
the same reason again — and it is the third setting a `setEffort`
{@link ControlPayload} can still move mid-session. Named, it is the
session's chosen effort from then on ({@link InstanceRow.chosenEffort});
absent, the hub starts the process at the one already chosen, or, when
nobody chose, leaves the level to the harness, which is not the same as
asking for its default: only the model knows which stops it has.

fence.description:
This spawn is a project's memory curator or a fleet-watch triage run (a
`curator` or `overseer` row): the machine gives it CawCo's MCP server
and no other. Set by the hub alone, on every launch of such a row, and
never taken from a caller.

harness.description:
Which harness runs the session. Every start names it: the hub refuses one
that does not (`enforceRowSessionKey`), and the agent starts none without
it. Optional on the wire only until TestFlight 20261015, 20261015.3,
20261017 and 20261018 are expired (the app they hold declares it
optional); then it is required here.

homeLoginMove.description:
The machine's own Claude Code login is moving into this account
(`POST /api/accounts/move-login`) and has not moved yet, so this Claude
session runs on that login: Claude Code with no `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, in
the machine's own store, where the credential still is. Granted by the
hub alone, as a Claude launch with no {@link accountDir} starts
({@link LaunchGrant}), and only while that move is pending. A machine
that has moved the login by the time the launch starts runs the session
in the account's dir instead.

hostScratch.description:
A host-scope work item's session (hub work-items.ts `startHost`): the id
of its host workspace, whose scratch dir (core paths/workspace.ts
`workspaceScratchDir`) the machine makes, `outputs/` in it, and gives its
commands as `TMPDIR`, though they run on the host with no boundary.
What it leaves in `$TMPDIR/outputs/` the hub copies into its project's
folder (core harness.ts `CONTROL_HOST_OUTPUTS`). Set on each
spawn of such a session, as {@link workspace} is on a bounded one's, and
on no other.

ingested.description: Hub ingest cursor for a recovery sent after the registration handover.

instructions.description:
The fleet's role-scoped memory documents this session loads, in path
order: the hub picks them for its role and project as it grants the
launch ({@link LaunchGrant}), and the harness puts them in the session's
own instructions. Never set by a client; a reattach launches nothing and
keeps what its process started with.

keepAliveTurn.description: The in-flight maintenance send a surviving Claude process is answering.

mayStart.description:
The delegate types this session may start ({@link MayStart}): `["any"]`
an orchestrator's; any other list a leaf's, which never gets the
spawning tools but `delegate` (for a list that names a type), and whose
every other start the hub refuses. Set by the `delegate` call's
`may_start`, else its type's. Absent on a session nobody delegated (a
mainline session may always delegate).

model.description:
Which model answers, from the session's first turn. Hoisted for the same
reason as `permissionMode`. Absent leaves the choice to the harness.

options.description: Harness-specific spawn options, passed through verbatim.

parent.description:
The session that started this spawn (a delegate's parent, or the caller
of `start_session`): the child nests under it in every rail, and
`toolUseId` names the delegating tool call so the parent transcript can
render the round trip. Absent on a spawn a person asked for.

permissionMode.description:
How the session answers tool permissions. Hoisted out of `options` because
it is the one option the user keeps choosing — and the only one they can
still change afterwards, with a `setPermissionMode` {@link ControlPayload}.

persistSession.description: `false` asks the harness never to store this session's transcript.

processGeneration.description: Hub-owned launch identity, retained when reattaching a surviving process.

projectId.description: The project this session was started from, when it was started from one.

reattachOnly.description: Existing custody only: `busy` recovers active turns; `inspect` only reports them.

relaunch.description:
The process the session runs in is replaced, though the spawn resumes
its own conversation: it moves to another account, or starts again on a
permission mode its harness only takes at launch. Without it, a resume
for a session the machine carries is a recovery of that process, and
the process is kept.

requestId.description:
Correlates the `control_result` frame the agent answers the spawn with, once
the session is in place.

resume.description:
Re-open (or fork) a stored session. `sessionKey` is the harness's own
session id; `fork` reads the origin conversation into a new one; `atMessage`
resumes through that assistant turn in Claude; OpenCode reverts from
the selected user turn. A fork includes its anchor in either harness.

role.description:
The toolset the session runs in, written on its row at this first spawn
and kept there: a delegate type's `role` is its work item's. Absent: the hub derives it (`delegate` or `worker`).

schedulesToParent.description:
A schedule this session makes that would outlive it goes to its parent:
it is refused `routine_create` (hub roles.ts `makesRoutines`), so Claude
Code's durable CronCreate, which writes `<cwd>/.claude/scheduled_tasks.json`
and fires in whichever session next runs in that folder, is refused too,
with words that send it to its parent (agent claude.ts). Set by the hub
alone, from the session's row, on every spawn of it.

scratch.description:
A spin-off (NEW.md §1): throwaway work. `worktree` runs the session in a
detached git worktree of `baseCwd` (the spawn's `cwd` when absent) so the
experiment cannot touch the checkout the mainline session is using.

scratchWorktree.description: Creation provenance, stored by the agent and carried durably on its hub row.

skills.description:
Skill names to load natively before the first prompt. Each harness loads
them via its own mechanism — opencode sends `/skill` commands, claude pushes
them into the input stream — so the delegate session sees the skill the same
way it would if the user had typed the slash command.

spawnedBy.description:
The session a hub job spawns for (a continuation's summariser and its
new session, on the person's ask): provenance for account placement,
not nesting. Unlike {@link parent}, it neither nests the child nor
routes reports, since no session started it.

startingSet.description:
The exact skills and MCP servers the session starts with
({@link import ("./delegate-types").StartingSet}): its delegate type's
set, with CawCo's own skills and server and the skills its start named
({@link skills}) joined. Set by the hub alone: resolved as its row first
opens, kept on that row, and put on every spawn of it, so a wake or
restore starts with the set its first spawn had. Absent: everything
installed.

title.description:
What the session is for, one line — a delegate's brief headline. Display
only.

workspace.description:
The workspace whose boundary every shell command of this session runs
inside. Set on each spawn of a work item's session — the first, and every
restore, revive and relaunch after it — and on no other session. A
machine that cannot hold the boundary refuses the spawn and says why.

SshJoinJob.description: `GET /api/machines/ssh/:id`: one SSH add, as the hub holds it in memory.

hubUrl.description:
The hub as the machine reaches it, `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`: the port on
its loopback the hub's connection carries to the hub. Empty until that
connection is up.

lines.description:
Everything the SSH session printed, stdout and stderr in arrival order.
A step line ({@link INSTALL_STEP_PREFIX}) means it has signed in: the
remote command prints one before anything else it does.

machineId.description: From the `joined as` line, once it has been printed.

passwordProblem.description:
Never sent: declared while an installable app reads it (TestFlight
20261018), as the wire check (hub scripts/openapi.ts) counts a property
gone from the schema as gone from what that app receives. A password ssh
refused is the sign-in `step` now, in ssh's words. It goes once no
installable app reads it.

state.description:
`done` means the script exited 0 and the hub has the machine online;
`stopped`, that the person stopped it and its `ssh` is gone.

SshPasswordProblem.description: A password add's refusal as the shipped apps read it (TestFlight 20261018): the hub no longer sends one.

color.description: Its mark's colour (stages.md `color:`); none: the muted ink.

icon.description: Its mark's glyph (stages.md `icon:`); none: no mark but its kind's.

StageCloneFrame.description:
The daemon's word that a place's stage clone (agent `stage-clone.ts`) is
cut and in step, sent on each use: the hub files it as a workspace of the
stage kind (schema `workspaces.stageFor`), which its retire sweep settles
once the place's stage sleeps.

id.description: The clone's workspace id (core workspace-policy.ts `stageCloneId`).

place.description: The place whose sheets' stage runs in it.

repoRoot.description: The repository root of the checkout it was cut from.

StageError.description:
A section's problem as the stage host keeps it (its kind), and the doc's
`meta.stage.errors` carries it to the panel and the agent's read alike:
the file from the toolchain root (a missing states file, or the module
that doesn't compile), 1-based line and column when Vite's payload has
them, the stage's words (a missing file's) or Vite's message and code
frame, and the states files whose section it stops, which the hub files
it under.

kind.description: Always sent; optional on the wire, so an app built from this reads a hub from before it.

sheets.description: The states files (from the toolchain root) whose section it stops: a missing one itself, else each whose sheet imports the module.

StageFrame.description: The daemon's word on each change of a stage: every artifact of the workspace's that previews its port hears it.

port.description: The port it serves on, in the workspace's network: a sheet's stage's or a preview's server's.

StageState.description:
A stage as the hub keeps it in each of its artifacts' docs (`meta.stage`),
as the daemon states it: a sheet's, with the toolchain it runs, or a
workspace preview's server's.

StageStatus.description:
Where a stage is: `starting` its first start, `waking` a start after
sleep, `live` serving, `error` it could not start or failed its restarts,
`asleep` stopped for want of a viewer, started again on the next open.

StageUnreached.description:
The hub's word that a canvas's stage couldn't be reached by its last read
(the doc's `meta.unreached`, which the panel and the agent's read both
say): the hop that failed, in the preview proxy's kinds; why, in the hub's
words; and since when, the first read that failed since one that reached
it. A read that reaches the stage, or the daemon's next word of it, takes
it away.

StagesSource.description: Where a project's stages come from (StagesView `source`).

StagesTemplateView.description: A template the dashboard offers: its stages, and the stages.md it writes.

StagesView.description: A project's stages as the dashboard reads them.

decisionStarters.description:
What an empty Decisions tab offers to ask Caw for: the project's open
choices to lay out as a decision page (project-starters.ts), in that
order; none while Jev is off.

problems.description: What is wrong with stages.md, one sentence each; stages, moves and views are empty while there is any.

source.description:
`file`: the project's stages.md; `template`: it has none and was set up
as the code template, which the hub reads in its place; `none`: it is
not set up yet (no stages.md, no template), and it has no stages.

template.description: The template the stages are, word for word, if any.

Stall.description:
A session stopped at its account's limit, as its tray chip and
`delegate_list` say it (core `accountsWords.stalled`): the words, and
when it carries on (epoch ms): the reset it waits for.

stale.description: Held past the cutoff: nothing carries it on until a person or its parent writes (at-limit.ts `goneStale`).

StarterSource.description:
One thing a starter comes from: a task id, a thread id (from before
conversations were sessions, kept for starters stored then), a folder path, a
commit sha, a routine id, or an event source and kind (`github:acme/site
issue.opened`).

StartingSet.description:
What a session starts with (tsk-329): an allowlist of skills, each named
as a session's listing names it (a plugin's as `plugin:skill`), and of MCP
servers by their fleet name. The hub adds CawCo's own skills and server to
every set (hub starting-set.ts), so a type names neither. A session's set
is fixed as it starts: a later change applies to sessions started after it.

StatementChange.description: What a revision changed, by statement name: new ones, rewritten ones, and those it dropped (unreachable now).

StatusOption.description: One option of a GitHub Project's single-select Status field.

id.description: GitHub's option id (`ProjectV2SingleSelectFieldOption.id`).

StopPayload.description: `stop`: interrupt and close a live session, as the hub sends it to its machine.

claimedSessionIds.description: Addresses claimed by other rows; only unclaimed server runners make a legacy read ambiguous.

discard.description: Explicitly abort unadopted custody too, then tear down spin-off resources.

forget.description:
The hub forgets the session once this stop is confirmed (its end is a
delete or a transcript delete): the machine lets go of what it kept for
the session to be reattached, its browser door among it.

from.description: The instance a fleet-originated stop claims as its caller; the hub honours the call only when the target is that instance's own delegate.

harness.description:
The row's harness, which ends its process and its server custody without
adoption. The hub names it on every stop it sends a machine, and the
agent ends nothing without it; a dashboard's or an app's ask is a
{@link StopRequest}. Optional on the wire only until TestFlight 20261015,
20261015.3, 20261017 and 20261018 are expired (the app they hold sends
this type); then it is required here.

processGeneration.description: The row's launch identity, including a held process not yet attached.

requestId.description: Correlates the `control_result` frame confirming stop/discard or its failure.

scratchWorktree.description: Creation provenance, stored by the agent and carried durably on its hub row.

stopSequence.description: Connection-local hub order, echoed by reads begun after receipt.

ended.description: Positive server-session receipt; absent receipts cannot confirm OpenCode.

kind.description: Authoritative daemon confirmation, never merely delivery of a stop request.

StoredFrame.description: Hub-originated: Recent's stored transcripts, whole, on each change.

StoredRecent.description:
What Recent draws of the transcripts the machines store, kept by the hub
off each machine's catalog (hub stored-recent.ts): `GET /api/stored`, then
each `stored` frame, whole.
- `rows`: the sessions wrapping a stored transcript in a project's folder
  that the board no longer lists, where the session at the top of their
  chain is the person's own ({@link personsOwn}), each with the sessions
  it nests under, as the board hands a row.
- `transcripts`: the transcripts in a project's folder that a person
  started (`NeutralSessionInfo.startedBy`) and no session of the hub
  wraps: transcripts run outside CawCo.

StoredTranscript.description: A transcript stored on a machine, in a project's folder there ({@link StoredRecent}).

projectId.description: The project whose folder holds it most closely (core `projectAt`).

Story.description:
One named export of a story file: a story, by its export's 1-based place,
with its `args` as the file writes them. A literal arg (a string, number,
boolean, null, or an array or object of those) is its value; any other
(a fixture import, a function) is in `code`, its source text, and the
inspector shows it read-only.

code.description: Args whose value is code, not a literal: their source text.

component.description: The story's own component, from the toolchain root, when it names one apart from the meta's.

display.description: Its CSF `name`, the name it is shown by where its export can't hold it (an apostrophe); null when it writes none.

form.description: Its form, from `parameters.viewport` (the story's, else the meta's); null when it names none.

formUnread.description: Why its `parameters.viewport` can't be read from its states file (an imported const, code), naming the story; null when it reads or names none. Its frames say it as their failure.

from.description: The story its flow move starts from (`from`), when it declares one with a `play`.

label.description: Its doc comment in plain words, the frame's label; null when it has none (`unnamed`).

play.description: Whether it has a `play`: with `from`, a flow move.

readOnly.description:
Why the inspector can't write this story's args, when it can't; null
when it can. `read` false: the story file builds it with code the
reader can't follow (an imported helper, a computed value), so
`component` and `args` say nothing of it, though it mounts all the same;
`reason` says its props can't be read and why. `read` true: its
component and args were read through a spread or a local helper,
shared code a pin changes. Its words are core words/story-read.ts.

records.description: The list arg its record sets are cut from (`parameters.records`); null when it names none.

tags.description: Its CSF `tags`, as the file writes them (`failure`: an error state).

pinnedAccountId.description: The account `pinned` names; ignored by the other strategies.

StreamBacklog.description:
Hub → client when the requested gap is inside its ring: events contiguous
ascending from `afterSeq + 1`. The client applies them in order, then
follows live deltas.

StreamDelta.description: Hub → client, live fan-out of one sequenced event.

StreamHeartbeat.description:
Client → hub, and the hub's answer, the same shape: "are you there?" and
"yes", sent at once. A client sends one every
{@link HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS}; when nothing at all arrives on the socket
within {@link HEARTBEAT_DEADLINE_MS} of it, the socket is dead though open
(a frozen hub, a dropped route that sent no FIN), and the client closes it,
reconnects and reads again. Application messages, not WebSocket pings:
URLSession rejects the pong Bun sends on a permessage-deflate socket
(NSPOSIXErrorDomain 100, "Protocol error"), so no client sends a ping.

StreamRelayState.description: The relay as its machine runs it.

StreamReset.description:
Hub → client when the gap is unrecoverable (older than the ring holds):
an honest refusal, never a partial replay. The client reads the newest
transcript page again and resumes from the `seq` it carries.

StreamServerMessage.description: Everything the stream protocol can put on the dashboard socket.

StreamSubscribe.description:
Client → hub. `afterSeq` present is a resume ("I have up to here — replay the
rest"): a client sends it with the `seq` its transcript page was read at, and
when a delta skips a seq on the same socket. Absent is a fresh join ("start
me from now").

Never across a connection: the hub numbers a session's stream in memory,
from 1 again when its process restarts, so a cursor from the socket before
may name another process's events. A client that reconnects reads each
transcript it follows again, and that read's page subscribes it.

StreamUnsubscribe.description:
Client → hub: this socket no longer follows the session, so the hub sends
it none of the session's events from here on. Sent when nothing the client
shows on that socket follows the session any more (every pane, the peek,
a delegate card); a `stream.subscribe` follows it again. A session the
socket does not follow is no change. The session's plan, when the socket
follows it alone (`plan.follow`), is not this message's.

SupportedCommands.description:
What {@link CONTROL_SUPPORTED_COMMANDS} answers, on every harness: the
session's `/` menu. A harness with no slash commands (pi) answers an empty
list, never nothing, so the menu reads one shape whoever answered.

SweepAt.description: Where a stage's sweep of a canvas stands: the section's states file, its step, and the story a move plays.

SweepStep.description: A step of a stage's sweep of one section: its module loaded, its frames' first draw, its states probed, a move played, its report posted.

TabNamed.description:
What the hub says a tab's id names (`POST /api/instances/named`): a tab
kept from an earlier visit, or an address, may name a session by its full
id, its short id, a former id, its harness key or a stored conversation's
key, or name nothing at all.
- `session`: the id the session is read by (`id`), the asked one or
  another.
- `none`: no session, stored conversation or ask goes by it.
- `unknown`: the hub can't tell now (the machine it names, or one it had
  to ask, is away or did not answer).

TailnetHttps.description: What `GET /api/tailnet-https` answers, and the `tailnet.https` frame carries.

command.description: The command the first step that stands runs on the hub's machine, for `operator` and `port`.

host.description: The hub's machine, by its hostname.

name.description: The machine's tailnet name (`machine.tailnet.ts.net`), once its tailnet names it.

step.description: What the person does next, while `needs`: the first of `steps` not done.

steps.description: Every step on the path, in the order to take them, while `needs`.

TailnetHttpsFrame.description:
Hub-originated: HTTPS on the hub machine's tailnet name changed state (hub
tailnet-https.ts): a step came to need the person, they took it, or the
name began or stopped answering. Every dashboard takes it at once, so its
onboarding row in Needs you shows the step that stands, or ticks.

TailnetHttpsTodo.description:
One step of the path to HTTPS, as the hub last read it: every step that
applies to this machine, done or not, so the person sees the whole path at
once and each step ticks as the hub finds it taken.

command.description: The command it runs on the hub's machine, for `operator` and `port`.

TailnetOrigin.description:
A session's preview origin on the tailnet name, beside its port
({@link PreviewAddress}): `origin` is `https://<name>:<port>`, and `hosts`
every host a client reaches the hub's machine by over the tailnet (its
tailnet addresses, its full name and its short one). A client that reached
the hub by one of them loads the preview from `origin`: on those
addresses the port answers HTTPS alone.

TakenSendFrame.description:
Daemon-originated: a send handed over again that its session has taken
already (agent taken-sends.ts). No turn started on it; its record is read,
and no turn follows that read.

TaskAttempt.description: One attempt at a task: a work item whose task it is, as a task read shows it.

endedAt.description: When it ended, ms epoch; null while it is live.

endedHow.description:
How it ended when it did not land, in a sentence the task shows beside
its Failed or Stopped badge: failed, the first line of what the hub
reported (`It failed without a reason.` when nothing was); cancelled,
`Stopped by <who>` (`Stopped` when the hub did not hear who). Null while
live and once done.

headline.description:
What its session said it did, in one or two sentences: its
`finish_item`'s headline. Null until an attempt finishes that way.

result.description: What its session handed in (`task_result`); null while it has not.

startedAt.description: When it was filed, ms epoch.

waitedOn.description: The cards and pins it was dispatched on, with the value each settled with then.

TaskComment.description: One entry of a task's `## Comments`, written only by the hub (tasks.ts `comment`).

at.description: When it was written, ms epoch: on its source, for one carried from there.

via.description:
Set when it was written on an outside source, as its heading names it
(its author's login, the source, its URL); the hub's `external_comments`
row adds its author's picture and when it was edited (tasks.ts). The
board draws the words under `via.author` with the source's mark and a
link to `via.url`.

TaskCommentAuthor.description: Who wrote a comment, as its entry's heading says: the hub's actor.

id.description: The session's instance id, or the approved action's; null when none.

mover.description: The mover they wrote as (`you`, `session`, …); null when the heading names none it knows.

name.description: The commit author's name: you, Caw, the session's title.

TaskHistory.description: A task's history as the API answers it: every commit to its file, oldest first.

path.description: Its file's path, or the last one it had.

state.description: `live`: on the board; `archived`: in tasks/archive/; `deleted`: its file deleted, its history kept.

id.description: The session's instance id (a session, the project's conversation), or the approved action's id; null when the commit names none.

mover.description: The mover the change was checked as; null, unknown, for a commit with no `CawCo-Mover` trailer (a hand edit, folder_write, the folder editor, one made before the hub wrote trailers).

name.description: The commit's author: you, Caw, the session's title as it was, hub, approved action.

TaskHistoryEvent.description: One commit to a task's file, as its history shows it.

at.description: When, ms epoch, by commit time.

path.description: The file's path once the commit was made: a rename's or an archive's new path.

reason.description: Why, when the change said: a close reason, the hub's cause (`attempt 5fd1e189 started`).

stage.description: The stage it went from and to; from is null for a new task. Null when the stage did not move.

what.description: What changed, in the commit's words: `stage draft → review`, `update title`, `tick td-2`.

TaskHistoryKind.description:
`created`: its file added. `moved`: a stage move. `changed`: fields,
to-dos or edges, through the hub. `commented`: a comment added through the
hub. `comment_edited`: a comment carried from an outside source, its words
changed there and rewritten in place by the hub (tasks.ts `editComment`).
`edited`: its file changed by a commit the hub's task code did not
make (a hand edit, folder_write); the hub putting back what one wrote
around it is `changed`, in words that say so. `archived`: its file moved
into tasks/archive/, or added there (a merged project's archived task);
`unarchived`: back out of it. `renamed`, `deleted`:
its file.

TaskLinkSummary.description: A link as a task's line on the board carries it: the card draws its mark and ref.

state.description: Its state as the source last said it; null until the item was read.

problems.description: Files in tasks/ the hub could not list as tasks, one sentence each.

stagesProblems.description: What is wrong with stages.md, one sentence each; empty when it reads.

TaskResult.description:
What a task's newest finished attempt handed back, read whole on a task's
own read (never on the list: a report runs to pages): its session's report
of what it did, which is how an attempt presents its result whatever the
work, beside the outputs it handed in (`assets/<task>/`).

at.description: When the attempt finished, ms epoch.

headline.description: Its `finish_item`'s headline, one or two sentences; null when it gave none.

TaskSummary.description: One task as a list shows it: the index's row, and what its attempts and edges say.

archivedAt.description: When its file moved into tasks/archive/, ms epoch; null while it is not archived.

builtOn.description: A done task's cards and pins that moved since its attempt was dispatched on them.

closeReason.description: The reason given with the move into the done or dropped stage it is in; null when none or open.

completedAt.description: When it moved into the done stage it is in, ms epoch; null while it is not in one.

createdAt.description: When the commit that first added its file landed, ms epoch.

createdBy.description: Who made the commit that first added its file; null while no commit has it.

droppedAt.description: When it moved into the dropped stage it is in, ms epoch; null while it is not in one.

duplicateOf.description: The task it repeats (`duplicate_of`); null when none.

fields.description: The fields its file carries beyond a task file's own that hold one scalar (`priority: high`), as written.

foundIn.description: The task or pin it was found in (`found_in`); null when none.

heldBy.description: The ancestor whose live attempt coordinates it, holding it from the hub's dispatch; null when none.

kind.description: The kind of its stage; null when its stage is not one of the project's.

lastAttemptFailed.description:
Its newest attempt failed, and it is not done or dropped since. The
failure is its starter's business (the session that started it, or the
project's conversation for the dispatcher's), who hears the report: never the person's
Needs you. It keeps the task off the dispatcher's frontier until someone
starts or retries it.

lastAttemptStopped.description:
Its newest attempt was cancelled (stopped), and it is not done or dropped
since: no failure, and off the frontier as a failed one is. Who stopped
it is its attempt's `endedHow`.

links.description: The external items it links (`issue:` first, then `links:`), as the card draws them: each source's mark and ref.

liveAttempt.description: An attempt at it is starting or running.

needsYou.description:
It waits for you: its stage is of kind `you`, where only you move it on.
An attempt that failed or was stopped is its starter's business, not
yours. Derived on read, never stored.

outputs.description: The project folder files its work produces (`outputs:`).

partOf.description: The task it is a part of (`part_of`); null when none.

parts.description: Its parts: the tasks `part_of` it, by id.

problem.description: What in the file could not be read, or a stage the project lacks, in a sentence; null when all is well.

queuedStart.description: Its stage's `runs:` hook asked for an attempt, which waits for a slot under the project's max_attempts.

ready.description:
Ready: in a `todo` stage, every wait settled (its own and its `part_of`
ancestors'), no live attempt, and no coordinator holding it. The one
rule dispatch, the board and every tool answer read.

startProblem.description: Why the hub could not start an attempt the last time it tried, while the task is unchanged since.

startedAt.description: When it first moved into a stage of kind active, ms epoch; null while it never has.

todos.description: Its agreed to-dos ticked, of all agreed (core `todoProgress`): offered ones are left out.

unblocks.description: The tasks that wait on it (`waits_on`), by id.

updatedAt.description: When its file last changed, ms epoch: its last commit, or an edit no commit has yet.

updatedBy.description: Who made its last commit; null while its file holds an edit no commit has.

waits.description: Every wait it has, its own and its `part_of` chain's, unsettled first.

waitsOn.description: What it waits on (`waits_on`), as its file keeps it.

TaskTodo.description: One to-do of a task file (`## To-dos`), as a task read parses it.

id.description: Its marker, `td-3`; null on a to-do written without one.

path.description: Its position: `2` the second top-level to-do, `2.1` that one's first child.

promoted.description: The task it was promoted to (`tsk-152`), when its line ends in `→ #152`.

proposed.description: Offered by an attempt whose plan left it open (`(proposed)` before its words), not agreed yet.

text.description: The words after the box and marker, without the promoted link.

TaskView.description: One task, its file read whole, and what its attempts and edges say.

accounts.description: The accounts its attempts may run on; empty: every account.

archivedAt.description: When its file moved into tasks/archive/, ms epoch; null while it is not archived.

budget.description: What an attempt may spend before the hub stops it; null: the project's default.

builtOn.description: A done task's cards and pins that moved since its attempt was dispatched on them.

closeReason.description: The reason given with the move into the done or dropped stage it is in; null when none or open.

comments.description: Its `## Comments`, oldest first: each written by the hub with who and when.

completedAt.description: When it moved into the done stage it is in, ms epoch; null while it is not in one.

context.description: Project folder files its attempt's brief carries (`context:`), the conversation's pick.

createdAt.description: When the commit that first added its file landed, ms epoch.

createdBy.description: Who made the commit that first added its file; null while no commit has it.

droppedAt.description: When it moved into the dropped stage it is in, ms epoch; null while it is not in one.

duplicateOf.description: The task it repeats (`duplicate_of`); null when none.

extra.description: The fields its file carries that a task file does not know, with their values (a scalar or a list); kept as written.

foundInNamed.description: Where it was found, as its link names it: a task's title, what a pin stands on; null when it was found nowhere.

group.description: Its attempts' group: their parent hears one combined report once all have ended.

hash.description: sha256 hex of the file as read.

heldBy.description: The ancestor whose live attempt coordinates it, holding it from the hub's dispatch; null when none.

kind.description: The kind of its stage; null when its stage is not one of the project's.

lands.description: Where an attempt's work lands, as the file says; null: the project's default.

lastAttemptFailed.description:
Its newest attempt failed, and it is not done or dropped since. The
failure is its starter's business (the session that started it, or the
project's conversation for the dispatcher's), who hears the report: never the person's
Needs you. It keeps the task off the dispatcher's frontier until someone
starts or retries it.

lastAttemptStopped.description:
Its newest attempt was cancelled (stopped), and it is not done or dropped
since: no failure, and off the frontier as a failed one is. Who stopped
it is its attempt's `endedHow`.

links.description:
The external items it links (core external-items.ts): its record
(`issue:`, the tracker sync's) first, then its `links:`, each as the
source last said it.

liveAttempt.description: An attempt at it is starting or running.

needsYou.description: It waits for you: its stage is of kind `you` (see {@link TaskSummary.needsYou}).

owns.description: Globs of the repository's files an attempt owns.

parts.description: Its parts: the tasks `part_of` it, by id.

queuedStart.description: Its stage's `runs:` hook asked for an attempt, which waits for a slot under the project's max_attempts.

ready.description:
Ready: in a `todo` stage, every wait settled (its own and its `part_of`
ancestors'), no live attempt, and no coordinator holding it. The one
rule dispatch, the board and every tool answer read.

result.description: What its newest finished attempt handed back; null until one has.

runsOn.description: Where its attempts run (runs-on.ts), as the file says; null: the project's.

sections.description: The body's other `## ` sections, as written.

sendBack.description: Where Send back puts it and who takes it up there; null when it does not wait on you, or no stage before its own is open to you.

startProblem.description: Why the hub could not start an attempt the last time it tried, while the task is unchanged since.

startedAt.description: When it first moved into a stage of kind active, ms epoch; null while it never has.

unblocks.description: The tasks that wait on it (`waits_on`), by id.

updatedAt.description: When its file last changed, ms epoch: its last commit, or an edit no commit has yet.

updatedBy.description: Who made its last commit; null while its file holds an edit no commit has.

waits.description: Every wait it has, its own and its `part_of` chain's, unsettled first.

TaskWait.description: One wait of a task, its own or inherited, as task-waits.ts settles it.

dropped.description: A task target dropped since (not as a duplicate): the wait is removed.

flag.description: Why it is blocked for good until someone removes or re-points it (`closed unmerged`); null when it is not.

href.description: Where it opens: its `cawco:` reference, or the pull request's or run's page.

label.description: What it is called: a task's title, a card's question, what a pin stands on, `PR #418`.

state.description: Where it stands, in a word or two: `doing`, `open`, `picked`, `merged`, `red`.

target.description: The wait as its file keeps it ({@link waitHandle}).

value.description: What it settled with, for a card (its pick) or a pin; null otherwise or while unsettled.

via.description: The `part_of` ancestor it is inherited from; null for the task's own.

kind.description:
Hub-originated: a project's tasks changed (one was created or moved, or
its folder was written), by anyone: read them again.

taskId.description:
The one task that changed, when the change named one (a move, a write,
a comment); absent, any of them (its folder was written). An open task
reads itself again on either: its times are whole seconds, so two
changes in one second (a tracker's sync beside you) show no newer time.

TextAttachment.description:
What a turn carries beside its typed words, other than pictures: a text
the reader attached or pasted at length, folded into the prompt as quoted
material; or any other file, which the hub stores (`POST /api/files`) and
the session's machine fetches and puts on its own disk before the harness
sees the turn, naming its path in one line of the message.

asks.description:
An agent's reply that needs the person's answer or pick
(`comment_reply`'s `asks`): its pin waits on them in Needs you until
they reply or resolve it ({@link pinAsks}). Never on a person's entry.

attachments.description: What a person's entry carries, in the order attached.

files.description: Files an agent's reply names as changed.

held.description: The person held it to send with the others ({@link sendHeld}): no delivery carries it until then. A person's unsent entry only.

sentAt.description: When it was delivered to the session; a person's entry only.

text.description: Its words; empty only when it carries attachments (they alone may be the comment).

ToolBehind.description:
One tool some machines are behind on: the version CawCo runs, and each
such machine with where it stands, so Needs you draws one entry per tool
with a line per machine, or one per machine and tool, from the same data.

wants.description: What CawCo runs, as the first machine listed says it (its build's catalog).

ToolBehindMachine.description: One machine whose copy of a tool CawCo does not run, or is updating.

needsYou.description:
The copy waits on the person (`failed`, `own`, `asked`): Needs you
lists it, with Update. The rest CawCo is updating, or will once the
machine is connected (`due`).

online.description: Its agent is connected: an Update can be sent to it now.

ToolGlance.description: The tool a session is running right now — the fleet view's glance line.

ToolInstallMethod.description:
One way to put a tool on a machine. A copy already there goes on again
with the method that holds it (its `footprint`, or what `holds` asks);
any other install takes, in catalog order, the first method whose
`platforms` match and whose `needs` runs here ({@link needProbe}), among the methods that
hold nothing when the tool has any (a package manager's method is for the
copy it holds), else among all. A pinned install takes only a method with
a `pinnedCommand`. There is no fallback past a method that ran and failed
— a half-applied installer chain is harder to reason about than one
honest failure.

command.description: The install command, run through the Bun shell.

footprint.description:
How a binary this method put on a machine is told apart, from where it
resolves. A tool already present is installed again only with the method
whose footprint it bears, never a first-eligible one beside it: two
package managers each holding a copy is two copies on the PATH, and the
one that wins is not the one just installed.

holds.description:
For a package manager whose copies can't be told apart by where they
resolve (apk puts its files where other managers put theirs): the
question that asks it whether it holds a copy, `<needs> <holds…>
<file>`, which exits 0 and names the package when it does. A copy it
holds is held to this method, as one bearing its footprint is.

label.description: Names the method in status and errors: 'curl script', 'npm', 'winget'.

native.description:
Set on no method. Declared only because installable TestFlight builds'
schema has it (hub `openapi:check`); it goes in the change a TestFlight
build is made from, with `ToolSpec.dependencyOnly` and `requires`.

needs.description:
A binary that must already run on the machine for this method to be
eligible — 'npm', 'brew', 'winget': on the PATH, and its
{@link needProbe} neither failing to start nor exiting other than 0 (one
still running at the agent's bound runs). Absent means always eligible. CawCo
never installs it: a machine where it is missing or does not run takes
the next method, or is told what is missing and what it said.

pinnedCommand.description:
The command when the policy pins a version — `{version}` becomes the pin.
Kept apart from `command` because "latest" is not a version most
installers accept: the curl scripts and winget want no version argument
at all when they should take the newest. A method without one never runs
for a pin: the install says it can't put that version on, rather than
putting another on.

ToolPlatform.description: The platforms a daemon reports itself as — `platform()` from `node:os`.

ToolPolicy.description: The hub's per-tool policy row: what the fleet is supposed to have.

pinnedVersion.description: Exact version to install; null rides `{version}` as `latest`.

required.description: Required tools install automatically wherever a register finds them missing.

ToolRequirement.description: The shape of {@link ToolSpec.requires}, which no tool sets.

ToolSignin.description:
Whether a tool on a machine is signed in, as its own {@link * ToolSigninSpec.status} read said when it was last read (`at`, ms epoch):
`unknown` when that read said neither, with its words in `detail`.

ToolSigninChallenge.description: A tool's sign-in begun on a machine: the link the person opens, and until when it is kept (ms epoch).

ToolSigninSpec.description:
A tool's own sign-in, run as the tool itself on the machine (agent
tool-signin.ts): CawCo reads what it prints and types what the person
pasted into it, and never sees or keeps the login it stores.

login.description: Arguments after the binary for the tool's own interactive sign-in: it prints a link, takes the code pasted on its input, and ends once signed in.

loginHosts.description: The hosts its sign-in link may be on; no other link on its screen is read.

signedOut.description: Words, any case, in what {@link status} prints when it is not signed in.

status.description: Arguments after the binary for a read that spends nothing and exits 0 only when signed in.

bin.description: The executable whose presence means installed.

dependencyOnly.description: Set on no tool; declared for installable apps only, as {@link ToolInstallMethod.native} is.

exactVersion.description:
The one version this fleet runs, for a tool CawCo's own code is built
against: every install puts exactly this one on the machine, whatever the
policy pins, and a probe that finds another reports it failed.

formerVersions.description:
The versions earlier CawCo builds ran as {@link exactVersion}, oldest
first: a copy at one of them, held by one of the catalog's methods, is
taken for one CawCo put there when no record of the daemon's names it
({@link ToolCopy}), as every copy CawCo installed before its daemon
kept that record is. Each move of `exactVersion` adds the one it leaves.

install.description: Ordered by preference. Empty for a platform = unsupported there.

minVersion.description:
The oldest version CawCo runs, for a tool CawCo updates with the tool's
own updater (`claude update`, `pi update`): a copy older than it is
reported `failed` with why, and an install brings it to this version or
newer.

name.description: What the dashboard calls it.

release.description:
Where the tool's newest release is said, for a tool CawCo keeps at its
newest release on every machine that has it (hub tool-releases.ts): a
URL whose body's first `x.y.z` is that release. The hub reads it and
sends each machine whose copy is older an install, which runs the
copy's own updater ({@link ToolSpec.install}'s first method), so no
press is needed; an update that leaves the copy older says why on its
row.

requires.description: Set on no tool; declared for installable apps only, as {@link ToolInstallMethod.native} is.

signin.description:
For a tool that signs in to its own service with the machine's person's
own login, which CawCo never holds: how a machine reads whether it is
signed in, and runs its own sign-in.

updatesOff.description:
How a machine turns this tool's own updates off, for a tool CawCo keeps
current ({@link release}): the switches its owner set are CawCo's too.

versionCommand.description: Probe for the version; the first `x.y.z` in its output is the answer.

wellKnownPaths.description:
Where installers put the binary when it lands off the daemon's PATH —
probed with `~` expanded, after `which` misses. An installer that edits
shell rc files fixes the *user's* PATH, never a daemon that is already
running.

ToolState.description: What a probe or an install attempt found. The unit every surface renders.

at.description: When this was learnt, ms epoch.

copy.description:
Whose the copy on the machine is ({@link ToolCopy}), on every status of
a tool that is there, from a daemon that judges it (this field's build
on): absent from an older daemon, and where no copy is.

detail.description:
`failed`: the tail of the installer's stderr. `unsupported`: what is
missing, named exactly — 'needs npm (Node 20+)' beats a grey chip.
`installed`: set only on a tool CawCo keeps at its newest release
({@link ToolSpec.release}), when the last update it ran here left the
copy older than the release it was after: why, in the updater's words.
The copy still runs; the update is owed until a newer release, a Retry,
or the copy moving some other way.

method.description: The {@link ToolInstallMethod.label} that installed it or failed trying.

signin.description: For a tool with its own sign-in ({@link ToolSpec.signin}), installed here: whether it is signed in.

to.description: On `installing`: the version being put on, when the one asking knows it.

triedAt.description:
When an install attempt ran that left the copy where `detail` says, in
the installer's words: set on what an install answered short of a copy
CawCo runs, and on every report of the copy after it while it stays
where the attempt left it (agent tools.ts `failures`, per boot). The hub
sends no update unasked while it stands.

version.description:
The version the copy here says: on `installed`; on `failed`, a copy
CawCo does not run (older than its floor, or not its one version), or
the copy an attempt that failed left there; on `installing`, the copy
being updated. An attempt that failed with no copy there carries none.

wants.description:
Set while the copy here is one this machine's CawCo does not run: the
version it runs (its build's catalog, which may not be the hub's while a
release rolls out). Absent from an older daemon.

ToolUpdateSwitches.description:
How a machine turns a tool's own updates off, as the tool itself decides
it: a variable whose value is on ({@link switchOn}; any value at all for
one of `anyValue`) in the `env` of the tool's settings, else in the
environment the tool runs with, which its settings' `env` stands over.
The settings are what the tool's own merge engine resolves (`engine`):
the user's and every managed source, ranked as the tool ranks them.
`automatic` turns off the tool's own automatic updates, and so CawCo's;
`every` turns off every update, a press's included.

anyValue.description: Of the variables, those on whatever they are set to, rather than by {@link switchOn}.

engine.description:
Whose engine resolves the tool's settings: `claude-code`, Claude Code's
own, as the Agent SDK's `resolveSettings` runs it (agent tools.ts
`SETTINGS_ENGINES`).

places.description:
Where the tool's managed settings are kept, as a row names the place a
switch is set: its managed settings files (the system directory each
platform keeps them in, and the file and the folder of `.json` files
there), its macOS managed preferences domain, and the registry value its
settings are kept in, under each key.

ToolUpdates.description:
What the fleet does when a machine's copy of a tool CawCo manages is at a
version CawCo does not run, one choice for the whole fleet (the owner,
2026-11-14, default "Update it"). `update`: the hub sends that machine the
install its Update button sends, once, for a copy CawCo put there (hub
tool-installs.ts `keepRunnable`); `ask`: nothing installs, and the
machine's copy stands behind until a person presses Update. A person's own
copy ({@link ToolCopy}) is never updated unasked under either.

ToolUpdatesState.description:
`/api/tool-updates`: the fleet's choice, and every tool some machine is
behind on with each such machine ({@link toolsBehind}), as the hub holds
them when asked. After that, each machine's cell moves on the `instances`
frame, and {@link toolsBehind} over the machines says the same.

ToolWants.description: The version a machine's CawCo runs of a tool: `version` exactly, or `version` or newer (`orNewer`).

Tracker.description: Where a project's tasks live: CawCo's files alone, or an outside tracker beside them (tracker.ts).

TrackerBindingView.description: A project's binding: one connection and one target on it.

boundAt.description: When the project was bound, ms epoch: issues opened after it become tasks.

githubProject.description: GitHub: the Project its stages show on through Status; null when none is set.

githubProjectReason.description:
GitHub: why stages do not show on a Project, in GitHub's words (the
connection may not read or write the owner's Projects); null when
nothing stops them. Issues sync either way.

linked.description: Issues linked to the project's tasks.

polledAt.description: When its last poll answered, ms epoch; null before its first.

reason.description: Why it is `refused`, or why its last poll stopped short, in the tracker's words; null when all went through.

targetName.description: What a person reads: `owner/repo`, or the team's key and name (`ENG · Engineering`).

TrackerSyncState.description:
Where a project's sync stands: `syncing` until its first poll answers,
`synced` while the tracker answers, `refused` when the tracker refused the
connection's sign-in or scope, whose words are its `reason`.

TrackerTarget.description: A target a connection reaches, offered when a project is bound: a repository, or a team.

id.description: GitHub: `owner/repo`; Linear: the team's id.

name.description: `owner/repo`, or `ENG · Engineering`.

TrackerView.description: A project's tracker, as the dashboard reads it.

binding.description: Set while the tracker is GitHub Issues or Linear.

TranscriptBlock.description: One row of a transcript, as the hub built it.

id.description:
Stable for the life of the transcript, on every screen and after every
reload: the harness's uuid for the frame it came from (one assistant frame
is several blocks, `<uuid>:<index>`), a send's uuid, `task:<id>` for a
task line — and a hash of the frame for the few that carry no uuid.

metadata.description: Everything a renderer may need beyond `content`, keyed by the kind that uses it.

parentToolUseId.description: The Task call whose subagent said this. Absent on the main transcript.

queued.description: A send not read yet ({@link TranscriptPage.queued}).

sdkUuid.description: The harness's own uuid for the frame — the handle for rewind and fork.

state.description: A send's row: where its record stands.

timestamp.description:
When the turn happened, ISO-8601. A send: when the hub accepted it.
Anything else: when the harness stored its record. Absent when the
harness gives none — an invented clock would date a row by when it was read.

TranscriptBranch.description:
A subagent's branch: the Task call it hangs under, and how far it has got.
Its blocks are the blocks whose `parentToolUseId` is {@link toolUseId}.

lastEventAt.description: When the last branch event arrived, ISO-8601, for recency sorting.

model.description: Model that answered (wire id from assistant frames), or the requested alias until the first frame arrives.

taskId.description: The task the `task_*` progress messages report under.

toolUseId.description: The Task tool.use id that spawned this subagent.

TranscriptEvent.description:
One change to a transcript, in the order the hub made it. Applied in
sequence to the page a client fetched, it gives exactly the blocks the hub
holds.

commands.description: The `/` menu: names as the session lists them, which are skills, and their details once pushed.

harness.description: The harness the frames came from.

initialized.description: The transcript has turns in it: the session has already started.

inits.description: How many `init`s this transcript has seen since the hub built it.

lastCompaction.description: What the last compaction did, from the frames that reported it.

lastTurnFailed.description: The last turn came back an error — the SDK's `is_error`.

model.description: Which model answers the next turn, by the newest `init` or fallback.

permissionMode.description: How the session answers tool permissions, by the newest `init`.

sdkStatus.description: The session's own word on what it is doing: `compacting`, `requesting`, or nothing.

sessionId.description: The harness session key the newest `init` named.

tooling.description: The servers and tools the newest `init` announced.

totalCost.description: The cumulative cost the latest `result` reported, in dollars.

turnsEnded.description: How many turns have ended since the hub built this transcript.

busy.description: A turn is in flight, as the frames show it.

currentTool.description: The main loop's tool in flight, cleared by its result or the turn's end.

openBlock.description: Which content block the main loop has open right now, from the partials.

streaming.description: Partial assistant text of the main loop, between partials and the final message.

streams.description: Partial assistant text, per subagent branch, by its Task call id.

thinkingClosing.description: The SDK signed the thinking block: it is wrapping up, not still going.

thinkingSince.description: When the open thinking block started, epoch ms, by the hub's clock.

thinkingStream.description: What the open thinking block has reasoned so far.

TranscriptFacts.description: What the session has said about itself, kept beside its blocks.

commands.description: The `/` menu: names as the session lists them, which are skills, and their details once pushed.

harness.description: The harness the frames came from.

initialized.description: The transcript has turns in it: the session has already started.

inits.description: How many `init`s this transcript has seen since the hub built it.

lastCompaction.description: What the last compaction did, from the frames that reported it.

lastTurnFailed.description: The last turn came back an error — the SDK's `is_error`.

model.description: Which model answers the next turn, by the newest `init` or fallback.

permissionMode.description: How the session answers tool permissions, by the newest `init`.

sdkStatus.description: The session's own word on what it is doing: `compacting`, `requesting`, or nothing.

sessionId.description: The harness session key the newest `init` named.

tooling.description: The servers and tools the newest `init` announced.

totalCost.description: The cumulative cost the latest `result` reported, in dollars.

turnsEnded.description: How many turns have ended since the hub built this transcript.

TranscriptPage.description:
One page of a session's transcript, newest first. The newest page carries
the live state too, and the stream position it is consistent with: a client
subscribes with `afterSeq: seq` and applies the events after it.

blocks.description: The main transcript's blocks on this page, oldest first.

branches.description: The branches whose Task call is on this page, each with its blocks.

continuedTo.description:
Newest page only: the session a continuation took this one's work item
on in (`InstanceRow.continuedInto`, followed to the last), by its id and
title: its page says where the work went in its composer's place, from
its first paint and for a reader whose board no longer lists either row.

cursor.description: Pass as `before` for the page older than this; null at the conversation's start.

facts.description: Newest page only: what the session has said about itself.

hubRun.description:
Newest page only: the hub run that numbered `seq`, one value per hub
start (frames.ts `InstancesFrame.hubRun`). The hub numbers each stream from 1
again when it restarts, so a `seq` resumes a stream only on a socket
whose board names the same run.

queued.description: Newest page only: the sends waiting to be read.

removed.description:
Newest page only: the blocks this transcript took out on purpose since
the hub built it (a rewind's cut, one of the hub's lines taken back), by
id. A row a client holds stays where it is until its `block.remove`
reaches it or this lists it: a read that lacks a row is no word that it
went.

seq.description: Newest page only: the stream position this page is consistent with.

tail.description: Newest page only: the live tail.

TranscriptPageBranch.description: A subagent branch with its own blocks, as a page carries it.

TranscriptStreamFrame.description: A transcript event batch, as it rides a session's Ledger stream.

TranscriptTail.description:
The live tail: what the turn is doing between frames. The one part of a
transcript that moves token by token.

busy.description: A turn is in flight, as the frames show it.

currentTool.description: The main loop's tool in flight, cleared by its result or the turn's end.

openBlock.description: Which content block the main loop has open right now, from the partials.

streaming.description: Partial assistant text of the main loop, between partials and the final message.

streams.description: Partial assistant text, per subagent branch, by its Task call id.

thinkingClosing.description: The SDK signed the thinking block: it is wrapping up, not still going.

thinkingSince.description: When the open thinking block started, epoch ms, by the hub's clock.

thinkingStream.description: What the open thinking block has reasoned so far.

TranscriptWhere.description: Where a transcript was found: the machine, folder, key and harness.

TurnWakes.description:
The work a session started that will wake it later, counted as a turn
ends: `background`, its own work still running in the background (a shell
command or a monitor, a subagent moved to the background), whose end
starts a turn of its own; `scheduled`, the wake-ups it set itself (Claude
Code's ScheduleWakeup, CronCreate and `/loop`). Every harness says both:
pi and OpenCode schedule nothing, so theirs is 0.

TypeFileProblem.description: A file under `delegates/` that did not make a type, or a field one ignored.

source.description: The folder it is in: the project's, or its area's.

Undoable.description: What a config delete answers: core's {@link Deleted}, the entry the dashboard's Undo names.

ok.description: Always true: what every delete has answered since before the trash.

UpdateReport.description:
What an {@link UPDATE_CAWCO} run did. Every field is what actually
happened, not what was asked for.

changed.description:
The services whose code the update changed: the only ones it rebuilt or
restarted, and the only way a deploy leaves the agent owing a restart.
Every service when nothing was pulled (an update asked of a current
checkout restarts the stack) and for a registry install.

pulled.description: The tail of what git said — 'Already up to date.' included.

skipped.description: Why something asked for did not happen.

claude.description: Hub-originated: every Claude account's own limits, every machine's Go plan, and the fleet's spend.

UsageLimitsResponse.description:
What `/api/usage/limits` returns: each Claude account's own limits, and
each machine's OpenCode Go plan. Claude's limits are an account's, never a
machine's: a machine signed in to several accounts has no one reading.

UsageRowMachine.description: The machine a summary row ran on: named, never shown by id.

UsageSpend.description:
The fleet's real spend, as the hub reckons it and serves it at
`/api/usage/spend` and on every `kind: 'usage'` frame: the one figure every
"today" in CawCo reads.

Real money is opencode's messages, each priced by CawCo at its provider's
rates and its prompt's tier (`costForUsage`); Claude is a subscription
whose constraint is a percentage, so its API-price estimate is never added
in. The days are the hub's: `todayStart` is local midnight and `weekStart`
