this Monday's midnight in `timeZone`, the hub's own zone (IANA name).

UsageSummary.description: What `/api/usage/summary` returns: the groups, their totals, and unpriced models.

UsageSummaryRow.description:
One aggregated group in a usage summary. `key` is the group's identity (a
session id, a machine id, an hour's epoch ms); `label` is what a reader is
shown. Session rows carry their machine and the instance that ran them (null
for a session run outside CawCo); machine rows carry the machine.

UsageTotals.description: The whole-window sums a summary's groups roll up to.

UserAnswers.description: The reader's choices, back the way the tool reads them.

UserQuestion.description: One question of an `AskUserQuestion`-shaped prompt, as every harness can express.

UserQuestionAnswered.description:
A question the reader answered: the questions asked and the choices made,
keyed by question text.

`answers` values are `string | string[]` by wire truth: the Claude SDK types
them `string` ("multi-select answers are comma-separated") but a real
transcript carries an array for a multi-select answer, and freeform "Other"
text lands inside `answers` too — so a value is not guaranteed to match any
option `label`. The union is the truth; nothing coerces it.

annotations.description: Per-question notes (preview selections), keyed by question text.

response.description: Freeform text the reader typed instead of selecting a structured option.

UserQuestionDismissed.description:
A question the reader walked away from. Every harness expresses this as a
denial of the question's permission, and it carries no answers at all — so
it is a separate member rather than an answered result with an empty map,
which would let a consumer draw a card with blank choices and call it an
answer.

ValidationErrorResponse.description: Request validation problem. Diagnostic fields are development-only.

Verb.description: The whole agent↔hub↔dashboard protocol. Adding a verb is a design decision.

ViewEvent.description: One inbound event from outside (GitHub, a polled connection).

handledAt.description: When a routine took it, or null while none has.

kind.description: What kind of event it is (`issues.opened`, `pull_request.closed`, a connector's kind).

routedTo.description: The routine a route sent it to, by name; null when no route took it.

source.description: Where it came from (`github`, a connection's name).

ViewRemoval.description:
What removing a kept view does, in the hub's words, before it is done
(`GET /api/projects/:id/views/:name/removal`): the person's confirm on
the block or the tab says this.

ask.description: The question the confirm asks: what goes, and the block it leaves.

file.description: The view's file, deleted as a commit.

page.description: The page it stands on as a block, or null: it is its own tab.

ViewRemoved.description: A kept view removed (`DELETE /api/projects/:id/views/:name`): what went.

commit.description: The commit that deleted its file.

page.description: The page whose block it was, or null: it was its own tab.

said.description: What went, in the hub's words.

ViewRoutine.description: One routine of the project, with its newest runs.

nextRuns.description: Its runs ahead, as the hub's scheduler will start them: the next week's, at most 288, epoch ms.

target.description: A fresh delegate each run, a message to Caw, or the project's memory curator.

outcome.description: How it ended: `delivered`, `silent`, `failed`; null while it runs or when it was skipped.

reason.description: Why it was skipped or queued, or how it failed.

slot.description: `test`, `by-hand`, `event`, `inbox`, or the time of its scheduled slot in the routine's zone ("09:00").

byRoutine.description: Each routine of the project: what its runs in the window spent, and how many there were.

byType.description: Each delegate type the project's delegated work ran on in the window (null: none named), and its items.

byKind.description: Tasks in a stage of each kind.

stages.description: The project's stages, in the order its stages file names them.

ViewTaskRow.description: One task as the `tasks` tool answers it: the board's row, and its dates.

WaitReason.description:
Why a session at its account's limit waits rather than moving: it is a
fork (it reads its origin's cache, on its origin's account), moving is
switched off, no account can take it now (`full`), its own account resets
within the wait the policy allows (`soon`), or its prompt cache lasts past
that reset, so waiting costs nothing where a move re-reads it cold
(`free`). `room` and `work` are history only: lines a hub stored when
admission kept a share of each account's room from moves, and while a
delegate's work could be set to carry on after its own account's reset;
never written now, still read.

WaitWitness.description: One card or pin an attempt was dispatched on, and the value it settled with (`workItems.waitedOn`).

target.description: The wait as its task's file keeps it (wait-targets.ts).

days.description:
How far back it looks, days: nothing recorded which revision of an
artifact you had on screen before the hub kept it, so older things can't
be told apart from ones you looked at.

missing.description: What could not be read, one sentence each (a project whose tasks did not read): the list may be short by it.

artifactKind.description: For an artifact or decision: which kind of artifact.

conversation.description: The conversation it came from, when one made it.

id.description: The object's id: an artifact's, a work item's, `project:tsk-142`.

revision.description: For an artifact or decision: the revision it waits at.

since.description: When it began waiting, ms epoch: made, revised, reported, moved to its stage.

why.description: Why it waits, in a few words: an artifact's Needs-you line ("3 of 9 picked · 2 unsent") or its notice's, "unread", the stage.

WaitingKind.description: What waits on the person's eyes (`GET /api/find/waiting`).

WaitingMachine.description: A machine that dialled the hub without a key's proof and waits for the person.

WindowForecast.description:
One window of an account, and where it is heading: `pace` is percent per
hour from the account's successive readings in this window, null when no
session runs on it (nothing CawCo can see is spending it); `runsOutAt` is
when it reaches 100% at that pace, only when that lands before its reset.
A window past its reset with no newer reading is a fresh one: 0%, no pace.

group.description: How long it runs (core `LimitWindow.group`): `session`, `weekly`, `monthly`, or another.

WindowRef.description: Names one of an account's windows.

WorkBudget.description:
What a work item may spend before the hub stops it: dollars (the usage its
machine reports for its session), turns its session ends, and minutes of
wall time since it started. Each is optional; one reached fails the item.

kind.description: Hub-originated: a delegate work item's state; `instanceId` is its parent's.

WorkItemState.description: A work item's life. Only `starting` and `running` take messages.

WorkItemSummary.description:
One delegate's work item as its parent's delegate tray reads it: the hub's
`work_items` row cut to what a chip and its panel say, pushed as a
`work_item` frame on every change and read back over
`GET /api/work-items?parent=`. Times are epoch ms. A `delegate` call that
waits for files a live item owns is one too, `starting` with `queued` set,
under the ids its item takes when it starts.

checkQueue.description:
While its landing waits between `finish_item` and its outcome (the
merge checks' shared machine slot, a machine's pause, its turn to land):
"queued for the Mac's build slot behind …", and since when (epoch ms);
null otherwise. Named for the checks it once was: shipped iOS builds
decode it under this key.

dismissReason.description: Why the reader dismissed it, in their words; null unless dismissed with a reason.

firstLines.description:
The glance of each: what it was asked, what it reported (its
`finish_item` headline whole, else its report's first line), why it
failed (first lines).

machinePaused.description:
While the machine its workspace is on is paused: "Omars-MacBook-Pro is
paused until 00:57". Its session runs no turn until then. Null otherwise.

queued.description:
While it waits to start: the files it owns, which a live item owns too
(`src/theme/**`), and the pause of the machine it starts on ("obelisk is
paused until 00:57"), when that is what it waits for; null once it has
started.

replacedBy.description: The later item of the same tray the reader said took over its work; null otherwise.

stalled.description:
While its account's limit (or a refused sign-in) has stopped its
session: "Stopped at A's limit; continues on B", "…; continues at
15:40" (core `accountsWords.stalled`). It runs no turn until then; null
otherwise.

waitUntil.description: A declared wait's deadline in epoch ms.

WorkspaceCut.description:
Where a workspace cut again is cut ({@link CONTROL_WORKSPACE_CREATE}'s
`at`): the commit its clone's HEAD was on when it retired, on `origin`'s
branch `branch` that held it then (its base when the base held it), read
by its machine's archive ({@link WorkspaceArchived} `head`) and fetched as
the clone is. Never the base's tip: a landing stopped while queued leaves
commits no landing recorded, and a cut at the tip left them behind
(2026-10-17).

`carry`, for a workspace whose commits went to a carry as it retired (an
item that lands none, hub workspaces.ts `settle`): that carry's folder on
its machine. `commit` is then where its HEAD built on `branch`, and the
carry's commits are fetched from its bundle on top: the clone is cut again
at the HEAD it had.

WorkspaceFrom.description:
Where a workspace cut `from` another started ({@link workspaces.cutFrom}):
that workspace, and its HEAD then, which this one's clone took.

commit.description: The source's HEAD as this clone took it.

landed.description:
Whether this workspace's landing put every patch of that commit's work
on the base branch (landing-run.ts `vouchLanded`): then the source holds
none of it as its own, and an archive is told so (core
`WorkspaceArchive.landed`).

WorkspaceHolding.description:
What a workspace holds that is nowhere else, read with git on its machine's
host once its boundary is closed (agent workspace.ts `closeClone`): commits
on HEAD or any local branch that no remote-tracking ref of `origin` has
(`git rev-list --count HEAD --branches --not --remotes=origin`: landed work
was pushed, whether onto the base or to a branch of its own, and a cut
again fetches it from `origin`), entries of `git status
--porcelain` (untracked files included; the paths `skip` names, the outputs
its items handed over, left out), stash entries, and the files kept out of
git only by the clone's own excludes (`excluded`). Files a committed
`.gitignore` covers (dependencies, builds, caches) are none of it: they go
with the clone. `bytes` is the clone's size on disk.

excluded.description:
The untracked paths git ignores through no `.gitignore` the repository
tracks: by a line of the clone's `.git/info/exclude`, or a `.gitignore`
that is itself untracked, each as `git status --ignored=matching` names
it, relative to the clone (a folder ends in `/`). The paths `skip`
names, and what CawCo writes into a clone and lists there itself (its
deny paths' stand-ins, the placed skills and memory, its stage), are not
among them. On 2026-10-17 a delegate kept a design page's source out of
its landing this way, and retirement deleted it. Absent when none.

refused.description:
Set when CawCo does not run git in the clone, so nothing of it was read
and `ahead`, `dirty` and `stashes` are 0: why, as agent workspace.ts
`gitRefusal` says it (its `.git` no folder of its own, or a key its own
config sets past core safe-git.ts's allowlist). Only the person, or a
session continuing it, can change that, so the workspace is held until
one does, not tried again each sweep: on 2026-10-25 a clone whose config
held git-lfs's `lfs.<url>.access` was archived and refused every minute.

strays.description:
Set when the clone's folder is there and its `.git` is no repository
git can read: how many entries down its tree are not CawCo's (agent
stand-ins.ts `straysIn`, which names each by its path relative to the
folder). CawCo's are a deny path's stand-in exactly as made, a mount
point a sandbox left on a deny path, a `.git/config` holding only
git-lfs's `[lfs] repositoryformatversion = 0` marker, a project skill
exactly as CawCo placed it (agent fleet.ts `placedAsMade`), and a
dir (`.git`, `.claude`) holding only those. None is a husk, a deleted
clone a sandbox refilled, which holds nothing; any keeps the folder.

WorkspaceKind.description:
What a workspace was made from: a repository's root, which lands by git
(rebase onto its base, the merge checks, push), or any other folder, which
lands by its change set ({@link CONTROL_WORKSPACE_APPLY}).

WorkspaceRef.description: A workspace as the machine that holds it is told about it.

WorkspaceState.description:
A workspace's life, which is its work items' (workspaces.ts `settle`):
`active` while an item there is live, or ended a moment ago and the hub
has not settled it, or while something holds it (a session attached, an
artifact showing what it serves); `held` once its item ended with work
that is nowhere else, which the session that started its work ends, told
so, by continuing it or discarding it (workspaces.ts `heldNotice`), or a
workspace cut from it ends by landing that work (`vouchLanded`);
`archived` once its boundary and clone are gone.

WorkspaceTool.description: A tool a delegate's workspace needs, as a machine that lacks it reports it.

command.description: The command it is looked for by.

lookedIn.description: Every folder it was looked for in that is there, each once, in the order searched, `:`-joined as a PATH is.

need.description: What needs it: the walls every workspace runs in, or the git checkout a workspace is.

package.description: The package that ships it, as the install command names it.

anyOf.description:
A route's 422: the exported `ValidationErrorResponse`, spelled out (and
pinned equal in `test/types`) because a consumer's d.ts prints a reference
to it as an `import()`, which a d.ts reader such as `fromTypes` can't
follow. Not exported, so it prints inline. A mapped copy would print
`detail?: string | undefined`

A route's 422: the exported `ValidationErrorResponse`, spelled out (and
pinned equal in `test/types`) because a consumer's d.ts prints a reference
to it as an `import()`, which a d.ts reader such as `fromTypes` can't
follow. Not exported, so it prints inline. A mapped copy would print
`detail?: string | undefined`

at.description: When the hub last stored it, ms epoch.

hash.description: sha256 hex of `content` — what tells a machine's copy apart from the fleet's.

anyOf.description:
A route's 422: the exported `ValidationErrorResponse`, spelled out (and
pinned equal in `test/types`) because a consumer's d.ts prints a reference
to it as an `import()`, which a d.ts reader such as `fromTypes` can't
follow. Not exported, so it prints inline. A mapped copy would print
`detail?: string | undefined`

pinned equal in `test/types`) because a consumer's d.ts prints a reference
to it as an `import()`, which a d.ts reader such as `fromTypes` can't

kept.description: Where the moved credential is kept now, as its owner names it.

provider.description:
Who bills the account: a provider id. `anthropic` is a Claude subscription
or Console organization, for Claude Code alone: Anthropic's terms keep its
OAuth tokens out of every other product. Any other is a provider pi or
OpenCode speaks, by pi-ai's id for it (`openai-codex` for a ChatGPT
subscription, `github-copilot`, `opencode-go`, `zai`…), or OpenCode's own
id for one pi-ai has no provider for (`zai-coding-plan`, a configured
`litellm`) — see {@link ProviderInfo}.

auth.description: `unknown` until a daemon that probes has registered at least once.

build.description: The cawco build this machine's daemon is running (NEW.md §12).

chosenModes.description:
The permission mode the person last started each harness's session in
on this machine, from any device (the hub's `chosen_modes`): the mode the
New session form opens on there. Absent for a harness never started.

custody.description: Last register's sessiond read, distinct from an available empty list.

fleetItems.description:
Each fleet item as the machine's harnesses converge it (core fleet.ts
`FleetConvergeFrame`), by item id. Absent until the machine has said.

fleetSync.description:
What became of the last fleet sync the hub sent it: sent, applied,
failed in the machine's words, or unanswered. Absent until the hub has
sent it one.

harnesses.description: What each installed harness can do, as the daemon reported at register.

home.description: The machine's home folder, absolute, as its daemon reported at register; absent until one that says so has.

hostsHub.description: The hub runs on this machine, as the hub reads it: live, never stored.

lostAt.description:
Since when (epoch ms) the hub has heard nothing from this machine, once
that has lasted `MACHINE_LOST_MS` with sessions on it (hub
machine-contact.ts): Needs you's item. Null while it answers. Live, as
`status` is: never stored.

pauseStopped.description:
What the pause stopped as it began, as said ({@link stoppedWords}):
"stopped 1 running check". Null when it stopped nothing, or is not paused.

pausedUntil.description:
The owner paused the machine until this time (epoch ms): CawCo starts
nothing on it until then, though its agent stays connected. Null when it
is not paused.

reconnectingUntil.description:
Until when (epoch ms, the hub's clock, as `lostAt`) the hub reads this
machine as on its way back after its agent's link went: a read off it
answers so then (`Retry-After`), and offline after. Null while it is
connected or once it is offline. Live, as `status` is: never stored.

tools.description: Last-known tool status by tool id (NEW.md §10).

getApiAgentsByMachineIdCommands200.description:
What {@link CONTROL_SUPPORTED_COMMANDS} answers, on every harness: the
session's `/` menu. A harness with no slash commands (pi) answers an empty
list, never nothing, so the menu reads one shape whoever answered.

name.description: What the rule is called in the list, and in the reply the session reads.

pattern.description: The phrase to watch for, a regular expression, or a yes/no question, as `matchKind` says.

repeat.description:
Fire again on every later match. Off makes the rule fire once per session
and then go quiet.

reply.description: What the session is sent when the rule fires.

wholeWord.description: Phrase mode only: refuse matches that sit inside a longer word.

ackedAt.description: When a turn last ended without matching the rule again, re-arming it.

fireCount.description: Fires in a row, each in a turn that matched again. Stops at {@link RULE_FIRE_CEILING}.

status.description: `pending` means fired, and no turn has since ended without matching it.

totalFires.description: Fires over the session's whole life, which re-arming does not reset.

auth.description: `unknown` until a daemon that probes has registered at least once.

build.description: The cawco build this machine's daemon is running (NEW.md §12).

chosenModes.description:
The permission mode the person last started each harness's session in
on this machine, from any device (the hub's `chosen_modes`): the mode the
New session form opens on there. Absent for a harness never started.

custody.description: Last register's sessiond read, distinct from an available empty list.

fleetItems.description:
Each fleet item as the machine's harnesses converge it (core fleet.ts
`FleetConvergeFrame`), by item id. Absent until the machine has said.

fleetSync.description:
What became of the last fleet sync the hub sent it: sent, applied,
failed in the machine's words, or unanswered. Absent until the hub has
sent it one.

harnesses.description: What each installed harness can do, as the daemon reported at register.

home.description: The machine's home folder, absolute, as its daemon reported at register; absent until one that says so has.

hostsHub.description: The hub runs on this machine, as the hub reads it: live, never stored.

lostAt.description:
Since when (epoch ms) the hub has heard nothing from this machine, once
that has lasted `MACHINE_LOST_MS` with sessions on it (hub
machine-contact.ts): Needs you's item. Null while it answers. Live, as
`status` is: never stored.

pauseStopped.description:
What the pause stopped as it began, as said ({@link stoppedWords}):
"stopped 1 running check". Null when it stopped nothing, or is not paused.

pausedUntil.description:
The owner paused the machine until this time (epoch ms): CawCo starts
nothing on it until then, though its agent stays connected. Null when it
is not paused.

reconnectingUntil.description:
Until when (epoch ms, the hub's clock, as `lostAt`) the hub reads this
machine as on its way back after its agent's link went: a read off it
answers so then (`Retry-After`), and offline after. Null while it is
connected or once it is offline. Live, as `status` is: never stored.

tools.description: Last-known tool status by tool id (NEW.md §10).

accounts.description: The accounts its attempts may run on; empty: every account.

archivedAt.description: When its file moved into tasks/archive/, ms epoch; null while it is not archived.

budget.description: What an attempt may spend before the hub stops it; null: the project's default.

builtOn.description: A done task's cards and pins that moved since its attempt was dispatched on them.

closeReason.description: The reason given with the move into the done or dropped stage it is in; null when none or open.

comments.description: Its `## Comments`, oldest first: each written by the hub with who and when.

completedAt.description: When it moved into the done stage it is in, ms epoch; null while it is not in one.

context.description: Project folder files its attempt's brief carries (`context:`), the conversation's pick.

createdAt.description: When the commit that first added its file landed, ms epoch.

createdBy.description: Who made the commit that first added its file; null while no commit has it.

droppedAt.description: When it moved into the dropped stage it is in, ms epoch; null while it is not in one.

duplicateOf.description: The task it repeats (`duplicate_of`); null when none.

extra.description: The fields its file carries that a task file does not know, with their values (a scalar or a list); kept as written.

foundInNamed.description: Where it was found, as its link names it: a task's title, what a pin stands on; null when it was found nowhere.

group.description: Its attempts' group: their parent hears one combined report once all have ended.

hash.description: sha256 hex of the file as read.

heldBy.description: The ancestor whose live attempt coordinates it, holding it from the hub's dispatch; null when none.

kind.description: The kind of its stage; null when its stage is not one of the project's.

lands.description: Where an attempt's work lands, as the file says; null: the project's default.

lastAttemptFailed.description:
Its newest attempt failed, and it is not done or dropped since. The
failure is its starter's business (the session that started it, or the
project's conversation for the dispatcher's), who hears the report: never the person's
Needs you. It keeps the task off the dispatcher's frontier until someone
starts or retries it.

lastAttemptStopped.description:
Its newest attempt was cancelled (stopped), and it is not done or dropped
since: no failure, and off the frontier as a failed one is. Who stopped
it is its attempt's `endedHow`.

links.description:
The external items it links (core external-items.ts): its record
(`issue:`, the tracker sync's) first, then its `links:`, each as the
source last said it.

liveAttempt.description: An attempt at it is starting or running.

needsYou.description: It waits for you: its stage is of kind `you` (see {@link TaskSummary.needsYou}).

owns.description: Globs of the repository's files an attempt owns.

parts.description: Its parts: the tasks `part_of` it, by id.

queuedStart.description: Its stage's `runs:` hook asked for an attempt, which waits for a slot under the project's max_attempts.

ready.description:
Ready: in a `todo` stage, every wait settled (its own and its `part_of`
ancestors'), no live attempt, and no coordinator holding it. The one
rule dispatch, the board and every tool answer read.

result.description: What its newest finished attempt handed back; null until one has.

runsOn.description: Where its attempts run (runs-on.ts), as the file says; null: the project's.

sections.description: The body's other `## ` sections, as written.

sendBack.description: Where Send back puts it and who takes it up there; null when it does not wait on you, or no stage before its own is open to you.

startProblem.description: Why the hub could not start an attempt the last time it tried, while the task is unchanged since.

startedAt.description: When it first moved into a stage of kind active, ms epoch; null while it never has.

unblocks.description: The tasks that wait on it (`waits_on`), by id.

updatedAt.description: When its file last changed, ms epoch: its last commit, or an edit no commit has yet.

updatedBy.description: Who made its last commit; null while its file holds an edit no commit has.

waits.description: Every wait it has, its own and its `part_of` chain's, unsettled first.

areaId.description:
The hub `areas` row this is bound to, in place of one project: every
project in that area as the hub reads it (core areas.ts). A machine is
sent it under each such project it holds, as that project's own row
(hub project-placements.ts); a project's own row of the same key wins.
One of `projectId` and `areaId` is required unless `user`, never both.

cwd.description:
The folder this copy is written into: set by the machine as it places a
project's row at one of the project's places there (agent
fleet-place.ts), never by the hub, which sends each row once.

enabled.description:
A disabled hook is simply not written to any machine. Claude Code itself
has no way to disable one hook while keeping it, so this is cawco's
to provide: the row stays, the registration goes.

force.description: Set on a targeted push only: overwrite a machine copy that drifted.

hash.description: sha256 hex of the material a machine compares before writing.

id.description: Client-generated, like a rule's — the editor owns creation.

name.description: What the reader calls it. Unique across the fleet.

placeId.description:
The place this copy is for ({@link placeKeyOf} of its folder), on a
copy the machine placed: its converge keys what the copy came to under
`<key>@<placeId>`, and its report says it per place
({@link FleetSyncReport.placed}).

projectId.description: The hub `projects` row this is bound to. One of it and `areaId` is required unless `user`.

scope.description:
Where a fleet row applies, in Claude Code's own vocabulary:

- `user` — every machine, every project. The default, and what most rows
  want.
- `local`, `project` — one project ({@link FleetPlacement.projectId}),
  or every project in one area ({@link FleetPlacement.areaId}):
  the hub sends the row once to a machine that holds the project
  ({@link MachineFleetConfig.projects}), the machine places a copy at each
  checkout and workspace clone of it there, and each session in that
  folder takes it. An MCP server, a hook, Claude Code
  settings, an OpenCode plugin and a pi extension reach the folder's
  sessions through CawCo's own files and their launch (agent
  fleet-mcp-set.ts, fleet-harness-set.ts), never a file in the checkout.
  A skill is placed in `<cwd>/.claude/skills/` under either scope, kept
  out of the checkout's status.

script.description:
A command hook's script body. CawCo writes it to a file on every machine
and points the registration at that path, so the hook travels — a machine
that has never seen this hook still runs it correctly. Absent means the
handler carries its own `command` and the reader is on their own for
getting that command onto each box.
